72-00-00-980-801-F00Turn the N2 RotorPDF p. 33

2. Turn the N2 Rotor (Figure 201, Figure 202, and Figure 203)

A. General

(1) This task gives the steps on how to turn the N2 rotor with an electronic turning tool (preferred method), or manually with an extension (alternative method), or with a drive motor (alternative method). (2) The high pressure compressor rotor is also referred to as the N2 rotor. (3) For this procedure, the accessory gearbox will be referred to as the Accessory Gear Box (AGB). (4) For this procedure, the handcranking gearbox drive pad will be referred to as the drive pad and the handcranking drive cover will be referred to as the cover.

H. Turn the N2 Rotor

SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-054-F00 (1) If you will turn the N2 rotor with the electronic turning tool, SPL-14866 (preferred method), do these steps: (a) Make sure that the core turning adapter, SPL-14868, is fully clean of foreign objects or dirt before you insert it into the gearbox drive pad. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT USE A TOOL TO PUT THE 3/4-INCH SQUARE DRIVE INTO THE GEAR SHAFT. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AGB BEARING. (b) Install the core turning adapter, SPL-14868, on the gearbox drive pad. NOTE: Attach the core turning adapter, SPL-14868, to the AGB with the same bolts that attached the handcranking drive cover. NOTE: If it is necessary for more access near the N2 drive pad, you can disconnect the connectors to the N2 speed sensor. (c) Attach the offset adapter, SPL-14867, to the core turning adapter, SPL-14868. (d) Use the manufacturer’s assembly instruction to set up the turnover kit for use. 1) Make sure that the motor programming software (9471M90P01) is loaded into the electronic turning tool per the manufacturer’s instructions. (e) Install the electronic turning tool, SPL-14866, to the offset adapter, SPL-14867. (f) Set the motor tool display of the electronic turning tool, SPL-14866, to zero degrees. NOTE: Use the manufacturer supplied instruction to set the motor tool display to zero degrees. CAUTION DO NOT USE THE DRIVE MOTOR AS A BRAKE TO STOP ENGINE MOVEMENT. THE REVERSAL OF THE DRIVE MOTOR WHILE THE ENGINE TURNS CAN BREAK THE TORQUE LIMIT DEVICE OF THE DRIVE. (g) Operate the drive motor in a clockwise direction as seen from forward looking aft. (h) After you complete the task to turn the N2 rotor, remove the electronic turning tool, SPL-14866, as follows: 1) Remove the electronic turning tool, SPL-14866, from the offset adapter, SPL-14867. NOTE: Follow the manufacturer’s instructions to remove the electronic turning tool from the offset adapter and store the tool kit. 2) Remove the offset adapter, SPL-14867, from the core turning adapter, SPL-14868. 3) Remove the core turning adapter, SPL-14868, from the gearbox drive pad. SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-020-F00 (2) If you will turn the N2 rotor manually with a hand tool (alternative method), do these steps: (a) Make sure that the tool is fully clean of foreign objects or dirt before you insert it into the gearbox drive pad. CAUTION DO NOT USE A TOOL TO PUT THE 3/4-INCH SQUARE DRIVE INTO THE GEAR SHAFT. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AGB BEARING. (b) Attach a 3/4-inch square drive tool with a two-foot long extension to the drive pad. NOTE: If it is necessary for more access near the N2 drive pad, you can disconnect the connectors to the N2 speed sensor. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Turn the handle of the tool in the counterclockwise direction as seen from the rear. NOTE: During engine operation, the engine turns in the clockwise direction as seen from the rear. Because of the accessory gearbox gearing, when you turn the tool in the counterclockwise direction as seen from the rear, the engine will turn in the correct clockwise direction. (d) Remove the tools from the drive pad. (e) Remove the 3/4-inch square drive tool and the two-foot long extension. ALL; FOR ALL NON 7BE PRE CFM SB 72-0564 OR PRE SB 72-0879 SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-021-F00 (3) If you will turn the N2 rotor with the drive motor [15] (alternative method), do these steps: (a) Make sure that the tool is fully clean of foreign objects or dirt before you insert into the gearbox drive pad. (b) Install the Drive Motor, SPL-11937, Drive Motor, SPL-2298, or Drive - Motor, SPL-11936, on the gearbox drive pad [13]. NOTE: If it is necessary for more access near the N2 drive pad, you can disconnect the connectors to the N2 speed sensor. 1) Engage the extension [6] with the gearshaft [10]. a) Make sure that the drive motor [15] is horizontal and the ports for the air hoses face outboard. (c) Align the fastener holes in the adapter flange [9] with the gearbox drive pad [13]. (d) Install the adapter flange [9] on the gearbox drive pad [13] with the screw [14], three screws [7], and four washers [8]. (e) Connect the air hoses [11] from the foot or hand control to the quick disconnect ports [5] on the drive motor [15]. (f) Connect the air supply inlet [12] to a compressed 60-105 PSIG dry filtered regulated air source, STD-1057. 1) Adjust the air supply pressure to 90 psi (621 kPa). CAUTION DO NOT USE THE DRIVE MOTOR AS A BRAKE TO STOP ENGINE MOVEMENT. THE REVERSAL OF THE DRIVE MOTOR WHILE THE ENGINE TURNS CAN BREAK THE TORQUE LIMIT DEVICE OF THE DRIVE. (g) Use the manufacturer's instructions to operate the foot or hand control to turn the drive motor in a counterclockwise direction as seen from the rear. NOTE: During engine operation, the engine turns in the clockwise direction as seen from the rear. Because of the accessory gearbox gearing, when you turn the tool in the counterclockwise direction as seen from the rear, the engine will turn in the correct clockwise direction. (h) Do these steps to remove the drive motor [15] from the gearbox drive pad [13] as follows: 1) Disconnect the air supply inlet [12] from the facility air supply. 2) Disconnect the air hoses [11] from the foot or hand control at the quick disconnect ports [5] on the drive motor [15]. 3) Loosen and remove the screw [14], three screws [7] and washers [8]. 4) Remove the drive motor [15] from the gearbox drive pad [13]. G. Find the Index Mark

SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-018-F00 (1) Remove the plug from the S4 borescope port on the stage 3 compressor case: (a) The plug can be found between the 4:00 and 5:00 o'clock position on the case. SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-023-F00 (2) Put the rigid borescope probe with the 90 degree right angle viewer and a 60 degree field of vision into the borescope port. SUBTASK 72-00-00-700-001-F00 (3) Find the zero index mark on the N2 rotor as follows: (a) Turn the N2 rotor so the blades turn in a clockwise direction when seen through the borescope. NOTE: Counterclockwise when seen from the rear. (b) Turn the rotor until you can see the locking lug of the first blade slot. 1) The locking lug is found between the blades. (c) Turn the rotor again until you can see the subsequent (second) locking lug. NOTE: The subsequent blade after the second lug is the blade 1 of the stage 4 compressor. (d) Align the leading edge of the blade 1 with the leading edge of the stage 4 vane (as seen from the rear). NOTE: This is the zero index mark. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-010-F00 (4) Remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the light source to OFF, but keep the blower ON until the lamp and case are cool. SUBTASK 72-00-00-410-016-F00 (5) Do these steps to install the S4 borescope plug: (a) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], to the threads and to the friction surfaces of the plug. (b) Install the plug in the compressor case. 1) Tighten the plug to 57 in-lb (6.4 N·m) - 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m). (c) Put safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006], on the plug. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-025-F00 (6) Remove the tools or the drive motor [15] from the gearbox drive pad [13] (TASK 72-00-00-980-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-00-00-410-043-F00 (7) Install the handcranking drive cover [3] on the gearbox drive pad [13] (TASK 72-00-00-980-801-F00). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL

D. Engine Tubes, Hoses, and Fittings Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-119-F00 CAUTION USE THESE INSTRUCTIONS FOR CFMI SUPPLIED PARTS. DO NOT USE THESE INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUPPLIED PARTS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Examine the engine tube, hose, or fitting. NOTE: The limits in this procedure are general and do not replace the limits on components given in other locations in this manual. If you will examine the fuel manifold, refer to this task: Fuel Manifold - Inspection/Check, TASK 73-11-05-700-801-F00. (a) Tubing for: 1) Splits, cracks, or kinks: a) Not permitted, replace the tube. 2) Dents or flat areas: a) Permitted when the contour is not more than 20 percent of the original tube Outside Diameter (OD). b) If the damage is more than 20 percent, replace the tube. 3) Nicks or scores on drain lines, drain shrouds, and scavenge lines, but does not include the aft sump oil scavenge line: a) Blend the nicks or scores. Refer to Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL b) The maximum permitted depth is not more than 0.010 inch (0.26 mm) after blending. 4) Nicks or scores on all other air and oil lines and aft sump oil scavenge lines: a) Blend the nicks or scores. Refer to Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00. b) The maximum permitted depth is not more than 0.005 inch (0.13 mm) after blending. 5) Nicks or scores on all other fuel lines: a) Blend the nicks or scores. Refer to Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00. b) The maximum permitted depth is not more than 0.010 inch (0.26 mm) after blending. (b) Seating surfaces of the fitting for: 1) Scratches in the circumference areas A and C: a) Remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). b) All amounts up to 0.005 inch (0.13 mm) is permitted after you remove the high metal. 2) Scratches in circumference area B: a) Remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). b) Amounts not found when you use a 0.040 inch (1.02 mm) radius ball scribe. 3) Axial scratches in areas A and C: a) Remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). b) Amounts not more than 0.005 inch (0.13 mm) is permitted after you remove the high metal. 4) Axial scratches in area B: a) Not permitted, replace the tube. 5) Nicks and pits in area C: a) Blend the depressions. Refer to Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00. b) Amounts not more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth is permitted after blending. 6) Nicks and pits in areas A and B: a) Not permitted, replace the tube. 7) Score marks in the circumference of silver plated seating (mating) surfaces: a) Permitted if the score mark does not go through the parent metal. b) If the damage goes through, replace the tube. 8) Deformation in the circumference (spreading) of the tube/ferrule: a) Permitted if the nut is free to turn. b) If the nut does not turn, replace the tube. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 9) Deformation in the circumference (spreading) of the flare nut: a) Permitted if the nut is free to turn. b) If the nut does not turn, replace the tube. 10) Axial deformation (dishing) of the spherical seat fitting surfaces: a) Permitted if the depth does not change and is less than 0.005 inch (0.13 mm) to the initial surface. b) If the damage is more than the limit, replace the tube. (c) Tube and hose fitting nuts for: 1) Damaged corners: a) Permitted only if you can apply the correct torque. b) If you cannot apply the correct torque, replace the tube or hose. 2) Damaged threads: a) Total of one full thread or one continuous thread can be missing after chasing the thread. b) Chase the threads. 3) Lockwire hole torn out: a) Permitted, if one hole is still there. b) If one hole is not there, replace the tube of hose. (d) Swivel flange fittings for: 1) Nicks or scratches on seating surface (surface B): a) Not permitted, replace the tube. 2) Nicks or scratches on mating surfaces (areas A and C): a) Nicks or scratches not more than 0.020 inch (0.51 mm) deep are permitted if you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). 3) Cracks: a) Not permitted, replace the tube. 4) Seating surfaces (surface B) out-of-flat: a) The maximum out-of-flat dimension permitted is 0.006 inch (0.15 mm). b) If the out-of-flat dimension is more than the above limit, replace the tube. 5) Cracks that extend out from the bolt holes: a) The cracks are permitted when not more than two bolt holes are cracked. b) If more than the above limit, replace the tube. 6) Weld joint cracks: a) Not permitted, replace the tube. (e) Tube and hose assemblies for: 1) Leakage: a) Not permitted, replace the tube or hose. (f) Hose assemblies for: 1) Broken hose braid: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Three broken wires per plait and no more than six broken wires per assembly or per 1.0 linear foot (305 mm) of hose is permitted. b) If more than the above limit, replace the hose. 2) Crimps: a) Not permitted, replace the tube or hose. 3) Internal obstructions: a) Not permitted, remove the obstruction or replace the hose. 4) Cuts in the fire sleeve in areas A and B: NOTE: Area A is defined as follows: L = 2.5 x hose OD at the two ends of the hose. Area B is defined as the length between the two areas A. a) Up to 3 cuts that do not cross per hose section are permitted if the length is not more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm). b) If the cuts are more than the limit, replace the hose. 5) Tears in the fire sleeve material in area A: a) Not permitted, replace the hose. 6) Tears in the fire sleeve material in area B: a) One per hose section is permitted if the depth is not more than 0.010 inch (0.25 mm) and the total area is not more than 0.40 square inch (258 square mm). b) Replace the hose. (g) Tube mechanical joint (ferrules) for: 1) Wear on the end face: a) Permitted if the O-ring retention flange is not deformed. 2) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the end face: a) Permitted if the O-ring retention flange is not deformed after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-00-00-910-001-F00 (2) If it is necessary, replace the damaged tube as follows: WARNING DO NOT GET FUEL IN YOUR MOUTH, OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THE FUEL. KEEP THE FUEL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT. FUEL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE, WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. WARNING DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN. (a) Disassemble the connection. NOTE: Tubes can have oil or fuel in them as they are removed. Drain the fuel into a container. (f) Do an inspection of the mating and threaded surfaces for cleanliness, contamination, scratches, dents or other surface defects. (j) Apply a thin layer of oil, D00599 [CP2442], to the gaskets and seals. (k) Install the new O-rings or serviceable gaskets as necessary. (l) Install the tube but do not use force. NOTE: A small elastic distortion is permitted to engage the connections. (m) Tighten all the end fittings and all clamps with your hand. 1) After a system is installed, tighten the clamps first, then tighten the end fittings. (n) Do not chafe the tubes when you install the clamps. 1) Attach the tube loosely with a clamp and orient the tube to get the best clearance and tighten the clamps. NOTE: Use the correct minimum clearances between the tube and equipment given below. 1) Structure (frames, bolts, rivets, webs, etc.): a) The minimum clearance is 0.25 inch (6.4 mm). b) Not less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) clearance in 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) or less of clamping points. 2) Mechanism (actuators, linkages, etc.): a) The minimum clearance is 0.50 inch (12.7 mm). b) Keep the clearance during the full travel of (25.4 mm) of the mechanism. 3) Grouped tubes (parallel runs, intersections, etc.): a) The minimum clearance is 0.19 inch (4.8 mm). b) Attach clamps to the lines that go across each other to get the minimum clearance of 0.12 inch (3.0 mm). (q) Coupling nuts must turn freely in your hand. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (r) The mating surfaces of the flanges of the tube must be installed at 90 degrees to each other. (t) Attach safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] to the connection. NOTE: Make sure that the lockwire or cable is corrosion resistant steel. 72-00-00-200-801-F00Continue-In-Service (CIS) Limits - GeneralPDF p. 65

2. Continue-In-Service (CIS) Limits - General

A. General

(1) Use the CIS limits when you find a defect that you cannot correct at the present location. (2) The CIS limit permits the airplane to be flown to a facility where the defect can be corrected. (a) The necessary maintenance must be scheduled before the end of the CIS limit extension. (b) The CIS limit can be used only one time. 1) When the limit is reached, the defect must be corrected. (3) When CIS flight cycles and flight hours are given in the same limit, the condition that occurs first is the maximum limit. (4) The CIS limits are listed after the serviceable limits. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) On defects that do not have CIS limits, contact CFM.

4. Stages 2-4 Booster Blades and Vanes Borescope Inspection (Figure 601, Figure 603, and Figure 604)

A. General

(1) This task provides the instructions on how to examine the booster blades and vanes with a borescope. (2) These are the areas of the booster rotor blades that you can see: (a) The leading edge of the stage 2 blades, through the inlet to the primary gas path or the booster inlet. (b) The trailing edge of the stage 3 blades, through the borescope port S0. (c) The leading edge of the stage 4 blades, through the borescope port S0. (3) The area of the stage 2-4 booster vanes that can be seen is limited to what you can see through the inlet and around the S0 borescope port.

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-006-F00 (5) Do these steps to do an inspection of the stage 2 booster blades: NOTE: If you find Foreign Object Damage (FOD) or missing pieces, you must examine all of the downstream booster blades and vanes, and the compressor. NOTE: If the fan blades are removed, you can see the leading edges of the stage 2 booster blades without borescope equipment. WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU TURN THE FAN ROTOR. MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE IN A STABLE POSITION. ALSO, YOU MUST WEAR HEAVY PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. (a) Manually turn the fan rotor, from the front of the engine, while you do the inspection of the stage 2 booster blades. (b) Put the borescope probe so that you can view the stage 2 booster blades as you look through the booster inlet. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-007-F00 (6) Examine the stage 2 booster blades as follows: (a) Missing pieces in Area G and the tip corners of the leading and trailing edges 1) A maximum of 20 blades is permitted with these conditions: a) The axial length is less than 0.252 in. (6.4 mm). b) The radial length is less than 0.252 in. (6.4 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) The radial length is less than 0.787 in. (20 mm). b) The axial length is less than 0.492 in. (12.5 mm). (b) Cracks or tears in Area G CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) There is no limit if the radial length and the axial length are less than 0.256 in. (6.5 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) The radial length is less than 0.787 in. (20 mm). b) The axial length is less than 0.492 in. (12.5 mm). (c) Worn areas or local distortion at the blade tip corner on the leading and trailing edges 1) There is no limit with these conditions: a) The radial length is less than 0.787 in. (20 mm). b) The axial length is less than 0.492 in. (12.5 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 100 cycles or 150 flight hours with these conditions: a) The radial length is less than 0.984 in. (25 mm). b) The axial length is less than 0.59 in. (15 mm). c) No more than 15 blades are damaged. (d) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the airfoil surfaces that are in Area E 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The indication is less than 0.019 in. (0.5 mm) deep. b) The indication does not go through the metal. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) The diameter is less than 0.59 in. (15.0 mm). b) The damage does not go through the metal. (e) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the airfoil surfaces that are not in Area E, and not on the leading and trailing edges 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The diameter is less than 0.157 in. (4.0 mm). b) The damage does not go through the metal. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) The diameter is less than 0.236 in. (6.0 mm). b) The damage does not go through the metal. (f) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the leading and trailing edges, but not in Area E 1) Permitted if the maximum axial length is not more than 0.039 in. (1.0 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours if the axial length is less than 0.059 in. (1.5 mm). (g) Distortion to the leading and trailing edges and not in Area E 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The maximum axial length is 0.197 in. (5.0 mm). b) The maximum radial length is 0.59 in. (15 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) The maximum axial length is 0.275 in. (7.0 mm). b) The maximum radial length is 0.708 in. (18.0 mm). (h) Nicks, dents and scratches on the leading and trailing edges in Area E CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Permitted with this condition: a) The indication is less than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) deep. (i) Distortion to the leading and trailing edges in Area E 1) Permitted with this condition: a) The damage is less than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) from original contour. (j) Deposits and erosion 1) Permitted. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-008-F00 (7) Do these steps to install the borescope probe for the inspection of the stage 2 through 4 stator vanes: (a) Put the probe so that you can view the stage 2 stator vanes through the booster inlet. (b) Put the probe so that you can view the stage 3 and 4 stator vanes through borescope port S0. NOTE: This inspection is limited to what you can see with the rigid borescope. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-009-F00 (8) Examine the stage 2 through 4 booster vanes as follows: (a) Missing pieces 1) A maximum of 20 vanes is permitted with these conditions: a) The axial length is less than 0.256 in. (6.5 mm). b) The radial length is less than 0.728 in. (18.5 mm). c) The damage is not in Areas A and B. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) No cracks start from the damaged area. b) Cracks do not go into Areas A and B. (b) Cracks or tears 1) There is no limit to the number in Areas A and B with these conditions: a) The damage is less than 0.128 in. (3.25 mm) radially. b) The damage is less than 0.04 in. (1 mm) axially. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 15 flight hours if the damage is more than the limits but there is no possibility that a piece could break free. (c) Nicks, dents, and scratches in Areas A and B of the concave and convex surfaces 1) There is no limit to the number with these conditions: a) The diameter is less than 0.09 in. (2.3 mm). b) The damage does not go through the metal. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 15 flight hours with this condition: a) The diameter is less than 0.157 in. (4 mm). (d) Nicks, dents, and scratches in Area C 1) Permitted with this condition: a) The diameter is less than 0.197 in. (5 mm). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours if the diameter is less than 0.295 in. (7.5 mm). (e) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the leading and trailing edges 1) Permitted if the axial length is less than 0.079 in. (2 mm). (f) Vanes which have disengaged from the inner shroud 1) Vanes that are disengaged are not permitted. (g) Distortion of the leading and trailing edges 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The damage is less than 0.709 in. (18 mm) radially. b) The damage is less than 0.256 in. (6.5 mm) axially. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles or 75 flight hours with these conditions: a) The damage is less than 1 in. (25.4 mm) radially. b) The damage is less than 0.492 in. (12.5 mm) axially. (h) Separation, flaking, missing material, or booster blade tip rubbing on the abradable material of the outer shroud (stage 3 and stage 4 booster vanes only) 1) Permitted. (i) Surface oxidation, pitting or corrosion marks 1) Permitted. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-010-F00 (9) Do an inspection of the trailing edges of the stage 3 blades and the leading edges of the stage 4 blades. (a) Carefully put the borescope in the borescope port S0. NOTE: This port is found between the Outlet Guide Vane (OGV)s at the 3:30 o'clock position. (b) While you turn the fan rotor manually, examine the trailing edges of the stage 3 blades and the leading edges of the stage 4 blades. 1) Use the same damage limits given for the stage 2 blades above. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-001-F00 (10) When the inspection is complete, remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the light source to OFF, but keep the blower on until the lamp and case are cool.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-012-F00 (1) If the borescope inspection is complete, do this task: Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition, TASK 72-00-00-200-814-F00.

5. HP Compressor Blades Borescope Inspection (Figure 601, Figure 605, Figure 606, Figure 607, Figure 608 and Figure 609)

F. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-013-F00 (1) Do this task: Borescope Inspection Preparation, TASK 72-00-00-200-802-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-109-F00 (2) Connect the applicable rigid borescope to its light source as follows: NOTE: Use the rigid borescope with the yellow band. (a) Connect rigid borescope, COM-2195 to light source, SPL-4305. (b) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4302 to light source, SPL-4306. (c) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4303 to light source, SPL-2197. (d) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4304 to light source, SPL-4308 SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-047-F00 (3) Connect the rigid borescope with the long, right angle borescope extension, 90 degree right-angle viewer, and 60 degree field of vision. SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-048-F00 (4) Turn the light source to the ON position. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-014-F00 (5) Actuate the variable stator vanes (VSV) to full open (TASK 75-31-00-790-801-F00). NOTE: During engine shutdown, the VSV's will close and VSV actuator will be fully extended. (a) As an alternate procedure, do these steps: 1) If installed, remove the borescope equipment from the engine. 2) For engine no. 1, remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE 3) For engine 2, remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE 4) Do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00. 5) Put the ENGINE START switch to the CONT position to stop the dry motor procedure. NOTE: When you stop the engine with the ENGINE START switch in the CONT position, the EEC will command the VSV's to the full open position and the VBV's to the full close position. 6) After the engine stops completely, put the ENGINE START switch to the off position and do the remaining steps in the Dry Motor Procedure. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 7) For engine 1, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE 8) For engine 2, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-032-F00 (6) Find the applicable borescope plugs for the HPC stages you will examine as follows: NOTE: Do the applicable steps to get access to the applicable HPC stage. (a) Remove the lower right shroud segment (TASK 72-23-03-000-802-F00). NOTE: This is required to access the S1 borescope plug. (b) Remove the S1-S6 borescope plugs. 1) Put a tag on each plug to make sure it will be installed in the correct borescope port. (c) Remove the S7-S9 borescope plug assemblies as follows: 1) Loosen the borescope cap. a) Disengage the borescope cap from the compressor case. b) Pull the borescope cap outward to engage the internal shaft spline. CAUTION WHEN YOU REMOVE THE BORESCOPE PLUG, DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 280 IN-LB (32 N·M) TO THE PLUG. THE BORESCOPE PLUG CAN BREAK. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. 2) Loosen the borescope plug from the stator rear case. a) Remove the borescope plug assembly. 3) If the borescope plugs do not come loose at 280 in-lb (32 N·m) or less of torque, do these steps: a) Remove the retaining ring. NOTE: The retaining ring attaches the borescope cap to the shaft of the borescope plug. b) Remove the borescope cap from the borescope plug. c) Remove the borescope plug with a deep well socket. d) If it is not damaged, put the borescope cap on the borescope plug again. e) Install the retaining ring. 4) If the borescope plug breaks, do these steps: a) Remove all the pieces that fall between the inner and outer cases. b) Remove the borescope plug with a deep well socket. c) Discard the parts of the borescope plug assembly. 5) Put a tag on the borescope plug assemblies to make sure that they will be installed in the correct borescope port. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) When you examine the 6th thru 9th-stage rotor blades, and the vane segments have moved to a position that covers the borescope holes, do these steps: 1) If the diameter of the borescope holes are more than 0.24 in. (6.1 mm), use the 0.24 in. (6.1 mm) flexible borescope. 2) If the diameter of the borescope holes are less than 0.24 in. (6.1 mm), do these steps: a) Put an alignment rod (locally available) in the hole for the vane segment. b) Apply a light, downward force on the end of the rod to move the vane up in the case. NOTE: The aluminum rod has a diameter of 0.375 inch (9.52 mm), with a length of 18 inches (457 mm). There is a 4 inch (102 mm) taper at one end. Because of this taper, the diameter of the rod decreases to 0.062 inch (1.57 mm) at the end. 3) If the 7th-stage borescope hole is closed, do this step: a) Do a borescope inspection of the aft end of the compressor through the 8th or 6th stage blades, in that sequence. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-017-F00 (7) Prepare for the inspection of the compressor blades as follows: (a) Connect the rigid borescope to the light source. 1) Use the rigid borescope with the yellow band to get a general view of the airfoil. 2) Use the rigid borescope with the green band to get a better view of the blade platform area. 3) Use the rigid borescope with the blue band to get a better view of the blade tips. (b) Make sure the borescope is correctly adjusted. (c) Turn the light source ON.

G. HP Compressor Blades Borescope Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-018-F00 (1) Examine the compressor rotor blades as follows: (a) Turn (and index, if it is necessary) the N2 rotor (TASK 72-00-00-980-801-F00). (b) Put the borescope into the applicable borescope port. (c) Stop the N2 rotor when you put each blade in a position for its inspection. NOTE: This lets you do a full inspection of each blade. SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-009-F00 (2) Examine the applicable stages of the compressor blades (Figure 608): NOTE: Unless otherwise identified, all damage limits for the HPC blades are the same for the different blade configurations. Use the limits for the applicable stages. NOTE: The depth of a defect such as a nick is measured along the axis of the damage unless stated differently. NOTE: HPC blades with P/N P33XPXX (3D Aero) have a 'C' marked on the aft platform. HPC blades with P/N P39XPXX (TI) have a 'H' marked on the aft platform. (a) Cracks in stages 1 thru 4 are not serviceable unless they meet the conditions that follows: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Any number of radial tip cracks within 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) of the leading or trailing edge, up to 0.25 inch (6.4 mm) in length are serviceable. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.25 inch (6.4 mm) but less than 0.40 inch (10.2 mm) in length. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) Any number of radial tip cracks more than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the leading or trailing edge, up to 0.10 inch (2.5 mm) in length are serviceable. 3) Any number of chord-wise cracks up to 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the tip, up to 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) in length are serviceable. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) but less than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) in length. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (b) Cracks in stages 5 thru 9 are not serviceable unless they meet the conditions that follows: 1) Up to 25 blades across stages 5 thru 9 can have radial tip cracks that are no more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) from the leading or trailing edge. a) The cracks can be up to 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) in length and are serviceable. b) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) in length on less than 20% in each stage. c) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. d) Radial tip cracks more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) from the leading or trailing edge are not serviceable. 2) Up to 25 blades across stages 5 thru 9 can have chord-wise cracks that are no more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) from the tip. a) The cracks can be up to 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) long are serviceable. b) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) long. c) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (c) Missing or chipped erosion coating on the stages 1 thru 9 blades: 1) There is no limit with this condition. (d) Nicks, dents and scratches in the airfoil root radius, stages 1 thru 9, (does not include the trailing edge root radius of stage 2 and stage 3) 1) There is no limit to the number with any of these conditions: a) Elliptical, smooth, round bottom dents having no sharp edges with a maximum diameter of 0.030 inch (0.76 mm). Dents must not connect or overlap. b) Any damage with 0.005 inch (0.13 mm) maximum in depth. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL c) The scratches are not parallel to the platform. (e) Tears in the root radius, stages 1 thru 9 1) Not serviceable. (f) Nicks, dents and scratches in the trailing edge root radius of stage 2 and stage 3 1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, dents and scratches that are less than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. 2) Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours if the nicks, dents and scratches are more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. 3) There is no limit to the amount of wear on the adjacent HPC inner shroud lip. (g) Wear or scratches in the trailing edge platform of stage 2 and stage 3 1) There is no limit to the amount of wear or scratches that are less than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. 2) Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours if the wear or scratch is more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. 3) There is no limit to the amount of wear on the adjacent HPC inner shroud lip. (h) Tears, nicks, dents, and missing material on the leading and trailing edge of stages 1 thru 9 compressor blades found in the lower 25% of the airfoil (but not in the root radius). 1) Tears are not permitted. 2) There is no limit of nicks, dents and missing material if the damage is less 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours if the damage is less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm). 4) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (i) Tears, nicks, dents, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge of stages 1 thru 4 compressor blades found in Dim. B of the airfoil. 1) Tears are not serviceable. a) If you find tears, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. NOTE: You can find the limits for the repair of tears in Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) For stages 1-3, no maximum number of nicks, missing material and erosion if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 3) For NOT a Tech insertion stage 4 blade (P/N P394XXX), no maximum number of nicks, missing material and erosion if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in depth. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 4) For Tech insertion stage 4 blade (P/N P394XXX), no maximum number of nicks, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge found in Dim. B if the damage is less than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 5) No maximum number of dents in Dim. B if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) maximum depth and less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) maximum deflection from the original contour. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth, and less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) deflection from the original contour. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (j) Tears, nicks, dents, missing material and erosion at the leading and trailing edge tip corners in Dim. A of stages 1 thru 4 compressor blades. 1) No maximum number of tears, nicks and dents if the damage is less than 0.25 inch (6.4 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.25 inch (6.40 mm) in depth but less than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) Missing material and erosion at the leading and trailing edge tip corners. a) Individual blades with missing material greater than 0.30 x 0.30 inch (7.6 x 7.6 mm) on both leading and trailing edges are not permitted. b) Any number of blades for each stage 1 thru 4, up to 0.30 x 0.30 inch (7.6 x 7.6 mm) if the downstream damage is serviceable. c) For stage 2, a maximum of four blades up to 0.40 x 0.40 inch (10.2 x 10.2 mm), and 46 blades up to 0.30 x 0.30 inch (7.6 x 7.6 mm) for total of 50 blades with missing tip corners. d) For stage 3, a maximum of five blades up to 0.40 x 0.40 inch (10.2 x 10.2 mm) and 51 blades up to .30 x 0.30 inch (7.6 x 7.6 mm) for a total of 56 blades with missing tip corners. e) For stage 4, maximum of six blades up to 0.40 x 0.40 inch (10.2 x 10.2 mm) and 57 blades up to 0.30 x 0.30 inch (7.6 x 7.6 mm) for a total of 63 blades with missing tip corners. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL f) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the stage 1 damage is more than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) but less than 0.40 inch (10.2 mm) in depth. g) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if additional stage 2-4 blades have damage, which is more than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) but less than 0.40 inch (10.2 mm) in depth. (k) Tears, nicks, dents, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge of stages 5-9 compressor blade found in Dim. B. 1) No maximum number of tears, nicks, missing material and erosion if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm). b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) No maximum number of dents if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) maximum depth and less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) maximum deflection from original contour. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth, and less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) maximum deflection from the original contour. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (l) Tears, nicks, dents, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge of stages 5-9 compressor blade found in Dim. A. 1) No maximum number of tears, nicks and dents if the damage is less than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) Missing material and erosion at the leading edge and trailing edge tip corners. a) All blades can have missing material and erosion at the tip corner up to 0.15 inch x 0.15 inch (3.8 mm x 3.8 mm) if the downstream damage is serviceable. b) Up to a total of 25 blades across stages 5 thru 9, with missing material up to 0.20 inch x 0.20 inch (5.1 mm x 5.1 mm) if the downstream damage is serviceable. c) If more than 25 blades across stages 5-9 have damage that is more than 0.15 inch x 0.15 inch (3.8 mm x 3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch x 0.20 inch (5.1 mm x 5.1 mm), a maximum service extension of 100 cycles is permitted. d) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.20 inch x 0.20 inch (5.1 mm x 5.1 mm) but less than 0.30 inch x 0.30 inch (7.6 mm x 7.6 mm) on a maximum of 20% in each stage. (m) Any amount of tears, nicks, dents, missing material, erosion, bends and burrs found on the stage 1 thru 9 compressor blade tip is serviceable. NOTE: The blade tip is the top 0.10 inch (2.5 mm of the blade. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (n) Curl on the end of the of the stage 1 thru 9 blades 1) Up to 25% of the stages 1 thru 4 blade chord, and maximum radial length of 0.30 inch (7.6 mm), when it does not engage the stationary parts during operation. 2) Up to 50% of the stages 5 thru 9 blade chord radially down 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the tip when it does not engage the stationary parts during operation. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is up to 75% of the blade chord radially down 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the tip when it does not engage the stationary parts during operation. (o) Nicks, dents, erosion, and scratches on the stages 1 thru 9 blade airfoil center panel 1) There is no limit to the quantity of erosion and scratches. 2) There is no maximum number of nicks and dents if the damage is not cracked on either side of the blade. (p) Platform of stages 4-9 locking blades. 1) Clearance between the blade platforms is permitted. 2) There is no maximum limit to the size and quantity of distortions on a blade. 3) Cracks in the material are not serviceable. 4) Shingling is not serviceable. (q) Blade locks for the stages 4-9 blades 1) Any number of cracks on one lock is permitted for each stage. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted for two blade locks in the same stage with any number of cracks, if no blade locks are loose in the given stage. 2) Loose blade locks are not permitted. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted for one loose blade lock on a stage, if the other blade lock on the same stage is not loose or cracked. (r) Material on blades 1) No maximum amount of material which is found on the blades. (s) Compressor stator vane shrouds, stages (Figure 610) 1) No maximum limit of wear caused by rubbing on vanes. (t) The rub coat at the stator flow path NOTE: The area adjacent to the borescope ports is the only rub coat you can examine. 1) No maximum limit of areas where the rub coat is gone. 2) No maximum number of cracks which are crazed. (u) Through holes on stage 1 thru 9 blades 1) Through holes are not serviceable. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-002-F00 (3) If the inspection is complete, remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the lightsource to OFF, but keep the blower ON until the lamp and case are cool. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 72-00-00-980-004-F00 (1) If you manually opened the VSV's, actuate the VSV's to full close and remove the equipment (TASK 75-31-00-790-801-F00). NOTE: If you did the Dry Motor Procedure to open the VSV's, no action is necessary. The EEC will move the VSV's and VBV's to their usual position at the subsequent engine start. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-021-F00 (2) Do these steps to install the S1-S6 borescope plugs: (a) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] to the threads and to the friction surfaces of the plug. (b) Install the plugs in the compressor case. 1) Tighten the plug to 57-63 pound-inches (6.4-7.1 Newton-meters). (c) Put safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] on the plugs. SUBTASK 72-00-00-410-021-F00 (3) If removed, install the lower right shroud segment (TASK 72-23-03-400-802-F00). SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-022-F00 (4) Do these steps to install the S7-S9 borescope plugs: (a) Before you install the S7-S9 borescope plugs, make sure the inner borescope port is open as follows: 1) Put the compressor borescope tool in the borescope port (Figure 606). (b) Apply a light layer of these lubricants to the borescope plug assembly as follows: 1) Apply pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619], graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] to the threads and mating surfaces on the inner plug. 2) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] to the threads of the outer plug. (c) Install the borescope plug in the applicable borescope port and tighten as follows: 1) Tighten the inner plug to 76-84 pound-inches (8.6-9.5 Newton-meters). 2) Loosen the inner plug by one-quarter turn. 3) Tighten the inner plug again to the run-on torque plus 15-20 pound-inches (1.7-2.3 Newton-meters). 4) Push the outer plug to engage the threads in the compressor case. a) Tighten the outer plug by hand. 5) Tighten the outer plug to 57-63 pound-inches (6.4-7.1 Newton-meters). a) Attach all three outer plugs together with safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] or safety wire, G02345 [CP8001]. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-023-F00 (5) If the borescope inspection is complete, do this task: Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition, TASK 72-00-00-200-814-F00.

F. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-120-F00 (1) Do this task: Borescope Inspection Preparation, TASK 72-00-00-200-802-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-004-F00 (2) Connect the applicable rigid borescope to its light source as follows: NOTE: Use the rigid borescope with the yellow band. (a) Connect rigid borescope, COM-2195 to light source, SPL-4305. (b) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4302 to light source, SPL-4306. (c) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4303 to light source, SPL-2197. (d) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4304 to light source, SPL-4308 SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-049-F00 (3) Connect the rigid borescope with the long, right angle borescope extension, 90 degree right-angle viewer, and 60 degree field of vision. SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-050-F00 (4) Turn the light source to the ON position. SUBTASK 72-00-00-860-022-F00 (5) To actuate the variable stator vanes (VSV) to full open, do this task: VSV Actuation System - Manual Operation, TASK 75-31-00-790-801-F00. NOTE: During engine shutdown, the VSV's will close and the VSV actuator will be fully extended. (a) As an alternate procedure, do these steps: 1) If installed, remove the borescope equipment from the engine. 2) For engine no. 1, remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE 3) For engine 2, remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE 4) Do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00. 5) Put the ENGINE START switch to the CONT position to stop the dry motor procedure. NOTE: When you stop the engine with the ENGINE START switch in the CONT position, the EEC will command the VSV's to the fully open position and the VBV's to the fully closed position. 6) After the engine stops completely, put the ENGINE START switch to the OFF position and do the remaining steps in the dry motor procedure. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 7) For engine 1, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE 8) For engine 2, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-041-F00 (6) Find the applicable borescope plugs (S2-S9) for the HPC stages (2,4,6 and 8) that you will examine. SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-034-F00 (7) Do these steps to get access to the applicable HPC stage. (a) Remove the S2-S6 borescope plugs. 1) Put a tag on each plug to make sure it will be installed in the correct borescope port. (b) Do these steps to remove the S7-S9 borescope plug assemblies: 1) Loosen the borescope cap. a) Disengage the borescope cap from the compressor case. b) Pull the borescope cap outward to engage the internal shaft spline. CAUTION WHEN YOU REMOVE THE BORESCOPE PLUG, DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 280 IN-LB (32 N·M) TO THE PLUG. THE BORESCOPE PLUG CAN BREAK. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. 2) Loosen the borescope plug from the stator rear case. a) Remove the borescope plug assembly. 3) If the borescope plugs do not come loose at 280 inch-pounds (31.5 Newton-meters) or less of torque, do these steps: a) Remove the retaining ring. NOTE: The retaining ring attaches the borescope cap to the shaft of the borescope plug. b) Remove the borescope cap from the borescope plug. c) Remove the borescope plug with a deep well socket. d) If it is not damaged, put the borescope cap on the borescope plug again. e) Install the retaining ring. 4) If the borescope plug breaks, do these steps: a) Remove all the pieces that fall between the inner and outer cases. b) Remove the borescope plug with a deep well socket. c) Discard the parts of the borescope plug assembly. 5) Put a tag on the borescope plug assemblies to make sure that they will be installed in the correct borescope port. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) When you examine the 6th and 8th-stage rotor blades, and the vane segments have moved to a position that covers the borescope holes, do these steps: 1) If the diameter of the borescope holes are larger than 0.24 inch (6.1 mm), use the 0.24 inch (6.1 mm) flexible borescope. 2) If the diameter of the borescope holes are less than 0.24 inch (6.1 mm), do these steps: a) Put a alignment rod (locally available) in the hole for the vane segment. b) Apply a light, downward force on the end of the rod to move the vane up in the case. NOTE: The aluminum rod has a diameter of 0.375 inch (9.52 mm), with a length of 18 inches (457 mm). There is a 4 inch (102 mm) taper at one end. Because of this taper, the diameter of the rod decreases to 0.062 inch (1.57 mm) at the end. 3) If the 7th-stage borescope hole is closed, do this step: a) Do a borescope inspection of the aft end of the compressor through the 8th or 6th stage blades, in that sequence. SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-005-F00 (8) Do these steps to prepare for the inspection of the compressor blades: (a) Connect the rigid borescope to the light source. 1) Use the rigid borescope with the yellow band to get a general view of the airfoil. 2) Use the rigid borescope with the green band to get a better view of the blade platform area. 3) Use the rigid borescope with the blue band to get a better view of the blade tips. (b) Make sure the borescope is correctly adjusted. (c) Turn the light source ON.

G. HP Compressor Blades (Stages 2,4,6 and 8) Borescope Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-006-F00 (1) Examine the compressor rotor blades as follows: (a) Turn (and index, if it is necessary) the N2 rotor (TASK 72-00-00-980-801-F00). (b) Put the borescope into the applicable borescope port. (c) Stop the N2 rotor when you put each blade in a position for its inspection. NOTE: This lets you do a full inspection of each blade. SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-010-F00 (2) Examine the stage 2, 4, 6 and 8 HP compressor blades with the HPC Inspection Limits for the applicable stages in the following subtask. (a) If the HPC limits are listed for stages 1 thru 9, then use these limits for stages 2, 4, 6, and 8. (b) If the HPC limits are listed for stages 1 thru 4, then use these limits for stages 2 and 4. (c) If the HPC limits are listed for stages 5 thru 9, then use these limits for stages 6 and 8. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-011-F00 (3) Examine the applicable stages of the compressor blades (Figure 608): NOTE: Unless otherwise identified, all damage limits for the HPC blades are the same for the different blade configurations. Use the limits for the applicable stages. NOTE: The depth of a defect such as a nick is measured along the axis of the damage unless stated differently. NOTE: HPC blades with P/N P33XPXX (3D Aero) have a 'C' marked on the aft platform. HPC blades with P/N P39XPXX (TI) have a 'H' marked on the aft platform. (a) Cracks in stages 1 thru 4 are not serviceable unless they meet the conditions that follows: 1) Any number of radial tip cracks within 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) of the leading or trailing edge, up to 0.25 inch (6.4 mm) in length are serviceable. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.25 inch (6.4 mm) but less than 0.40 inch (10.2 mm) in length. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) Any number of radial tip cracks more than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the leading or trailing edge, up to 0.10 inch (2.5 mm) in length are serviceable. 3) Any number of chord-wise cracks up to 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the tip, up to 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) in length are serviceable. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) but less than 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) in length. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (b) Cracks in stages 5 thru 9 are not serviceable unless they meet the conditions that follows: 1) Up to 25 blades across stages 5 thru 9 can have radial tip cracks that are no more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) from the leading or trailing edge. a) The cracks can be up to 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) in length and are serviceable. b) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) in length on less than 20% in each stage. c) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. d) Radial tip cracks more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) from the leading or trailing edge are not serviceable. 2) Up to 25 blades across stages 5 thru 9 can have chord-wise cracks that are no more than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) from the tip. a) The cracks can be up to 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) long are serviceable. b) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) long. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL c) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (c) Missing or chipped erosion coating on the stages 1 thru 9 blades: 1) There is no limit with this condition. (d) Nicks, dents and scratches in the airfoil root radius, stages 1 thru 9, (does not include the trailing edge root radius of stage 2 and stage 3) 1) There is no limit to the number with any of these conditions: a) Elliptical, smooth, round bottom dents having no sharp edges with a maximum diameter of 0.030 inch (0.76 mm). Dents must not connect or overlap. b) Any damage with 0.005 inch (0.13 mm) maximum in depth. c) The scratches are not parallel to the platform. (e) Tears in the root radius, stages 1 thru 9 1) Not serviceable. (f) Nicks, dents and scratches in the trailing edge root radius of stage 2 and stage 3 1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, dents and scratches that are less than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. 2) Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours if the nicks, dents and scratches are more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. 3) There is no limit to the amount of wear on the adjacent HPC inner shroud lip. (g) Wear or scratches in the trailing edge platform of stage 2 and stage 3 1) There is no limit to the amount of wear or scratches that are less than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. 2) Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours if the wear or scratch is more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. 3) There is no limit to the amount of wear on the adjacent HPC inner shroud lip. (h) Tears, nicks, dents, and missing material on the leading and trailing edge of stages 1 thru 9 compressor blades found in the lower 25% of the airfoil (but not in the root radius). 1) Tears are not permitted. 2) There is no limit of nicks, dents and missing material if the damage is less 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours if the damage is less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm). 4) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (i) Tears, nicks, dents, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge of stages 1 thru 4 compressor blades found in Dim. B of the airfoil. 1) Tears are not serviceable. a) If you find tears, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. NOTE: You can find the limits for the repair of tears in Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) For stages 1-3, no maximum number of nicks, missing material and erosion if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 3) For NOT a Tech insertion stage 4 blade (P/N P394XXX), no maximum number of nicks, missing material and erosion if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 4) For Tech insertion stage 4 blade (P/N P394XXX), no maximum number of nicks, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge found in Dim. B if the damage is less than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 5) No maximum number of dents in Dim. B. 1) No maximum number of tears, nicks, missing material and erosion if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) but less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm). b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) No maximum number of dents if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) maximum depth and less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) maximum deflection from original contour. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is less than 0.08 inch (2.0 mm) in depth, and less than 0.06 inch (1.5 mm) maximum deflection from the original contour. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. (l) Tears, nicks, dents, missing material and erosion on the leading and trailing edge of stages 5-9 compressor blade found in Dim. A. 1) No maximum number of tears, nicks and dents if the damage is less than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) in depth. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.15 inch (3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) in depth. b) If you find damage that is more than the limits, do this task: Repair the HPC Rotor Blades, TASK 72-00-00-300-801-F00. 2) Missing material and erosion at the leading edge and trailing edge tip corners. a) All blades can have missing material and erosion at the tip corner up to 0.15 inch x 0.15 inch (3.8 mm x 3.8 mm) if the downstream damage is serviceable. b) Up to a total of 25 blades across stages 5 thru 9, with missing material up to 0.20 inch x 0.20 inch (5.1 mm x 5.1 mm) if the downstream damage is serviceable. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL c) If more than 25 blades across stages 5-9 have damage that is more than 0.15 inch x 0.15 inch (3.8 mm x 3.8 mm) but less than 0.20 inch x 0.20 inch (5.1 mm x 5.1 mm), a maximum service extension of 100 cycles is permitted. d) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is more than 0.20 inch x 0.20 inch (5.1 mm x 5.1 mm) but less than 0.30 inch x 0.30 inch (7.6 mm x 7.6 mm) on a maximum of 20% in each stage. (m) Any amount of tears, nicks, dents, missing material, erosion, bends and burrs found on the stage 1 thru 9 compressor blade tip is serviceable. NOTE: The blade tip is the top 0.10 inch (2.5 mm of the blade. (n) Curl on the end of the of the stage 1 thru 9 blades 1) Up to 25% of the stages 1 thru 4 blade chord, and maximum radial length of 0.30 inch (7.6 mm), when it does not engage the stationary parts during operation. 2) Up to 50% of the stages 5 thru 9 blade chord radially down 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the tip when it does not engage the stationary parts during operation. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if the damage is up to 75% of the blade chord radially down 0.30 inch (7.6 mm) from the tip when it does not engage the stationary parts during operation. (o) Nicks, dents, erosion, and scratches on the stages 1 thru 9 blade airfoil center panel 1) There is no limit to the quantity of erosion and scratches. 2) There is no maximum number of nicks and dents if the damage is not cracked on either side of the blade. (p) Platform of stages 4-9 locking blades. 1) Clearance between the blade platforms is permitted. 2) There is no maximum limit to the size and quantity of distortions on a blade. 3) Cracks in the material are not serviceable. 4) Shingling is not serviceable. (q) Blade locks for the stages 4-9 blades 1) Any number of cracks on one lock is permitted for each stage. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted for two blade locks in the same stage with any number of cracks, if no blade locks are loose in the given stage. 2) Loose blade locks are not permitted. a) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted for one loose blade lock on a stage, if the other blade lock on the same stage is not loose or cracked. (r) Material on blades 1) No maximum amount of material which is found on the blades. (s) Compressor stator vane shrouds, stages (Figure 610) 1) No maximum limit of wear caused by rubbing on vanes. (t) The rub coat at the stator flow path NOTE: The area adjacent to the borescope ports is the only rub coat you can examine. 1) No maximum limit of areas where the rub coat is gone. 2) No maximum number of cracks which are crazed. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (u) Through holes on stage 1 thru 9 blades 1) Through holes are not serviceable. SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-008-F00 (4) If the inspection is complete, remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the light source to OFF, but keep the blower ON until the lamp and case are cool.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 72-00-00-860-023-F00 (1) If you manually opened the VSV's, actuate the VSV's to full close and remove the equipment (TASK 75-31-00-790-801-F00). NOTE: If you did the Dry Motor Procedure to open the VSV's, no action is necessary. The EEC will move the VSV's and VBV's to their usual position at the subsequent engine start. SUBTASK 72-00-00-410-025-F00 (2) Do these steps to install the S2-S6 borescope plugs: (a) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] to the threads and to the friction surfaces of the plug. (b) Install the plugs in the compressor case. 1) Tighten the plug to 57-63 pound-inches (6.4-7.1 Newton-meters). (c) Put safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] on the plugs. SUBTASK 72-00-00-410-026-F00 (3) Do these steps to install the S7-S9 borescope plugs: (a) Before you install the S7-S9 borescope plugs, make sure the inner borescope port is open. 1) Put the aluminum rod in the borescope port (Figure 606). (b) Apply a light layer of these lubricants to the borescope plug assembly as follows: 1) Apply pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619], graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] to the threads and mating surfaces on the inner plug. 2) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] to the threads of the outer plug. (c) Install the borescope plug in the applicable borescope port. 1) Tighten the inner plug to 76-84 pound-inches (8.6-9.5 Newton-meters). 2) Loosen the inner plug by one-quarter turn. 3) Tighten the inner plug again to the run-on torque plus 15-20 pound-inches (1.7-2.26 Newton-meters). 4) Push the outer plug to engage the threads in the compressor case. a) Tighten the outer plug by hand. 5) Tighten the outer plug to 57-63 pound-inches (6.4-7.1 Newton-meters). a) Attach all three outer plugs together with safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] or safety wire, G02345 [CP8001]. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-121-F00 (4) If the borescope inspection is complete, do this task: Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition, TASK 72-00-00-200-814-F00.

7. Combustion Section Borescope Inspection (Figure 601, Figure 611, Figure 612 or Figure 613, Figure 614, Figure 615) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
