F. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-024-F00 (1) Do this task: Borescope Inspection Preparation, TASK 72-00-00-200-802-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-004-F00 (2) Remove the S13 and S15 borescope plugs. NOTE: To do an initial inspection, it is only necessary to remove the S13 and S15 borescope plugs. If you find damage, you must remove the main igniter plugs and the other borescope plugs to do a complete inspection. (a) Identify each BSI plug. (b) Remove the S13 and S15 BSI plugs. (c) Attach an identification tag onto the borescope plugs to make sure that each borescope plug is installed back in the correct borescope port after this procedure. SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-005-F00 (3) If it is necessary to do a complete inspection, do these steps to remove the main igniter plugs and the other borescope plugs: NOTE: The port for the 4:00 o'clock main igniter plug is referred to as the S10 borescope port. The port for the 8:00 o'clock main igniter plug is referred to as the S11 borescope port. (a) Do this task: Main Igniter Plug Removal, TASK 74-21-02-000-801-F00. (b) Remove the S12 and S14 borescope plugs. 1) Identify each BSI plug. 2) Remove the S12 and S14 BSI plugs. 3) Attach an identification tag onto the borescope plugs to make sure that each borescope plug is installed back in the correct borescope port after this procedure. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-027-F00 (4) Do these steps to prepare for the inspection of the combustion section: (a) Connect the applicable rigid borescope to the light source. 1) Connect rigid borescope, COM-2195, and light source, SPL-4305. 2) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4302, and light source, SPL-4306. 3) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4303, and light source, SPL-2197. 4) Connect rigid borescope, COM-4304, and light source, SPL-4308. 5) Use the rigid borescope with the yellow band to get a general view of the combustion chamber. 6) Use the rigid borescope with the green band as follows: a) Use the borescope to view circumferentially around the combustion chamber. b) Use the borescope to view the inner liner that is adjacent to the borescope port. 7) Use the rigid borescope with the blue band to view the outer liner that is adjacent the borescope port. 8) Use the rigid borescope with the black band to view the aft ends of the inner and outer liners. 9) Use the rigid borescope with the black band to evaluate defects that you found with the other borescopes. 10) Use the fiberscope to view the outside of the outer liner. (b) Make sure that you adjust the borescope correctly. (c) Turn the lightsource ON. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-028-F00 (5) If it is necessary to do an inspection of the cold-side of the outer liner, do these steps to prepare for the inspection: (a) Connect the borescope, COM-2196, to the applicable light source. (b) Make sure that you adjust the borescope correctly. (c) Turn the light source ON.

G. Combustion Section Borescope Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-118-F00 (1) Examine all surfaces as follow: (a) Discoloration 1) Permitted. (b) Carbon accumulation 1) Permitted. (c) Missing, chipped or spalled areas of the thermal barrier coating 1) Permitted. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-029-F00 (2) Examine the dome assembly as follows: (a) Distortion of the deflector or the sleeve 1) Permitted. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Radial cracks in the spectacle plate 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The cracks are not connected. b) The cracks are less than 2 in. (50.8 mm) in length. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 flight hours is permitted with these conditions: a) The cracks are not connected. b) The cracks are less than 2.5 in. (63.5 mm) in length. (c) Circumferential cracks in the spectacle plate 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The cracks are less than 3 in. (76.2 mm) in length. b) The minimum distance between cracks is not less than 6 in. (152.4 mm) . 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 flight hours, is permitted with these conditions: a) The cracks are less than 3.6 in. (91.4 mm). b) The minimum distance between cracks is not less than 4.8 in. (121.9 mm). (d) Cracks in the spectacle plate that are connected 1) One radial crack can be connected to one circumferential crack that extends between adjacent deflectors with these conditions: a) The radial crack is less than 2 in. (50.8 mm) in length. b) The circumferential crack is less than 3 in. (76.2 mm). c) The minimum distance between cracks is not less than 6 in. (152.4 mm). 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 flight hours is permitted with these conditions: a) The radial crack is not more than 2.5 in. (63.5 mm) in length. b) The circumferential crack is not more than 3.6 in. (91.4 mm) in length. c) The minimum distance between cracks is not less than 4.8 in. (121.9 mm). (e) Missing material from the spectacle plate 1) A maximum area of 0.060 x 0.060 inch (1.52 x 1.52 mm) is permitted at the point where the cracks connect. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 flight hours is permitted if the damage is more than the limits. (f) Radial cracks in the deflector or the sleeve 1) Permitted, if they are less than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) in length. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted if the cracks are not more than 0.6 in. (15.2 mm) in length. (g) Circumferential cracks in the deflector or sleeve 1) There is no limit to the number of cracks if they are less than 0.75 in. (19.0 mm) in length. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted if the cracks are not more than 0.9 in. (22.9 mm) in length. (h) Cracks that connect in the deflector or sleeve 1) One radial and one circumferential crack that connect are permitted, with these conditions: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) The radial crack is less than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) in length. b) The circumferential crack is less than 0.75 in. (19.0 mm) in length. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) The radial crack is not more than 0.6 in. (15.2 mm) in length. b) The circumferential crack is not more than 0.9 in. (22.9 mm) in length. (i) Missing material from the extensions on the deflector NOTE: Examine the deflector surface as close to perpendicular as possible. 1) Up to 15-exposed dome cooling holes permitted in each deflector quadrant (Figure 612 or Figure 613, View C2). 2) Not more than 20-exposed dome cooling holes in any deflector (Figure 612 or Figure 613, View C3). 3) Do this inspection again after 750 cycles if up to 25 dome cooling holes total in any deflector are exposed. 4) More than 25-exposed dome cooling holes total in any deflector, the continue-in-service limit is 25 cycles. (j) Missing material from the extensions on the sleeve 1) Permitted if the depth is not more than 0.20 in. (5.08 mm). 2) A continue-in-service limit of 50 cycles is permitted if the depth is not more than 0.240 in. (6.10 mm). (k) Burn holes 1) 3 areas for each dome are permitted if the maximum area of each hole is not more than 1.0 x 1.0 inch (25.4 x 25.4 mm). 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) There are not more than 3 areas on each dome that have missing material. b) Each area is not more than 1.2 x 1.2 inch (30.5 x 30.5 mm). (l) Cracks in the primary swirl nozzle 1) Permitted. (m) Cracks and missing material from the secondary swirl nozzle venturi. 1) Any number of secondary swirl nozzle venturis with indications (cracks) permitted. 2) Any number of secondary swirl nozzle venturis with total missing material at each venturi up to 0.100 in. (2.5 mm) in width permitted (Figure 612 or Figure 613 , View C1). 3) Up to six secondary swirl nozzle venturis with total missing material at each venturi over 0.100 in. (2.5 mm), but not more than 0.300 in. (7.6 mm) in width permitted. 4) Do this inspection again after 750 cycles if there is up to ten secondary swirl nozzle venturis with total missing material at each venturi over 0.100 in. (2.5 mm), but not more than 0.300 in. (7.6 mm) in width. 5) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles for: a) Any of the secondary swirl nozzle venturis that have total missing material over 0.300 in. (7.6 mm) in width, or b) More than ten secondary swirl nozzle venturis that have total missing material at each venturi over 0.100 in. (2.5 mm). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-030-F00 (3) Examine the inner and outer liners as follow: (a) Axial cracks on the outer liner NOTE: The dome band is counted as a panel. NOTE: Axial cracks that become circumferential cracks for a length that is less than one dilution land, should be counted as one continuous axial crack. 1) Cracks that go across only one panel are permitted. 2) A maximum of 4 cracks that go across more than one panel are permitted with this condition: a) The cracks cannot go across more than 3 panels. 3) If a crack is longer than 3 panels, do the borescope inspection of the cold side of the outer liner. NOTE: Do the inspection of the cold side only if you have no more than 3 cracks that are longer than 3 panels. More than 3 cracks that are longer than 3 panels are not permitted. 4) A continue-in-service limit of 100 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) There are not more than 5 cracks that go across more than one panel. b) A crack cannot go across more than 5 panels in sequence. (b) The cold side of the outer liner for cracks NOTE: Do this inspection of the cold side only if you find not more than 3 cracks that are longer than 3 panels during the hot side inspection. More than 3 cracks that are longer than 3 panels is not permitted. 1) The cracks must not go through more than one of the last three cooling ribs (cooling ribs 4, 5, or 6). 2) Cooling rib 1 must not be cracked through. 3) Do this inspection again after 750 cycles. 4) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) There are no more than 5 cracks that go across more than one panel. b) There are no cracks that go across more than 5 panels. c) At least one of the cooling ribs (3, 4, 5, or 6) do not have cracks that go through to the cold side. d) Cooling rib 1 does not have a crack that goes through. (c) Axial cracks on the inner liner 1) Permitted if the cracks do not go across more than one panel. 2) There are not more than 4 cracks that go across more than one panel. 3) Only one crack can go across more than three panels with these conditions: a) The crack does not go across more than 4 panels. b) The crack is connected to a hole caused by burn-through or missing material which is not more than 3 times the size of a dilution hole. c) The crack is not connected to a circumferential crack that is more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) in length. d) Do this inspection again after each 750 cycles. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 4) A continue-in-service limit of 100 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) There are not more than 5 cracks that go across more than one panel. b) There are no cracks that go across more than 4 panels in sequence. (d) Circumferential cracks on the inner and outer liners NOTE: Use the length of the dilution lands to help you find the length of the cracks. NOTE: For all non /3 Engines: For the dome bands and panel 2 of the inner and outer liner, use the dilution lands (the distance between the edges of the dilution holes) on panel 1. For the panels 4 and 5 on the outer liner and panel 4 of the inner liner, use the dilution lands on panel 3. NOTE: For /3 and /3 PIP Engines: For the dome bands of the inner and outer liner, use the dilution lands (the distance between the edges of the dilution holes) on panel 1. For the panels 3 to 5 on the outer liner and panels 3 and 4 on the inner liner, use the dilution lands on panel 2. 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The cracks are not longer than 2 dilution lands. b) There are no more than 2 adjacent cracks in a dilution land. c) The cracks are separated by a minimum of 3 dilution lands that do not have cracks. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) The cracks are not longer than 3 dilution lands. b) The cracks are separated by a minimum of 3 dilution lands that do not have cracks. (e) The inner and outer liners for axial and circumferential cracks that connect 1) One axial and one circumferential crack that connect are permitted, if the cracks are in the previous limits. 2) Multiple axial and circumferential cracks that connect are permitted, if: a) The cracks are contained in one panel. b) The cracks are contained in one dilution land area. c) There are not more than two locations in the adjacent panels that are axially aligned. d) The locations are separated by a minimum of 3 dilution lands that do not have cracks. e) There are not more than 5 locations with connected cracks. 3) A continue-In-service limit of 100 cycles is permitted with this condition: a) The cracks do not exceed their individual continue-in-service limits. (f) Holes that are burned through 1) All quantities of holes total for the two liners are permitted with these conditions: a) There are not more than two holes in the adjacent panels that are axially aligned. b) The maximum size of all holes are not more than 5 times the size of a dilution hole. c) The total area of burn through does not to exceed 15 times the size of a dilution hole. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) If the current condition exceeds the above limits but does not exceed the continue-in-service limit, repeat this borescope inspection of the holes that are burned through on the inner and outer liner every 250 cycles until the current condition exceeds the continue-in-service limit. 3) A continue-in-service limit of 100 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) There are more than three holes in the adjacent panels that are axially aligned. b) The maximum size of all holes are not more than 6 times the size of the dilution hole. c) The total area of burn through exceeds 24 times the size of a dilution hole. (g) Missing overhangs on the inner and outer liners 1) 14 areas in each liner are permitted with these conditions: a) Each area is not more than 2 times the size of the dilution hole. b) They are not axially aligned across more than 3 adjacent panels. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted with these conditions: a) There are not more than 17 areas in each liner. b) Each area is not more than 2 times the size of the dilution hole. c) They are not axially aligned across more than 3 areas in adjacent panels. (h) Distortion of the inner and outer liners 1) All distortions are permitted if each is not distorted more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) from the original contour. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted if the distortion is not more than 0.7 in. (17.8 mm) from the original contour for each area. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-115-F00 (4) If there was a birdstrike/FOD, do these steps to examine the combustion chamber: (a) Remove the borescope plugs from the combustor as follows: 1) Attach an identification tag onto the borescope plugs to make sure that each borescope plug is installed back in the correct borescope port after this procedure. 2) Borescope plug S15 at 10:00 o'clock position 3) Borescope plug S12 at 1:00 o'clock position 4) Borescope plug S13 at 3:00 o'clock position 5) Borescope plug S14 at 6:00 o'clock position. (b) Do a borescope or fiberscope inspection of the nozzle and swirlers as follows: 1) Put the borescope into one of the ports and turn on the light source for the borescope. 2) Look at the swirler and nozzle area in a clockwise and counter-clockwise direction. NOTE: When you use a rigid borescope, you will only see one swirler and two deflectors in a clockwise or counter-clockwise direction. 3) Do the fuel nozzle tip inspection as follows: a) The primary tips must be in the internal diameter of the primary swirler. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL b) If the damaged fuel nozzle is not in the internal diameter of the primary swirler, replace the engine (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00 and TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00). 4) Look at the opening between the forward edge of the deflector plate and the spectacle plate. a) The clearance must be more than 0.080 in. (2.03 mm). b) The clearance must not be more than 0.300 in. (7.62 mm). c) If the opening is more than 0.300 in. (7.62 mm), examine the area around the nozzle and the outer side of the combustion chamber. 5) Do the inspection through the other ports. 6) If one or more of the above deflector plates are out of limits, and if you are sure the tip is in the correct position, do these steps: a) Identify the fuel nozzle adjacent to the damaged area. b) Remove the borescope. c) Remove the adjacent fuel nozzle (TASK 73-11-04-000-805-F01 or TASK 73-11-04-000-804-F02). d) Examine the fuel nozzle for damage. e) If the fuel nozzle is in the internal diameter and does not touch the sides, continue to use the engine. f) If the fuel nozzle is damaged, replace the fuel nozzle (TASK 73-11-04-400-805-F01 or TASK 73-11-04-400-804-F02). (c) It is recommended (not mandatory) to do a one-time borescope inspection of the HPT nozzle leading edges at 400-800 cycles after the birdstrike event: 1) If no leading-edge distress is seen, go back to the usual borescope inspection interval. 2) If you can see missing material or burn through on the HPT nozzle leading-edge wall, contact CFMI and, do this task: Birdstrike/FOD/Ice Ingestion in Engine - Fault Isolation, FIM 71-05 TASK 801. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-003-F00 (5) When the inspection is complete, remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the light source to OFF, but keep the blower ON until the lamp and case are cool.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-032-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE BORESCOPE PLUGS ARE INSTALLED IN THE CORRECT PORT LOCATIONS. ENGINE DAMAGE CAN OCCUR IF A BORESCOPE PLUG IS NOT INSTALLED IN THE CORRECT LOCATION. (1) Do these steps to install the borescope plugs as follow: NOTE: The borescope plugs to the HPT, the LPT stage 1 and combustion case have the same thread size. The stem of the borescope plugs to the HPT or the LPT stage 1 nozzle will be burned away if it is installed in the borescope port for the combustion case (Figure 614). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Lubricate the threads of the borescope plugs with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619], or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064]. (b) Install the borescope plugs. 1) Tighten each borescope plug to 57 in-lb (6.4 N·m) - 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m). 2) Install a safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006], on each borescope plug. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-033-F00 (2) If it is necessary, do this task: Main Igniter Plug Installation, TASK 74-21-02-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-034-F00 (3) If the borescope inspection is complete, do this task: Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition, TASK 72-00-00-200-814-F00.

F. Prepare for the Inspection of the HPT Nozzle Guide Vanes

SUBTASK 72-00-00-840-028-F00 (1) If not already done, do this task: Borescope Inspection Preparation, TASK 72-00-00-200-802-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-130-F00 (2) Make sure that you verify the version of the CFM56 engine on the data placard. NOTE: The newest version of the CFM56-7B series engine is the CFM56-7BXXE engine. The “XX” in CFM56-7BXX/3 is the thrust rating of the engine. This information is found on the engine data placard on the engine fan case. NOTE: A Tech Insertion (TI) engine has a “/3” after the thrust rating on the engine data plate. An example of a Singular Annular Combustor (SAC) Engine with TI is CFM56-7B22/3. An example of a non-TI engine is CFM56-7B22. The “XX” in CFM56-7BXX/3 is the thrust rating of the engine. This information is found on the engine data placard on the engine fan case. SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-038-F00 (3) Remove the S13 and S15 borescope plugs (Figure 611 and Figure 615): NOTE: To do an initial inspection, it is only necessary to remove the S13 and S15 borescope plugs. If you find damage, you must remove the main igniter plugs and the other borescope plugs to do a complete inspection. (a) Identify each BSI plug. (b) Remove the S13 and S15 BSI plugs. (c) Attach an identification tag onto the borescope plugs to make sure that each borescope plug is installed back in the correct borescope port after this procedure. SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-039-F00 (4) If you find damage from the initial inspection, do these steps to remove the main igniter plugs and the other borescope plugs: NOTE: The port for the 4:00 o'clock main igniter plug is referred to as the S10 borescope port. The port for the 8:00 o'clock main igniter plug is referred to as the S11 borescope port. (a) Do this task: Main Igniter Plug Removal, TASK 74-21-02-000-801-F00. (b) Remove the S12 and S14 borescope plugs. 1) Identify each BSI plug. 2) Remove the S12 and S14 BSI plugs. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) Attach an identification tag onto the borescope plugs to make sure that each borescope plug is installed back in the correct borescope port after this procedure. SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-032-F00 (5) Do these steps to prepare for the inspection of the HPT nozzle. (a) Connect the applicable borescope to the light source. 1) rigid borescope, COM-2195 and light source, SPL-4305 2) rigid borescope, COM-4302 and light source, SPL-4306 3) rigid borescope, COM-4303 and light source, SPL-2197 4) rigid borescope, COM-4304 and light source, SPL-4308 5) Use the rigid borescope with the black band. (b) Put the rigid borescope through the borescope port. (c) Turn the light source ON. SUBTASK 72-00-00-480-033-F00 (6) If a complete inspection of the nozzle convex side is necessary, do the steps that follow (Figure 616/Figure 617): NOTE: This inspection is only necessary if you find an indication of damage on the convex side during the initial or complete inspection with the rigid probes. (a) Connect the borescope, COM-2196, to the applicable light source. (b) Put the borescope guide kit, SPL-2198, or borescope guide, SPL-2207, into the borescope port. 1) Use the borescope guide kit, SPL-2198, to do the inspection of the leading edge and the concave surfaces. 2) Use the borescope guide, SPL-2207, to do the inspection of the convex surfaces. (c) Put the fiberscope through the guide tube. (d) Make sure that the borescope is correctly adjusted. (e) Turn the lightsource ON.

G. Borescope Inspection of the HPT Nozzle Guide Vanes

SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-003-F00 (1) Examine the leading edges of the 42 HPT nozzle guide vanes: NOTE: To estimate the size of distress, use the applicable visual aid. To find distress locations relative to specific rows, refer to the applicable figure. NOTE: The airfoil baffle is visible inside the airfoil when missing material occurs. It is sheet metal with cooling holes. (a) Cracks that connect nose holes 1) There is no limit to the number with these conditions: a) The cracks are not longer than 0.3 in. (7.62 mm). b) There is no missing material. 2) Do the inspection again after each 800 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The cracks are not longer than 0.3 in. (7.62 mm). b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.25 in2 (161 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per90°arc (1.57 rad). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL c) Missing material does not extend aft of rows 3 or 9. 3) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The cracks are not more than 1 in. (25.4 mm) in length. b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.25 in2 (161 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per 90°arc (1.57 rad). c) Missing material does not extend aft of rows 3 or 9. 4) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The cracks are longer than 1 in. (25 mm) in length b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.30 in2 (194 mm2 )per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per90°arc (1.57 rad). (b) Other cracks 1) There is no limit to the number with these conditions: a) The cracks are not longer than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm). b) There is no missing material. 2) Do the inspection again after each 800 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The cracks are not longer than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm). b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.25 in2 (161 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per90°arc (1.57 rad). c) Missing material does not extend aft of rows 3 or 9. 3) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The cracks are not more than 1 in. (25.4 mm) in length. b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.25 in2 (161 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per 90°arc (1.57 rad). c) Missing material does not extend aft of rows 3 or 9. 4) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The cracks are longer than 1 in. (25 mm) in length b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.30 in2 (194 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per90°arc (1.57 rad). (c) Burns or spalled areas 1) There is no limit to the number with this condition: a) The area of missing material is not more than 0.15 in2 (97 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per 90°arc (1.57 rad). 2) Do the inspection again after each 800 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.25 in2 (161 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per90°arc (1.57 rad). b) The missing material does not extend aft of rows 3 or 9. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The cracks are longer than 1 in. (25 mm) in length b) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.30 in2 (194 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per90°arc (1.57 rad). (d) Baffle missing material CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Not Permitted 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The area of missing material is equivalent to a rectangle defined by 4 adjacent holes. SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-004-F00 (2) Examine the concave surfaces as follow: (a) Radial cracks that extend from the gill holes 1) Permitted if there is no missing material. 2) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The missing material, cause by cracks, is not more than 0.04 in2 (25.81 mm2 ). b) No more than 4 airfoils for each engine have missing material caused by cracks. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material, caused by cracks, is not more than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ). (b) Other cracks (not in the gill hole rows) 1) Permitted if there is no missing material. 2) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The missing material, cause by cracks, is not more than 0.04 in2 (25.81 mm2 ). b) No more than 4 airfoils for each engine have missing material caused by cracks. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material, caused by cracks, is not more than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ). (c) Burns 1) There is no limit to the quantity with this condition: a) There is no burn-through into the inner cooling passages. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The area which is burned through is not larger than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ) on each vane.. (d) Missing thermal barrier coating (TBC) 1) There is no limit to the quantity of TBC that can be missing. SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-005-F00 (3) Examine the convex surfaces as follows: NOTE: To find distress location relative to specific rows, refer to the applicable figure. (a) Radial or axial cracks 1) Permitted if there is no missing material. 2) If there is missing material, do the inspection again after each 800 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.05 in2 (32.3 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per 90°arc (1.57 rad). b) Cracking does not occur aft of cooling hole row 16. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) If there is missing material, do the inspection again after each 200 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The missing material is not more than 0.15 in2 (97 mm2 ) for each vane. b) There is no baffle missing material. c) After a minimum of four inspections at 200 cycle intervals, if the missing material area has not changed, increase the inspection interval to in or less than every 400 cycles. d) After a minimum of four inspections at 200 cycle intervals, if the missing material area has increased, keep the inspection interval at 200 cycles. 4) The Continue-In-Service limit is 200 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material is not larger than 0.20 in2 (129 mm2 ). 5) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material caused by cracks is not larger than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ). (b) Burns or bulges NOTE: An open area of the cavity caused by bulging is to be interpreted as missing material where the following limits apply. 1) Permitted if there is no missing material. 2) If there is missing material, do the inspection again after each 800 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The total area of missing material is not more than 0.05 in2 (32.3 mm2 ) per vane. Maximum of 4 vanes per 90°arc (1.57 rad). b) Bulging does not occur aft of cooling hole row 16. 3) If there is missing material, do the inspection again after each 200 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The missing material is not more than 0.15 in2 (97 mm2 ) for each vane. b) There is no baffle missing material. c) After a minimum of four inspections at 200 cycle intervals, if the missing material area has not changed, increase the inspection interval to in or less than every 400 cycles. d) After a minimum of four inspections at 200 cycle intervals, if the missing material area has increased, keep the inspection interval at 200 cycles. 4) The Continue-In-Service limit is 200 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material is not larger than 0.20 in2 (129 mm2 ). 5) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material caused by cracks is not larger than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ). (c) Missing thermal barrier coating (TBC) 1) There is no limit to the quantity of TBC that can be missing. SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-006-F00 (4) Examine the trailing edges as follows: (a) Cracks or burns 1) There is no limit to the number of cracks or the amount of burns permitted. (b) Buckled or bowed material CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) There is no limit. (c) Missing material 1) The maximum quantity of missing material from each vane is 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) length in the axial direction. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with these conditions: a) The missing material is not larger than 0.75 in. (19.05 mm) in the axial direction. b) Make sure that the HPT blades are in limits. (HPT Blades Borescope Inspection, TASK 72-00-00-200-807-F00). SUBTASK 72-00-00-211-001-F00 (5) Examine all airfoil surfaces: (a) Craze cracks NOTE: Craze cracks look like many surface cracks that do not have visual width or depth. 1) There is no llimit. (b) Nicks, marks, scratches, and dents 1) There is no limit. (c) Metal splatter 1) There is no limit. SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-007-F00 (6) Examine the inner and outer platforms: (a) Cracks in the parent metal 1) There is no limit. (b) Missing metal or burning of parent metal 1) There is no limit of missing metal or burning of parent metal with no through holes. 2) Do the inspection again after 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The through hole is in or less than 1 in. (25.4 mm) of the leading edge of the inner or outer platform. b) The through hole is not more than 0.06 in2 (38.71 mm2 ). c) No more than 4 segments for each engine have through holes on the inner or outer platform. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) Through hole is not more than 0.12 in2 (77.42 mm2 ). (c) Nicks, scores, scratches and dents on the platform surface 1) There is no limit. (d) Bulges and bowing 1) There is no limit. (e) Cracks in the braze joints of the airfoil-to-platform surfaces 1) There is no limit to the number with this condition: a) Separation of the braze joint is not permitted, unless it was caused by burning. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 72-00-00-420-022-F00 (1) Do these steps to install the borescope plugs: (a) Lubricate the threads of the borescope plugs with pure nickel special compound, D50034 [CP2619] or milk of magnesia compound, D50032 [CP1064] or graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (b) Install the borescope plugs. NOTE: The borescope plugs to the HPT, the LPT stage 1 and combustion case have the same thread size. The stem of the borescope plugs to the HPT or the LPT stage 1 nozzle will be burned away if it is installed in the borescope port for the combustion case (Figure 618). 1) Tighten each borescope plug between 57 in-lb (6.4 N·m) to 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m). 2) Install safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] on each borescope plug. SUBTASK 72-00-00-420-023-F00 (2) If they were removed, do this task: Main Igniter Plug Installation, TASK 74-21-02-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-860-085-F00 (3) If the borescope procedure is complete, do this task: Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition, TASK 72-00-00-200-814-F00.

SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-009-F00 (2) Examine the concave surfaces as follow: (a) Radial cracks that extend from the gill holes. 1) Permitted if there is no missing material. 2) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The missing material, cause by cracks, is not more than 0.04 in2 (25.81 mm2 ). b) No more than 4 airfoils for each engine have missing material caused by cracks. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material caused by cracks is not larger than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ). (b) Other cracks (not in the gill hole rows) 1) Permitted if there is no missing material. 2) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycle interval with these conditions: a) The missing material, cause by cracks, is not more than 0.04 in2 (25.81 mm2 ). b) No more than 4 airfoils for each engine have missing material caused by cracks. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The missing material, caused by cracks, is not more than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ). (c) Burns 1) There is no limit to the quantity with this condition: a) There is no burn-through into the inner cooling passages. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) The area which is burned through is not larger than 0.45 in2 (290 mm2 ) on each vane. (d) Missing thermal barrier coating (TBC) 1) There is no limit to the quantity of TBC that can be missing. 72-00-00-200-807-F00HPT Blades Borescope InspectionPDF p. 173

10. HPT Blades Borescope Inspection (Figure 601, Figure 624, Figure 625, Figure 627, Figure 628, Figure 629, Figure 630, Figure 626) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task provides the instructions on how to examine the HPT blades from the forward and aft sides. (a) Do an inspection of the rotor blades from the aft side with a rigid borescope through borescope port S16 or S17. (b) Do an inspection of the rotor blades from the forward side with a fiberscope through the main igniter plug port S10 or S11.

F. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-048-F00 (1) Do this task: Borescope Inspection Preparation, TASK 72-00-00-200-802-F00. SUBTASK 72-00-00-010-008-F00 (2) Remove the S16 or S17 borescope plug. (a) Identify each BSI plug. (b) Remove the S16 or S17 BSI plugs. (c) Attach an identification tag onto the borescope plugs to make sure that each borescope plug is installed back in the correct borescope port after this procedure. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-050-F00 (3) If it is necessary, remove the main igniter plugs to access the borescope inspection ports S10 and S11 (TASK 74-21-02-000-801-F00). NOTE: The 4:00 o'clock main igniter plug is referred to as the S10 borescope port. The 8:00 o'clock main igniter plug is referred to as the S11 borescope port. NOTE: If you see non-serviceable damage or fragmentation of the igniter plug tip, replace it and make a record of the findings in the borescope findings report. Pay special attention to the HPT Blades for impact damage, especially on the airfoil leading edge and outer/forward convex airfoil regions. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-051-F00 (4) Prepare for the inspection of the HPT blades from the aft side as follows: (a) If you will use the rigid borescope, COM-2195, connect it to light source, SPL-4305. (b) If you will use the rigid borescope, COM-4302, connect it to light source, SPL-4306. (c) If you will use the rigid borescope, COM-4303, connect it to light source, SPL-2197. (d) If you will use the rigid borescope, COM-4304, connect it to light source, SPL-4308. (e) Use the rigid borescope with the yellow band to get a general view. (f) Use the rigid borescope with the green band to view the blade platform. (g) Use the rigid borescope with the blue band to view the blade tip. (h) Put the rigid borescope through the borescope port. (i) Make sure the borescope is correctly adjusted. (j) Turn the light source ON. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-052-F00 (5) Prepare for the inspection of the HPT blades from the forward side as follows: (a) Put the borescope guide kit, SPL-2198, into the S10 or S11 borescope port. (b) Connect the borescope, COM-2196, to the applicable light source. (c) Put the fiberscope through the guide tube. (d) Make sure that the borescope is correctly adjusted. (e) Turn the light source ON. SUBTASK 72-00-00-820-001-F00 (6) Do this task: Turn the N2 Rotor, TASK 72-00-00-980-801-F00.

G. HPT Blades Borescope Inspection

NOTE: Unless otherwise identified, all damage limits for the HPT blades are the same for the different blade configurations. NOTE: One engine configuration has 76 HPT blades. The other engine configuration has 80 HPT blades. NOTE: After long exposure, once protective coatings are consumed, the base metal can start to oxidize. This oxidation is usually black or very dark in color and usually has a rough surface. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-053-F00 (1) Examine the trailing edge of the HPT blades as follows: (a) Cracks that connect to the trailing edge in Area A 1) One crack is permitted if the crack is not more than 0.1 in. (2.5 mm) in length. 2) For a crack that is more than 0.1 in. (2.5 mm) but less than 0.2 in. (5.1 mm) in length, do the inspection again in or less than 500 cycles. 3) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 10 cycles if the crack is more than 0.2 in. (5.1 mm) but less than 0.25 in. (6.4 mm) in length. (b) Missing material, burning, or holes in the tip and Area A 1) There is no limit if the missing material is not more than 0.50 x 0.50 inch (12.7 x 12.7 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles if the missing material is not more than 0.50 inch axially x 0.75 inch radially (12.7 mm axially x 19.1 mm radially). (c) Nicks and dents in Area A 1) Any number and size permitted. (d) Nicks and dents in Area B and C 1) Any number of nicks and dents are permitted that are not more than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) in length. 2) Repeat the inspection after each 400 cycles if the nicks and dents are 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) - 0.12 in. (3.05 mm) in length. 3) Repeat the inspection after each 200 cycles if the nicks and dents are 0.12 in. (3.05 mm) - 0.2 in. (5.08 mm) in length. 4) The Continue-In-Service limit is 40 cycles if the nicks and dents are more than 0.2 in. (5.08 mm), but less than 0.3 in. (7.62 mm) in length. (e) Cracks that connect to the trailing edge in Areas B, C, and root fillet 1) One crack is permitted, with these conditions: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Repeat the inspection after each 400 cycles, if the crack length is less than 0.12 in. (3.05 mm) in length. b) Repeat the inspection after each 200 cycles, if the crack length is 0.12 in. (3.05 mm) - 0.2 in. (5.08 mm) in length. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 40 cycles if the crack is more than 0.2 in. (5.08 mm) but less than 0.3 in. (7.62 mm) in length. (f) Missing Thermal Barrier Coating (TBC) 1) Any amount of TBC can be missing. 2) Oxidation related to the missing TBC is permitted. (g) Plugged air slots in Area A or B 1) One plugged air slot in each blade is permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 50 cycles if not more than two air slots in each blade are plugged. (h) Plugged air slots in Area C 1) Plugged air slots are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 50 cycles if not more than one blade has plugged air slot in Area C. (i) Bent material at the tip 1) Any amount. (j) Distortions or signs of melting 1) Distortions or melting are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles if no more than 10 blades have distortions or melting. SUBTASK 72-00-00-211-005-F00 (2) Examine HPT aft blade retainer outer seal wire protrusion at seal wire ends (Figure 630). (a) HPT aft blade retainer outer seal wire protrusion is permitted if it occurs at no more than two locations. NOTE: For all other, non-seal wire end, protrusions, contact CFM. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-054-F00 (3) Examine the tip of the HPT blade as follows: NOTE: Two blades approximately 90 degrees apart are notched to show the level of blade tip rub. If you cannot see the notches or if the quantity of blades with notches is different, the condition is serviceable if in limits below. The blade rub data can be used to find causes for EGT margin changes and other trends. (a) Damage that exposes the interior cooling passages of the blade between the leading and trailing edges. 1) Exposed interior cooling passages are not permitted unless the condition is acceptable per trailing edge inspection for Missing Material or Leading Edge Inspection for Through wall hole in area A and B. 2) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 10 cycles if the hole is less than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) in diameter (or equivalent area). (b) Radial cracks on the convex side that connect to the blade tip that are more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) distance from the trailing edge. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Permitted, if the radial cracks are not more than 0.15 in. (3.81 mm) in length. 2) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 50 cycles if the radial cracks are not more than 0.35 in. (8.89 mm) in length. (c) Radial cracks on the concave side that connect to the blade tip that are more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) distance away from the trailing edge. 1) Permitted, if the radial cracks are not more than 0.7 in. (17.8 mm) in length. 2) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 50 cycles if the radial cracks are not longer than 1 in. (25.4 mm). (d) Radial cracks on either side of the airfoil that connect to the blade tip, 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) or closer to the trailing edge. 1) Permitted. (e) Bent, curled, or missing material 1) Permitted, if the damage is in the tip area and none of the blade internal cavities are exposed. 2) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 10 cycles if missing material is below the tip shelf and the internal cavity is exposed with a size of less than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) in diameter (or equivalent area). (f) Distortions or signs of melting 1) Distortions or melting are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles if a maximum of 10 blades have distortions or melting. (g) Missing thermal barrier coating (TBC) 1) Any amount of TBC can be missing. 2) Oxidation related to the missing TBC is permitted. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-055-F00 (4) Examine the convex and concave surfaces that are not in the leading edge, trailing edge, or tip as follows: (a) Nicks or dents on the convex and concave surfaces in Areas A, B, and X 1) Permitted, with these conditions: a) In Areas A and X, the damage is not more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in length. b) In Area B, the damage is not more than 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) in length. 2) The Continue-In-Service (C-I-S) limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) Cracks or missing material is not permitted. (b) Nicks or dents on the convex and concave surfaces in Area C 1) Three nicks or dents are permitted with these conditions: a) They are not longer than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm). b) Dents are separated by at least 0.125 in. (3.18 mm). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) Cracks or missing material is not permitted. (c) Cracks in the concave and convex surfaces 1) Any number of cracks within concave surface Area X are permitted. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Do the inspection again after each 400 cycles. b) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles if cracks extend outside of Area X. c) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles if there is missing material in Area X that exposes the interior cooling passages and the hole is less than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) in diameter (or equivalent area). 2) Cracks in other areas are not permitted. (d) Distortions or signs of melting 1) Distortions or melting are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles, with this condition: a) A maximum of 10 blades can have distortions or melting. (e) Missing Thermal Barrier Coating (TBC) 1) Any amount of TBC can be missing. 2) Oxidation related to the missing TBC is permitted. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-056-F00 (5) Examine the leading edge of the HPT rotor blades as follows: (a) Axial and radial cracks in Area A 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) Cracks are not more than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) in length. b) Cracks can not connect more than 2 holes. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles, with this condition: a) Cracks are less than 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) in length. (b) Axial and radial cracks in Area B and C, that include the root fillet, and that do not intersect the nose or gill holes 1) Not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles, with this condition: a) Cracks are less than 0.100 in. (2.54 mm) in length. (c) Axial nose or gill hole cracks in Area B and C 1) Axial nose or concave (row 6) gill hole cracks in Area B and C: a) Not permitted. b) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles, with this condition: <1> Cracks are not more than 0.050 in. (1.27 mm) in length. 2) Convex (row 1) gill hole cracks in Area B and C that extend toward the leading edge (Figure 627): a) Permitted with these conditions: <1> Cracks are not more than 0.050 in. (1.27 mm) in length. <2> Do the inspection again after each 100 cycles. b) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles, with this condition: <1> Cracks are less than 0.100 in. (2.54 mm) in length. 3) Convex (row 1) gill hole cracks in Area B and C in the diffuser (Figure 627): a) Permitted with these conditions: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL <1> Cracks are not more than 0.050 in. (1.27 mm). <2> Do the inspection again after each 100 cycles. b) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles, with this condition: <1> Cracks are less than 0.100 in. (2.54 mm) in length. (d) Radial nose or gill hole cracks in Area B 1) One crack is permitted in Area B, with this condition: a) The crack is not more than 0.030 in. (0.76 mm) in length. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles, with this condition: a) The crack is not more than 0.060 in. (1.52 mm) in length. (e) Radial nose or gill hole cracks in Area C 1) Not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 10 cycles, with this condition: a) Cracks are not longer than 0.030 in. (0.76 mm). (f) Nicks and dents in Area A and B 1) Any number and size permitted. (g) Nicks and dents in Area C, that include the root radius 1) 3 nicks or dents are permitted, with these conditions: a) The nicks and dents are not longer than 0.050 in. (1.27 mm). b) The nicks and dents are separated by at least 0.125 in. (3.18 mm). (h) Dirt or environmental contamination 1) Permitted. (i) Discoloration, Missing Thermal Barrier Coating (TBC) or oxidation NOTE: After long exposure, once protective coatings are consumed, the base metal can start to oxidize. This oxidation is usually black or very dark in color and usually has a rough surface. NOTE: Once there is leading edge oxidation, it is possible that you can see cracks at cooling row #1, (convex gill hole row) holes 2, 3 and 4 up from the platform. Make sure that your borescope orientation provides good visibility of these holes. 1) Discoloration without oxidation is permitted. 2) Any amount of TBC can be missing. 3) Oxidation related to the missing TBC is permitted with reduced inspection interval as follows: a) If you see oxidation with continuous radial length of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) or less, do the inspection again after each 400 cycles. b) If the oxidation has a continuous radial length of more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm), do the inspection again after each 200 cycles. (k) Through wall hole in Area C ALL POST SB 737-CFM56-7B-72-0636 OR POST SB 737-CFM56-7B-72-0886 OR POST SB 737-CFM56-7B-72-0918 1) Permitted with these conditions: a) The hole size is less than 0.070 in. (1.78 mm) diameter, or 0.0038 in2 (2.45 mm2 ) equivalent area. <1> Do the inspection again after each 100 cycles. 11. HPT Shrouds Borescope Inspection

A. General

(1) This task gives the instructions to examine the High Pressure Turbine (HPT) shrouds with a borescope. (2) This inspection of the HPT shrouds is done with a rigid borescope through the borescope ports S16 and S17. You can see the shrouds from the aft side. (3) If you find damage, you must do an inspection of the HPT shrouds from the forward side. This is done with a fiberscope through the main igniter ports (S10 or S11).

F. HPT Shrouds Borescope Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-290-001-F00 (1) Examine the HPT shrouds as follow (Figure 631): (a) Axial cracks 1) Any amount. (b) Circumferential cracks 1) There is no limit to the number of circumferential cracks that do not connect and are no more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) long. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles if the circumferential cracks are more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) long. 3) Circumferential cracks that are connected to axial cracks cannot be more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) long and not less than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) from the shroud edge. 4) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles if the circumferential cracks connected to axial cracks are more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) long or closer than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) from the shroud edge, unless the connected cracks are in or less than the limit for missing material, then missing material can be used. (c) Burning, erosion or chipped/missing TDC exposing the backstrip. 1) Any amount if the shrouds do not drop into the flowpath. (d) Split-line aft corners CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Any amount of circumferential missing or distorted material less than 0.20 in. (5.08 mm) and axial missing or distorted material less than 0.40 in. (10.16 mm) measured from the edge of the shroud. (e) Split-line forward corners 1) Any amount of missing material in or less than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in the axial direction from the leading edge and in or less than 0.080 in. (2.03 mm) in the circumferential direction from the shroud side edges. 2) Continue-In-Service 400 cycles if material loss is more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in the axial direction and 0.080 in. (2.03 mm) in the circumferential direction, if there is no other burn-through on the shroud. NOTE: This C-I-S limit is for a reduced interval, repeat inspection. (f) Split-line other areas 1) Any amount of missing material if area (A) is below 0.013 in2 (8.387 mm2 ) and the distance from the original contour in the circumferential direction (d) is below 0.080 in. (2.03 mm). 2) Continue-In-Service 400 cycles if area (A) is above 0.013 in2 (8.387 mm2 ) or the distance from the original contour in the circumferential direction (d) is above 0.080 in. (2.03 mm), if there is no other burn-through on the shroud. NOTE: This C-I-S limit is for a reduced interval, repeat inspection. 3) Continue-In-Service 200 cycles if area (A) is above 0.013 in2 (8.387 mm2 ) and the distance from the original contour in the circumferential direction (d) is above 0.080 in. (2.03 mm), if there is no other burn-through on the shroud. NOTE: This C-I-S limit is for a reduced interval, repeat inspection. 4) Continue-In-Service limit 25 cycles if area (A) is above 0.013 in2 (8.387 mm2 ) and the distance from the original contour in the circumferential direction (d) is above 0.080 in. (2.03 mm) and other burn-through with the area over 0.001 in2 (0.645 mm2 ) is on the shroud. (g) Rubs and wear 1) All rubs and wear are permitted. (h) Distortion 1) There is no limit if the shroud is not in the flowpath. (i) Burn-through on the rub land (this includes holes through the backstrip) 1) Burn-through is not permitted. 2) Continue-In-Service 75 cycles if burn-through size area on all HPT shrouds is in or less than 0.001 in2 (0.645 mm2 ) < Area < 0.005 in2 (3.226 mm2 ), if the shrouds do not drop into the flowpath. NOTE: This C-I-S limit is for a reduced interval, repeat inspection. 3) Continue-In-Service 25 cycles if burn-through size area on all HPT shrouds is in or less 0.005 in2 (3.226 mm2 ) < Area < 0.015 in2 (9.677 mm2 ), if the shrouds do not drop into the flowpath. NOTE: This C-I-S limit is for a reduced interval, repeat inspection. 4) Continue-In-Service limit 25 cycles if burn-through size area on all HPT shrouds is more than 0.015 in2 (9.677 mm2 ), if the shrouds do not drop into the flowpath. (j) Missing, cracked or displaced shroud axial seals CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Permitted. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-011-F00 (2) When the inspection is complete, remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the light source to OFF, but keep the blower ON until the lamp and case are cool.

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-064-F00 WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU TURN THE FAN ROTOR. MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE IN A STABLE POSITION. ALSO, YOU MUST WEAR HEAVY PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. (1) Examine the LPT blades while you turn the fan rotor in a smooth, stable movement. (a) To examine the airfoil as the blades turn, you must change the depth of the probe in the LPT case. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Turn the probe (azimuth) at the same time you change the depth of the probe. NOTE: This will permit the maximum view for a given turn speed. NOTE: It can be necessary to make more than one complete rotation of the LPT as the length of the blade increases. Also, to fully view the platform and root areas, it can be necessary to put the full probe length into the LPT case. (c) When you examine the leading edges or concave sides of the blades, it is recommended that you reverse the rotation of the rotor so the blades come to the borescope, not away from it. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-065-F00 (2) Examine the LPT blades as follows (Figure 634): NOTE: If you think there is damage, you can look at the damage with the retro-angle viewer. For the blade tip and platforms, you can use the fore-oblique angle viewer. (a) Cracks in these areas 1) Airfoil surface a) Cracks are not permitted. 2) Platform or tip shroud a) Cracks are not permitted. b) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 hours, with this condition: <1> The crack is not more than 50 percent of the chord width. (b) Nicks and dents in the leading and trailing edges 1) There is no limit to the number with these conditions: a) The damage in Area E is less than 0.02 in. (0.51 mm) deep. b) The damage not in Area E is less than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) deep. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 hours. (c) Nicks and dents in the concave and convex surfaces 1) There is no limit to the number with these conditions: a) The damage is less than 0.015 in. (0.38 mm) in depth. b) The damage does not go through to the opposite side. 2) Not more than 5 dents are permitted with this condition: a) The damage goes through less than 0.01 in. (0.25 mm) on the opposite side. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 hours. (d) Large dents or pieces of metal that are missing in Area E 1) Large dents or missing metal are not serviceable. (e) Other areas for large dents or missing pieces 1) There must be less than two damaged areas on the same side of the airfoil. 2) There must be less than two damaged areas on opposite sides of the airfoil. 3) Damage must be separated by 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) radially and 0.2 in. (5.1 mm) from the leading edge and trailing edge. 4) There must be no more than 5 damaged blades in a 90-degree section. 5) No more than 5 percent of the blades can be damaged. 6) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 hours. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) Excess material on airfoil 1) Not more than 0.04 in2 (25.8 mm2 ) surface of cluster, 0.004 in. (0.10 mm) height, 0.02 in. (0.51 mm) diameter for each indication and maximum 5 percent of blade span impacted. (g) Deposit material on blade tip shroud except on lateral faces (hard faces are part of lateral faces) 1) Any amount, the sum of all deposits does not exceed 0.0121 in2 (7.81 mm2 ) per blade tip shroud. (h) Leading edges for distortion caused by over-temperature NOTE: Over-temperature damage is seen as melted areas or parallel grooves in the hard coat of the blade. 1) Distortion of the leading edge is not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 15 cycles or 25 hours with these conditions: a) The distortion is less than 0.8 in. (20.3 mm) on stage 1 blades. b) The distortion is less than 0.08 in. (2.03 mm) on stage 2 and 3 blades. (i) Gaps in the tip shroud interlocks 1) There is no limit, with these conditions: a) The interlocks must not show wear. b) Stage 2 and 3 gaps are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles. (j) Shingled or unlatched tip shrouds 1) Shingled or unlatched tip shrouds are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 hours, with this condition: a) The rotor must turn freely, with a vibration level that is not more than the advisory limit (TASK 71-00-00-800-806-F00). (k) Tip shroud out-of-flush NOTE: If this out-of-flush condition is caused by over welding and if there is no evidence of unusual wear on the mating or hard faces all along the notch and if the interlocks do fit one in another, this condition is serviceable. If different, refer to the criteria that follow. 1) Stage 1 blades a) Not more than 0.0472 in. (1.20 mm), and not more than 0.0413 in. (1.05 mm) on the hard faces. 2) Stage 2 blades a) Not more than 0.0472 in. (1.20 mm), and not more than 0.0354 in. (0.90 mm) on the hard faces. 3) Stage 3 blades a) Not more than 0.0472 in. (1.20 mm), and not more than 0.0433 in. (1.10 mm) on the hard faces. (l) Root platform out-of-flush 1) Stage 1 blades a) Not more than 0.0198 in. (0.50 mm). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Stage 2 and 3 blades a) Not more than 0.0236 in. (0.60 mm). (m) Circumferential looseness 1) There is no limit to circumferential looseness. (o) Flaking on the hardened seal teeth 1) There is no limit to the quantity of flaking. (p) Pitting / corrosion 1) Any amount. (q) Nicks, dents and casting marks on the forward and the rear bottom face of the blade root platform with edges included (but not the retainer lug) (Figure 636). 1) There is no limit to the number with this condition: a) The damage is not more than 0.0098 in. (0.25 mm) in depth. (0.25 mm) in depth. (t) Nicks, dents and casting marks on the inner surface of the blade tip shroud with edges included (but not the fillet radius) (Figure 636). 1) There is no limit to the number with this condition: a) The damage is not more than 0.0098 in. (0.25 mm) in depth. (u) Nicks, dents and casting marks on the front and rear edge of the blade tip shroud with edges included (Figure 636). 1) There is no limit to the number with this condition: a) The damage is not more than 0.0098 in. (0.25 mm) in depth. 72-00-00-200-809-F00Stage 4 LPT Blades Borescope InspectionPDF p. 218

13. Stage 4 LPT Blades Borescope Inspection

A. General

(1) This task provides the instructions on how to do a Borescope Inspection (BSI) of the stage 4 Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) blades. (2) The inspection of the leading edges of the stage 4 LPT blades is done with a rigid borescope through borescope port S20. The inspection of the trailing edges of these blades is done from the aft end of the engine. (3) There are 134 stage 4 blades on the NON-7BE engine. (4) There are 138 stage 4 blades on the 7BE engine.

G. Stage 4 LPT Blades Borescope Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-071-F00 (1) Examine the LPT blades while you turn the fan rotor in a smooth, stable movement. WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU TURN THE FAN ROTOR. MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE IN A STABLE POSITION. ALSO, YOU MUST WEAR HEAVY PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. (a) To examine the airfoil as the blades turn, you must change the depth of the probe in the LPT case. (b) Turn the probe (azimuth) at the same time you change the depth of the probe to permit the maximum view for a given turn speed. NOTE: It can be necessary to make more than one complete rotation of the LPT as the length of the blade increases. Also, to fully view the platform and the root areas, it can be necessary to put the full probe length into the LPT case. (c) When you examine the leading edges or concave sides of the blades, it is recommended that you reverse the rotation of the rotor so the blades come to the borescope, not away from it. SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-072-F00 (2) Examine the blades as follows (Figure 637): (a) Cracks in Area E of the airfoils 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours with these conditions: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) One full airfoil can be missing. b) Engine vibration level is not more than the vibration advisory limit (TASK 71-00-00-800-806-F00). (b) Cracks in the blade platform 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours. (c) Cracks in the tip shrouds 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours with these conditions: a) Engine vibration level is not more than the vibration advisory limit (TASK 71-00-00-800-806-F00). b) There is no limit to the number of tip shrouds and related airfoil tips that can be missing. (d) Nicks and dents on the leading and trailing edges, in Area E 1) There is no limit, with this condition: a) Damage must be less than 0.02 in. (0.5 mm) in depth. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours. (e) Nicks and dents on the leading and trailing edges, not in Area E 1) There is no limit, with this condition: a) Damage must be less than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) in depth. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours. (f) Nicks and dents on the concave or convex airfoil surfaces 1) There is no limit, with these conditions: a) Damage must be less than 0.015 in. (0.38 mm) in depth. b) Damage must not go through to the opposite side. 2) A maximum of 5 dents are permitted, with this condition: a) Damage goes through less than 0.01 in. (0.25 mm) on the opposite side. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours. (g) Nicks, dents and/or scratches (without protrusion) on front and rear edges of tip shroud 1) Any number not more than 0.002 in. (0.05 mm) deep, 0.003 in2 (2 mm2 ) length x width. (h) Nicks, dents and/or scratches (without protrusion) on root rear edge 1) Any number not more than 0.002 in. (0.05 mm) deep, 0.003 in2 (2 mm2 ) length x width. (i) Large dents or pieces of metal that are missing in Area E 1) Large dents or missing metal are not permitted. (j) Other areas for large dents or missing pieces 1) There must be less than two damaged areas on the same side of the airfoil. 2) There must be less than two damaged areas on the opposite sides of the airfoil. 3) Damage must be separated by 0.5 in. (13 mm) radially and 0.2 in. (5 mm) from the leading and trailing edges. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 4) There must be no more than 5 damaged blades in each quadrant. 5) No more than 5 percent of the blades can be damaged. 6) The Continue-In-Service limit is 5 cycles or 10 flight hours with this condition: a) Engine vibration level is not more than the vibration advisory limit (TASK 71-00-00-800-806-F00). (k) Excess material on airfoil 1) Not more than 0.04 in2 (25.8 mm2 ) surface of cluster, 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) height, 0.02 in. (0.5 mm) diameter for each indication and maximum 5 percent of blade span impacted. (l) Deposit material on blade tip shroud except on lateral faces (hard faces are part of lateral faces) 1) Any amount, the sum of all deposits does not exceed 0.0121 in2 (7.81 mm2 ) per blade tip shroud. (m) Leading edges for distortion caused by over-temperature NOTE: Overtemperature damage is seen as melted areas or parallel grooves in the hard coat of the blade. 1) Distortion of the leading edge is not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 15 cycles or 25 flight hours with this condition: a) The distortion is less than 0.08 in. (2 mm). (n) Tip shroud interlock gaps (Figure 638) 1) Gaps are not permitted. a) Do this task: Stage 4 LPT Blades Axial Preload Check, TASK 72-00-00-200-810-F00. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles or 50 flight hours. (o) Shingled or unlatched tip shrouds 1) Shingled or unlatched tip shrouds are not permitted. a) Do the procedure to put the shingled/unlatched blades back to their original position. b) If the blade tip shrouds are successfully put back in the correct position, do a check of the blade tip shrouds. 2) For shingled blades, the Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles or 50 flight hours, with these conditions: a) The rotor must turn freely. b) Engine vibration level is not more than the vibration advisory limit (TASK 71-00-00-800-806-F00). 3) For unlatched blades, the Continue-In-Service limit is 100 cycles or 200 flight hours, with these conditions: a) The rotor must turn freely. b) Engine vibration level is not more than the vibration advisory limit (TASK 71-00-00-800-806-F00). (p) Tip shroud interlock wear NOTE: Maximum interlock wear usually occurs at 2 to 6 locations, equally spaced. Measurement should be done at these locations. E. Stage 4 LPT Blades Axial Preload Check

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-077-F00 (1) Do the axial preload check as follows: NOTE: You must separate two tip shrouds in each quadrant to do the check for axial preload. (a) In a quadrant, separate the two tip shrouds by hand. Do not unlatch the tip shroud interlocks. 1) With your hands, push one blade as you pull the other. NOTE: This will separate the tip shrouds. (b) Release the blades, and do a check for a gap between the tip shroud interlocks. 1) Gaps between the tip shroud interlocks are not permitted. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles or 50 flight hours.

F. Stage 1 LPT Nozzle Guide Vanes Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-082-F00 (1) Examine the nozzle guide vanes as follows: NOTE: Use the rigid borescope or flexible borescope to do this inspection. If you use the rigid borescope, this inspection is limited to what you can see on the two airfoils of the nozzle segments. (a) Axial cracks on the leading and trailing edges. 1) If a rigid borescope is used, examine the axial cracks on the leading and trailing edges as follows: a) Cracks that are less than 1/3 of the chord width (0.6 in. (15.24 mm) in length) on the 2 airfoils of the nozzle segment are permitted. b) One crack is permitted per airfoil if the length is more than 1/3 of the chord width (0.6 in. (15.24 mm)) but less than 1/2 of the chord width (1.0 in. (25.4 mm)). c) A continue-in-service limit of 100 cycles is permitted for axial cracks over the above limits as follows: <1> There is only one crack on each airfoil. <2> There is no missing material on the airfoil. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL <3> The crack length is more than 1/2 of the chord width (1.0 in. (25.4 mm)) in length but less than 2/3 of the chord width (1.2 in. (30 mm)). 2) If a 360° flexible borescope is used, examine for axial cracks as follows: NOTE: Inspection must be followed step by step. a) Cracks that are less than 1/3 of the chord width (0.6 in. (15.24 mm) in length) on the airfoils of the nozzle segments are permitted. b) Eight cracks are permitted per set of nozzles with these conditions: <1> The length is more than 1/3 of the chord width (0.6 in. (15.24 mm)) but less than 3/4 of the chord width (1.35 in. (34.3 mm)). <2> There are not more than two cracks per segment and one crack per airfoil. <3> There is no missing material. c) A continue-in-service limit of 1600 cycles is permitted for axial cracks over the above limits as follows: <1> There is no full crack. <2> There are not more than two cracks per segment and one crack per airfoil. <3> There is no missing material. <4> After completion of the cycles permitted as continue-in-service, a new 360° flexible borescope inspection of the complete set of nozzles must be performed for continued operations. d) Use the continue-in-service limits in the Table 1 to Table 4 (Figure 643) below with these conditions: NOTE: An axial crack is considered as full axial crack if it runs from leading edge to trailing edge on the two concave and convex sides. <1> There are a maximum of two full cracks (leading edge to trailing edge) per LPT nozzle segment. <2> There is a maximum of one full crack (leading edge to trailing edge) per airfoil added to any amount of non-full cracks. <3> The missing material in each hole is not more than 0.039 in2 (25 mm2 ). <4> There are no more than two holes per segment and no more than one hole per airfoil. <5> Radial cracks: Each airfoil can only have one crack that is less than 1/2 of the chord width in length (1.0 in. (25.4 mm)). <6> After completion of the cycles permitted as continue-in-service, a new 360° flexible borescope inspection of the complete set of nozzles must be performed for continued operations. (b) Burns 1) Permitted with this condition: a) Discoloration with no missing material. 2) A continue-in-service limit of 25 cycles is permitted with this condition: a) Melted or missing material more than 0.102 sq. inch (66 sq. mm) for each engine set of nozzles. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Nicks, marks, scratches or dents in the concave/convex surfaces and inner and outer platforms. 1) Permitted. (d) Cracks in the inner and outer platforms. 1) Two cracks are permitted for each segment, with these conditions: a) The cracks are less than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) in length. b) The metal does not go into the gaspath. 2) The continue-in-service limit is 3 cycles, with this condition: a) The cracks are less than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) in length. F. Stage 2-4 LPT Nozzle Guide Vanes Inspection

SUBTASK 72-00-00-210-089-F00 (1) Examine the nozzle guide vanes as follows: NOTE: You can use rigid borescope or flexible borescope to do this Inspection. NOTE: If you use the rigid borescope, this inspection is limited to what you can see. (a) Cracks in the leading and trailing edges for stages 2 through 4: NOTE: LPT Stage 2 and 4 nozzles have six airfoils for each segment. LPT Stage 3 nozzles have seven airfoils for each segment. 1) There is no limit, with these conditions: a) Any number of cracks (leading or trailing edges) if cracks are less than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) in length (1/3 of the chord width). b) One crack maximum for each nozzle segment that is 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) (1/3 of the chord width) to 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) in length (2/3 of the chord width). 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 200 cycles with these conditions: a) Three cracks maximum for each nozzle segment if cracks are more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) (1/3 of the chord width) and less than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) (2/3 of the chord width) if the adjacent nozzle segments have no more than two cracks more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) (1/3 of the chord width) and less than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) (2/3 of the chord width). b) One crack maximum for each nozzle segment that is more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) (2/3 of the chord width) including open airfoil. 3) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles, with this condition: a) One full chord crack on two airfoils for each segment if the adjacent nozzle segments have no more than one airfoil with a full chord crack. (b) Burns 1) There is no limit, with this condition: a) Discoloration with no missing material. 2) The Continue-In-Service limit is 25 cycles with this condition: a) Missing material or melted. (c) Corrosion/Pitting 1) Any amount, if there is no missing material. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Oxidation for stage 3 1) Any amount, if there is no missing material. SUBTASK 72-00-00-080-007-F00 (2) When the inspection is complete, remove the borescope equipment. (a) Turn the light source to OFF, but keep the blower ON until the lamp and case are cool.

72-00-00-100-801-F00Engine Cleaning SpecificationsPDF p. 269

2. Engine Cleaning Specifications

A. General

CAUTION DO NOT USE METHANOL SOLVENTS TO CLEAN THE ENGINE. DAMAGE TO TITANIUM PARTS CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT CLEAN AN ENGINE AFTER EXPOSURE TO DRY CHEMICAL FIRE EXTINGUISHING AGENTS. DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT CLEAN THE ENGINE UNLESS THE EGT IS BELOW 150°F (66°C). IF NOT, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT COULD OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT CLEAN AN ENGINE IF THE OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS BELOW 14°F (-10°C). THIS CAN CAUSE ICE IN THE ENGINE AND POSSIBLE DAMAGE. CAUTION DO NOT USE BLEACH, DISINFECTANT OR SANITIZER ON ENGINE HARDWARE OR COMPONENTS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (1) You can clean the engine with pure water only, or with a solution of gas path cleaner, B01024 [CP5060] (TASK 72-00-00-100-803-F00 or TASK 72-00-00-100-804-F00). (a) For EGT margin recovery, it is recommended to do the engine gas- path water cleaning with pure water only (without cleaning agent) (TASK 72-00-00-100-803-F00). Pure water (without cleaning agent) is effective in most situations depending on the engine's operating environment and the engine gas-path cleaning program implemented by the Operator. (b) An engine gas-path water cleaning with detergent provides the most effective method to clean the engine compressors (TASK 72-00-00-100-804-F00). For the use of detergent, it is necessary to follow strict application of the engine rinsing and bleed system cycling per the procedures to prevent fumes in the cabin when the airplane goes back into service. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) It may be necessary to clean the engine more than one time if initial results are not satisfactory. 2) Considerations should be given to do an engine gas-path cleaning with detergent for any of these following conditions: a) Organic debris or oil deposits are observed on compressor airfoils b) The engine has less than 10°C EGT margin left. (2) If the air temperature is below 40°F (4°C), use alcohol, B00676 [CP1041], as the anti-freeze agent with the water rinse or the cleaner solution.

C. Engine Cleaning Specifications

SUBTASK 72-00-00-100-001-F00 (1) Water. (a) Water properties. 1) Use water with less than 500 ppm total solids, less than 25 ppm sodium plus potassium (Na + K), and a PH of 6.0 - 8.0. a) Potable water is usually sufficient. (b) Water flow. CAUTION DO NOT USE A WATER FLOW OF MORE THAN 6 GPM (23 L/MIN). IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. 1) A water flow of 5 gpm (19 l/min) - 6 gpm (23 l/min) is necessary at a temperature of more than 40°F (4°C). NOTE: If the water cart does not have a flowmeter, to calculate the flow rate use a container of known quantity and a stop watch. a) For the best results, increase the temperature of the water to 150°F (66°C) - 200°F (93°C) to wash and clean the gas path. SUBTASK 72-00-00-100-007-F00 (2) Anti-freeze (if it is necessary). (a) If the air temperature is below 40°F (4°C), prepare the anti-freeze mixture for the water wash or the cleaning solution. WARNING USE RUBBER GLOVES AND EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU HANDLE LIQUID DETERGENT. LIQUID DETERGENT AND ANTI￾FREEZE SOLVENT HAVE LOW FLASHPOINTS. KEEP AWAY FROM HEAT AND AN OPEN FLAME. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT COULD OCCUR. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (WARNING PRECEDES) CAUTION USE ONLY ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL AS AN ANTI-FREEZE MIXTURE. ALL OTHER ALCOHOL MIXTURES ARE NOT PERMITTED AND CAN CAUSE CORROSION OF THE TITANIUM PARTS OF THE ENGINE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 1) For air temperatures of 23°F (-5°C) - 40°F (4°C), mix a solution of 25 percent alcohol, B00676 [CP1041], with 75 percent water. 2) For air temperatures of 14°F (-10°C) - 23°F (-5°C), mix a solution of 35 percent alcohol, B00676 [CP1041], with 65 percent water. 3) For air temperatures below 14°F (-10°C), do not clean an engine. SUBTASK 72-00-00-100-006-F00 (3) Cleaning solutions (if it is necessary). (a) Prepare the cleaning solution mixture. WARNING USE RUBBER GLOVES AND EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU HANDLE LIQUID DETERGENT. LIQUID DETERGENT AND ANTI￾FREEZE SOLVENT HAVE LOW FLASHPOINTS. KEEP AWAY FROM HEAT AND AN OPEN FLAME. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT COULD OCCUR. 1) Mix a solution in volume ratio of 20 - 25 percent of gas path cleaner, B01024 [CP5060], with 75 - 80 percent of water.

F. Clean The Fan Blades

SUBTASK 72-00-00-100-002-F00 (1) Do these steps to clean the fan blades: WARNING MAKE SURE TO WEAR GLOVES WHEN YOU HANDLE THE FAN BLADES. IF YOU DO NOT WEAR GLOVES, PERSONAL INJURY CAN OCCUR. (a) Move each fan blade you are to clean to the 6:00 o'clock position. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT LET THE SOLUTION SPRAY INTO THE GASPATH. 72-00-00-100-803-F00Clean the Engine Gas-Path with Pure WaterPDF p. 274

4. Clean the Engine Gas-Path with Pure Water

A. General

(1) For Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT) margin recovery, it is recommended to clean the engine gas-path with pure water only. (2) It is not recommended to use a cleaning agent in the water for EGT margin recovery. NOTE: It is only recommended to clean the engine gas-path with a cleaning agent when organic debris or oil deposits are present or the remaining EGT margin is less than 50°F (10°C).

72-00-00-100-804-F00Clean the Engine Gas-Path with Cleaning SolutionPDF p. 287

5. Clean the Engine Gas-Path with Cleaning Solution

A. General

(1) For Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT) margin recovery, it is recommended to clean the engine gas-path with pure water only. (2) It is recommended that you use a cleaning agent only when organic debris or oil deposits are present. (3) It is recommended that you do the fan blade cleaning procedure and gas path cleaning procedure with cleaning agent at the same time.
