D. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 72-23-07-040-001-F00 WARNING DO THESE SPECIFIED TASKS IN THE CORRECT SEQUENCE BEFORE YOU OPEN THE THRUST REVERSERS: RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE, DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURES FOR THE LEADING EDGE AND THE THRUST REVERSER (FOR GROUND MAINTENANCE), AND OPEN THE FAN COWL PANELS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE ABOVE SEQUENCE, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-23-07-100-001-F00 (2) Clean dirt or unwanted material from the panels.

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 72-23-07-210-002-F00 (1) If you find damage that is not in the limits, replace the panels, unless you are given other instructions. These are the tasks: Fan Duct Panel Removal, TASK 72-23-07-000-801-F00, CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL Fan Duct Panel Installation, TASK 72-23-07-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-23-07-210-003-F00 (2) Examine the titanium strut panels for damage: (a) A maximum service extension of 100 cycles is permitted with one missing fan duct panel. 1) Do a check every 10 cycles that the Variable Bleed Valve (VBV) cavity is free of foreign objects. 2) Remove the panel and all the attaching screws. 3) Make sure that all other panels are correctly tightened. (b) Nicks, dents, and scratches 1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, dents, and scratches which are permitted with this condition: a) Not more than 0.012 in. (0.3 mm) in depth. (c) Missing material is not permitted (d) ENGINES PRE-CFMI-SB 72-202; Bonded seals 1) Missing or damaged seals are permitted. a) There is no limit to the amount of missing or damaged seals. 2) Unbonded seal is permitted provided you cut and remove the pieces of unbonded seal. a) There is no limit to the amount of unbonded seal. (e) Loose captive bolts 1) Not permitted. a) Tighten the bolts. SUBTASK 72-23-07-210-004-F00 (3) Examine the LPTACC strut panel for damage: (a) Punctures or tears 1) Not serviceable. (b) Impact, marks, and scratches 1) There is no limit to the number of impact, marks, and scratches which are permitted with this condition: a) Not more than 0.020 in. (0.5 mm) in depth. (c) ENGINES PRE-CFMI-SB 72-202; Bonded seal 1) Missing or damaged seal is permitted. a) There is no limit to the amount of missing or damaged seal. 2) Unbonded seal is permitted provided you cut and remove the pieces of unbonded seal. a) There is no limit to the amount of unbonded seal. (d) VBV cascade vanes 1) Cracks a) Not serviceable. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Looseness is not permitted. (e) LPTACC Scoop 1) Cracks a) Not serviceable. 2) Impact, marks, or scratches a) There is no limit to the number of impact, marks, or scratches which are permitted with these conditions: b) Not more than 0.01 in. (0.25 mm) in depth c) Not more than 0.59 in. (15 mm) in length d) Not less than 0.39 in. (10 mm) between two defects. 3) Looseness of the LPTACC scoop is not permitted. 4) Missing or loose bolts are not permitted. a) Replace or tighten the bolts.

WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. AFTER FIVE MINUTES WHEN THE APU STOPS, LET THE OIL SYSTEM PRESSURE GO TO ZERO. PUT ON PROTECTIVE CLOTHES, GOGGLES AND EQUIPMENT, OR LET THE APU BECOME COOL. IF YOU REMOVE THE OIL FILLER CAP WITH THE OIL SYSTEM PRESSURIZED, A SPRAY OF HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU. CAUTION DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER. SUBTASK 72-23-08-020-001-F00 (1) Disconnection of the forward sump (oil scavenge) tube [2] from the oil return tube [1]: (a) Remove the bolts [3]. (b) Disconnect the forward sump (oil scavenge) tube [2] from the oil return tube [1]. (c) Remove and examine the gasket [4] (Seals (Preformed Packings and O-Rings) and Gaskets, TASK 70-30-01-910-802-F00). 1) Discard the gasket [4], if it is in unsatisfactory condition. 2) Keep the gasket [4] for the subsequent installation, if it is in good condition. SUBTASK 72-23-08-020-002-F00 (2) Remove the bolts [5] which attach the oil return tube [1] and the bracket assembly [6] to the fan frame shroud. SUBTASK 72-23-08-020-003-F00 (3) Remove the oil return tube [1]. NOTE: It could be necessary to lift the airplane to get sufficient clearance between the engine and the ground. To get this clearance, extend the main and nose landing gear shock struts with dry air or nitrogen (TASK 12-15-31-610-802). SUBTASK 72-23-08-020-004-F00 (4) Remove and discard the o-rings [7].

SUBTASK 72-24-01-040-001-F00 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE SUBTASK 72-24-01-040-002-F00 (2) Make sure that the start levers are in the CUTOFF position. SUBTASK 72-24-01-040-004-F00 (3) Install a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the applicable start switch. SUBTASK 72-24-01-010-001-F00 WARNING OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE PROCEDURE TO OPEN THE THRUST REVERSERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (4) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-24-01-480-001-F00 CAUTION PUT THE PROTECTIVE MAT IN THE INLET COWL. THIS WILL PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE INLET COWL OR ENGINE BY TOOLS, PARTS, OR UNWANTED MATERIALS THAT FALL ON THE INLET COWL SURFACE. (5) Install a protective mat, STD-585, in the inlet cowl.

F. Examine the Shroud of the Fan Inlet Case

SUBTASK 72-24-01-210-002-F00 (1) Remove the high metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-24-01-210-003-F00 (2) Do a local swab etching of the blended area (TASK 70-10-11-800-801-F00). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-24-01-210-004-F00 (3) Do a Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI) of the suspected areas (TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-24-01-210-001-F00 (4) Do a check of the fan inlet case for damage (Figure 601, Figure 602, Figure 603, or Figure 604): (a) Cracks (except for holes 84/85 and 103/104 on B1 flange). 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) Missing material is not permitted. 3) Cracked holes 84/85 on B1 flange, refer to SB 72-0780. 4) Cracked holes 103/104 on B1 flange at location of fire detector bracket P/N 332A2920-XXX, refer to SB 72-0580 (Figure 603). a) A Continue-In-Service (CIS) limit of 10 cycles is permitted, provided the following: <1> The CIS limit is permissible only if one of the two lugs used at bracket P/N 332A2920-XXX is cracked or broken. Confirm by General Visual Inspection (GVI) of B1 flange approximately 11:30 o'clock Aft Looking Forward. <2> The CIS limit is permissible only if the operational test for the fire and overheat detection is accomplished without fault (TASK 26-10-00-710-801). <3> If both conditions are not met, proceed with B1 flange repair without deferral. (b) Erosion on Areas 4, 5 and 6 (Figure 603). 1) Do this task: Fan Inlet Case Erosion Inspection, TASK 72-24-01-270-801-F00. ALL POST SB 737-CFM56-7B-72-0553 2) Missing anti-erosion paint: Any amount. ALL (c) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the fan inlet case (Figure 603). NOTE: The trinomial inspection is the quickest method but gives you less margin in terms of limits. The template inspection takes more time but gives larger limits. NOTE: For areas 4, 5 and 6 post CFM56-7B-SB 72-0553, the following inspections are applicable after removal of a 13.937 in. (354 mm) radius anti-erosion paint around the nick, dent or scratch to check if other ones are present below anti-erosion paint. NOTE: One of the three following inspections shall be used for inspection of nicks, dents and scratches of the inner and outer skin of the fan inlet case. NOTE: Inspection of FWD and AFT zones (FWD zone: Areas 1 and 2, AFT zone: Areas 4, 5, and 6) shall be carried using only one inspection method. Each zone can be controlled with a different method. Area 3 can only be inspected per Inspection 2. • Inspection 1 is the simplest inspection method that does not take into account indications with a depth of 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) or less (only applicable for Areas 1 and 2). For Post SB 72–0931 parts, we recommend that you use Inspection 2 which is more permissive. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL • Inspection 2 is the most common trinomial inspection method and takes into account all nicks, dents and scratches, whatever their depth (applicable for all Areas). • Inspection 3 is the most efficient inspection method and provides the biggest range of indication allowance (only applicable for Areas 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6). NOTE: Among Inspections 1, 2 and 3, if one inspection or more pass, the fan inlet case is serviceable. 1) Alternative procedure available - Simplified Criteria for Areas 1 and 2 only. NOTE: Indications with a depth of 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) or less are not taken into account and are considered as acceptable whatever the distance with other indications. (22.86 mm)] is in Area 1 at 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) from Area 2, then no indication is permitted in Areas 1 and 2 if the distance is less than 3.0 in. (76.2 mm). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Nicks, dents and scratches on outer skin flange radii A1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, and B6 (Figure 604). 1) No indication is permitted. 2) If indication is found, do this task: Repair of the Radii of Flanges A1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, and B6 on the Containment Case by Blending, TASK 72-24-01-300-809-F00. (e) Elongated holes on the fan inlet case flanges (Figure 602): 1) There is no limit to the number of elongated holes for a single or double bracket configuration which are permitted with these conditions: a) Not more than 0.279 in. (7.1 mm) in width and not more than 0.31 in. (7.9 mm) in length (unidirectional wear) and not more than 0.019 in. (0.5 mm) in depth. b) Re-install the applicable bracket with the new bolts, washers, and nuts following an initial installation procedure. 2) There is no limit to the number of elongated holes with a double bracket (bracket on each side of the flange) that are permitted with these conditions: a) Not more than 0.279 in. (7.1 mm) in width and not more than 0.433 in. (11.0 mm) in length (unidirectional wear) and not more than 0.039 in. (1.0 mm) in depth. b) Re-install the applicable new bracket with the new bolts, washers, and nuts following an initial installation procedure. c) A CIS limit of 250 cycles is permitted to replace the bracket. (f) Riveted nuts holes and gang channel nut holes: 1) Corrosion/Fretting a) Not serviceable. b) To repair with these limits, do these steps: <1> Not more than 0.3326 in. (8.45 mm) diameter centered on the hole, do this task: Removal of the Corrosion in the Self-Locking Nuts Holes by Drilling, TASK 72-24-01-300-802-F00. <2> Not more than 0.4448 in. (11.30 mm) diameter centered on the hole, do this task: Removal of the Corrosion in the Self-Locking Nuts Holes by Bushing Installation, TASK 72-24-01-300-803-F00. <3> Within the limit of the repair, do this task: Removal of Corrosion/Fretting Under and Around Gang Channel Nuts by Blending, TASK 72-24-01-300-804-F01. SUBTASK 72-24-01-390-001-F00 (5) Do a spot touch-up of the oxide film coating on the inspected areas (TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00).

G. Examine the Flanges of the Fan Inlet Case

SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-003-F00 (1) Remove the sharp edges and the high metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (a) Do not increase the depth of the finding. SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-004-F00 (2) Do a local swab etching of the blended area (TASK 70-10-11-800-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-005-F00 (3) Do a FPI (Water Washable) of the suspected areas (TASK 70-40-01-910-801-F00). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-006-F00 (4) Do a check of the fan inlet case flanges for indications. (a) Record the position of a mark "R" if it was found on Area A or Area E of the A1 flange. 1) If it is necessary to remove mark "R" during hand blending, mark "R" at the same position after hand blending is completed (TASK 72-24-01-300-810-F00). NOTE: Without mark “R” the inlet cannot be assembled. (b) Examine the A1 flange (Figure 605). NOTE: If a finding is included in many areas, the most restrictive criterion of the concerned areas should be used. NOTE: The hand blending ratio must be minimum 10 between the depth and length for areas E and F. No blending ration is required for areas A, B, C, and D. 1) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area A (top of the inlet cowl lugs including the edge between Area A and Area E). a) All indications are permitted if not more than 0.2125 in. (5.3975 mm) in axial length, not more than 0.157 in. (3.988 mm) in radial length, and not more than 0.787 in. (19.990 mm) in circumferential length. 2) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area B (radius of the inlet cowl lugs). a) All indications are permitted if not more than 0.2125 in. (5.3975 mm) in axial length, not more than 0.2125 in. (5.3975 mm) in radial length, and not more than 0.787 in. (19.990 mm) in circumferential length. 3) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area C (inner edge of the forward face). a) All indications are permitted if not more than 0.0787 in. (1.9990 mm) in axial length, not more than 0.0787 in. (1.9990 mm) in radial length, and not more than 0.787 in. (19.990 mm) in circumferential length. 4) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area D (front face and rear face, except Area G and equipment lugs). a) All indications are permitted if less than 0.00197 in. (0.0500 mm) in depth or if not more than 0.276 in. (7.0104 mm) in length, not more than 0.0394 in. (1.001 mm) in depth, and with a minimum distance between two findings of 0.984 in. (24.994 mm). 5) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area E (front, top, and rear face of equipment lugs). a) For holes 61 to 66: <1> No indication is permitted. b) For all other holes: <1> No indication is permitted in a circle of diameter 0.512 in. (13.005 mm) around the hole. <2> All indications are permitted if S<0.0124 in2 (8.0000 mm2 ) with S = axial length x radial length if indication is on the edge, S = depth x length if indication is on the face, and if circumferential length is not more than 1.181 in. (29.997 mm). 6) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area F. a) All indications are permitted if S < 0.0093 in2 (6.0000 mm2 ) with S = axial length x radial length, and if circumferential length is not more than 1.575 in. (40.005 mm). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 7) Nicks, dents, and scratches on Area G (0.984 in. (25.0 mm) diameter centered on fan inlet cowl holes). a) No indication is permitted. b) If indication is found, do this task: Repair of Flange A1 Area G by Blending, TASK 72-24-01-300-808-F00. 8) Corrosion, pitting, elongation for fan inlet cowl bolt holes. a) No indication is permitted. b) If hole diameter is less than 0.5303 in. (13.47 mm), do this task: Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Drilling, TASK 72-24-01-300-807-F00 or Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Drilling or by Bushing with Fan Case Repair Kit, TASK 72-24-01-300-810-F00. NOTE: Hole 1 is not applicable to be repaired with fan case repair kit, SPL-23266 (Figure 605). c) If indication is within dimensional inspection limits of Dia AS and/or Dia AT and if depth in the aft face is less than 0.079 in. (2.0 mm), do this task: Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Bushing, TASK 72-24-01-300-806-F00 or Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Drilling or by Bushing with Fan Case Repair Kit, TASK 72-24-01-300-810-F00. NOTE: Hole 1 is not applicable to be repaired with fan case repair kit, SPL-23266 (Figure 605). 9) Corrosion, pitting, elongation for centering pin holes. a) No indication is permitted. b) If hole diameter is less than 0.2803 in. (7.12 mm), do this task: Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Drilling, TASK 72-24-01-300-807-F00 or Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Drilling or by Bushing with Fan Case Repair Kit, TASK 72-24-01-300-810-F00. c) If indication is within dimensional inspection limits of Dia AU and/or Dia AV and if depth on the forward face is less than 0.079 in. (2.0 mm), do this task: Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Bushing, TASK 72-24-01-300-806-F00 or Reconditioning of the Attachment Holes on Flange A1 by Drilling or by Bushing with Fan Case Repair Kit, TASK 72-24-01-300-810-F00. 10) Corrosion, pitting, elongation for equipment holes. a) No indication is permitted. 72-24-01-220-801-F00Fan Inlet Case Template InspectionPDF p. 881

4. Fan Inlet Case Template Inspection

A. General

(1) This task gives instructions to perform a template inspection of the containment case. (2) The template inspection is an alternative procedure to examine nicks, dents, and scratches for Areas 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6. (3) This task finds the most impacted area. (a) This area is delimited by a template. (b) The control area takes into account indications of the inner and outer skins. (c) Examine all combinations and turn the mask in many directions. 1) A combination is given by the depth and length of the indications on the inner and outer skins in the template. (d) Measure the length and depth of each indication. 1) Record these parameters in a table to find the severity of each indication. (e) The sum of the severities gives the serviceable limits of the containment case.

F. Fan Inlet Case Template Inspection

SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-001-F00 (1) Remove the high metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-007-F00 (2) Do a local swab etching before you examine the fan inlet case by Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI) (TASK 70-10-11-800-801-F00). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-008-F00 (3) Do a FPI of the suspected areas (TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-009-F00 (4) Examine the fan inlet case for nicks, dents, and scratches (Figure 615). (a) The template inspection is a 360-degree inspection. 1) Consider Areas 1 and 2, and Areas 4, 5, and 6 as one area to put the template on it. 2) Don't take into account the border between Areas 1 and 2, and Areas 4, 5, and 6. (b) All the possible combinations must be considered (Figure 610 and Figure 611). 1) The combination with the worst severity is the one that gives the serviceability status of the fan containment case. SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-002-F00 (5) Identify all the indications (nicks, dents, scratches) on the inner and outer skins that are more than 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) in depth. SUBTASK 72-24-01-211-001-F00 (6) Identify the worst combination and try all the possible template positions (Figure 610 and Figure 611). SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-001-F00 (7) For each combination, record the depth and length of the indications that are more than 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) in depth in the table (Figure 616). (a) If an indication is not fully in the template, include the full length of the indication even if that part extends out of the template. SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-004-F00 (8) For Areas 1 and 2 only, record the minimum distance from A1 flange and the maximum distance from A1 flange to use the multiplying factor to decrease the severity of each indication (Figure 612, Figure 613, and Figure 614). (a) Make sure that for Areas 1 and 2 there are less than 10 indications with a depth of 0.004 in. (0.102 mm) or less in the template. NOTE: If an indication cannot be measured because it is too small, do not take it into account. (b) If such a combination is possible, this inspection procedure cannot be used. SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-002-F00 (9) Define the severity of each indication with the example chart (Figure 617). (a) Go out to the indication depth up to the length indication curve (Step A, Figure 617). (b) Come back to the severity axis (Step B, Figure 617). (c) Use the applicable chart to determine each severity (Figure 619 and Figure 620). (d) Record the severity value in the table (Figure 614). 1) Use the table for combination 1 as an example (Figure 616). (e) Find the multiplying factor for each indication for Areas 1 and 2 only, as follows (Figure 613): 1) To find the multiplying factor for the minimum distance from the A1 flange and maximum distance from the A1 flange, do these steps: a) Project the distance from the A1 flange on the horizontal axis to the curve. b) Project the distance from A1 flange on the curve to the vertical axis. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL c) Get value for the minimum distance from A1 flange. d) Get value for the maximum distance from A1 flange. e) Take into account only the highest multiplying factor for each indication. 2) Find the special severity of each indication on Areas 1 and 2. a) Multiply the multiplying factor by the severity value. 3) Record this specific severity for Areas 1 and 2. 4) Do these steps for each combination. (f) If it is necessary, use the following steps as an example of calculation (Figure 618): 1) Indications 1 and 2 in Figure 612 are located in the same combination and are as follows: • Indication number 1: 24% • Indication number 2: 60% • Indication number 3: 20%. 2) Sum of these severities without the special severities is 104% > 100%. a) The indications without the special severities isn't serviceable. 3) Take into account the distance of each indication from the A1 flange (Figure 612 and Figure 613). 4) Values for indications are, as follows: • Indication number 1: minimum distance is 1.4 in. (36 mm) and maximum distance is 1.73 in. (44 mm) • Indication number 2: minimum distance is 3.46 in. (88 mm) and maximum distance is 3.77 in. (96 mm) • Indication number 3: minimum distance is 2.2 in. (56 mm) and maximum distance is 2.36 in. (60 mm). 5) Make a plot of these values on the multiplying factor curve (Figure 613). 6) Multiply the severities that you calculated before the multiplying factor: • Indication number 1: MAX [0.36 and 0.42] => 0.42 • Indication number 2: MAX [0.60 and 0.72] => 0.72 • Indication number 3: MAX [0.78 and 0.98] => 0.98. 7) The corrected severities are, as follows: • Indication number 1: 24% x 0.42 = 10.08% • Indication number 2: 60% x 0.72 = 43.20% • Indication number 3: 20% x 0.98 = 19.60%. 8) The sum of the special severities is 72.88%. 9) The indications are permitted with the correct severities. SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-003-F00 (10) For addition of all the severities, do these steps: (a) For a given combination add the special severities for the indications on Areas 1 and 2, and the severities for indications on Areas 4, 5, and 6. 1) Record the sum in the table (Figure 614). 2) The most impacted area is delimited by the template (Figure 621). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) For Areas 1 and 2: <1> Dimension A - 2.79 in. (70.87 mm) <2> Dimension B - 0.79 in. (20.07 mm). b) For Areas 4, 5, and 6: <1> Dimension A - 9.84 in. (249.94 mm) <2> Dimension B - 9.84 in. (249.94 mm). (b) If the combination of all the severities is less than or equal to 100 percent, the indications on the fan case are serviceable. SUBTASK 72-24-01-390-002-F00 (11) Do a spot touch-up of the oxide film coating on the inspected areas (TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00).

F. Examine the Abradable Shroud

SUBTASK 72-24-02-210-001-F00 (1) Do a visual check of the abradable shroud for damage: (a) If findings are more than these limits, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00, unless you are given other instructions. (b) Cracks. 1) There is no limit to the number of cracks. (c) Craters (length < 5 X width) and impacts other than cracks, grooves, circumferential impacts, disbonding or rub marks. 1) All craters and impacts (other than cracks, grooves, circumferential impacts, disbonding or rub marks) are permitted with these limits: a) The total of all impacted areas is not more than 160 in2 (1032 cm2 ). b) Each impacted area is not more than 30 in2 (194 cm2 ). c) Each impacted area is not more than 2.5 in. (63.5 mm) in axial width. d) The minimum distance between impacted areas is equal to the maximum width of the nearest single impacted area. e) The fan case parent metal does not show through. 2) If the fan case parent metal shows through, a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if: a) Craters and impacts are within dimensional limits. b) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check. 3) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area. a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00. 4) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00. (d) Grooves (length > 5 X width and pointed within 0-80 degrees the engine axis). 1) All grooves are permitted with these limits: a) The maximum width of one groove is not more than 0.32 in. (8 mm). b) The total groove width is not more than 1.25 in. (32 mm) with a separation of not less than 0.1 in. (2.5 mm). c) The fan case parent metal does not show through. 2) If the fan case parent metal shows through, a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if: a) Grooves are within dimensional limits. b) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area. a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00. 4) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00. (e) Circumferential impact (360 degrees or pointed within 80-90 degrees the engine axis) 1) All circumferential impacts are permitted with these limits: a) The maximum width of one or cumulative impact is not more than 1.5 in. (38.1 mm). b) The fan case parent metal does not show through. 2) If the maximum axial width of one or cumulative impact is not more than 2 in. (51 mm), a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if: a) The parent metal does not show through. 3) If the fan case parent metal shows through, a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if: a) The circumferential impacts are within dimensional limits. b) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check. 4) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area. a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00. 5) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00. (f) Disbonding (other than cracks, craters, grooves, circumferential impacts or rub marks), the fan case parent metal shows through. 1) A Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if: a) The cumulative of all impacted areas (including craters (length < 5 X width) and impacts other than cracks, grooves, circumferential impacts or rub marks) is not more than 160 in2 (1032 cm2 ). b) Each impacted area is not more than 30 in2 (194 cm2 ). c) Each impacted area is not more than 2.5 in. (63.5 mm) in axial width. d) The minimum distance between impacted areas is equal to the width of the nearest single impacted area. e) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check. 2) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area. a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00. 3) Check every 10 flight cycles or 15 flight hours (whichever occurs first) that the above conditions are still fulfilled. 4) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00. (g) Rear side strip erosion. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) The maximum permitted dimension is 2.756 in. (70 mm) in axial width from the aft side of the abradable and 0.138 in. (3.5 mm) in depth. 2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if the maximum depth from the aft side of the abradable is not more than 0.157 in. (4 mm). 3) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00. (h) Fan blade rubs. 1) There is no limit to the number of fan blade rubs.

(0.25 mm) of material. i) Turn the mobile part of the scouring fixture, SPL-15839, in clockwise direction, forward looking aft, smoothly with the handles located on the support, to remove material from the abradable liner. j) After this first machining, put mark of the tool position on the mobile table and move the milling cutter back. k) Read the measuring arm position on the dial indicators as follows: <1> The measuring arm must touch the machined abradable liner. <2> The dial indicators must give the same reading. l) If not, do these steps: <1> Set the dial indicator located near the mobile table to Zero. <2> Record the difference between the 2 dial indicators. <3> Set this value on the mobile table dial indicator; to do this, loosen nut, turn screws and do the above steps: <a> "R" is the value read on the mobile table dial indicator. <b> "A" is the value read on the dial indicator. <c> "B" is the value read on the dial indicator. <d> "C" is the correction to be done to "R". <e> If "C" is positive, add this value to "R". <f> If "C" is negative, subtract this value from "R". (0.25 mm) of material. n) Turn smoothly the mobile part of the tool with handles located on the support, in clockwise direction, forward looking aft, to remove material again. o) Do a new check procedure after each machining. p) Do the process until you have a correct machining angle. NOTE: Machining is completed when the measuring arm dial indicator shows a Zero indication on a full turn. q) Close the ball valve to stop the motor. WARNING PUT ON PROTECTIVE GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THE BASE AND HARDENER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS PRECAUTION, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Mix by weight, 100 parts of the base and 94 parts of the hardener. NOTE: Proportions of the base and hardener are the same for Scotchweld EC 3524B/A BLACK and Scotchweld EC 3524B/A BLUE. 1) Use the compound in less than 30 minutes. NOTE: Polymerization occurs at 86°F (30°C) after 30 minutes. Prepare the compound in small quantities. (b) Mix the base and hardener by hand until it becomes a homogeneous material. NOTE: For Scotchweld EC 3524B/A BLACK, mixed compound color should be grey. For Scotchweld EC 3524B/A BLUE, mixed compound color should be pale blue. 1) Mix the base and hardener slowly to prevent air bubbles in the mixture. (a) Installation of the reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838. 1) Put the carter protector of the reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838, in position (Figure 803). 2) Apply 3M 471 tape, G51486 [CP2109], to the edges of the reconditioning area, to protect the edges of the containment case (Figure 804). 3) Make sure that the reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838, is clean. If necessary, clean with acetone solvent, B01058 [CP1039]. 4) Manually make sure that the rolls and rollers turn correctly. 5) Make sure that the six clamps are turned out of the engine axle. They must not touch the fan disk (Figure 805). NOTE: The white mark on the knurled buttons must point in. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE SCRAPING BLADE AND THE ROLLER SET ARE IN THE UPPER POSITION NOT TO TOUCH THE CONTAINMENT CASE. a) Put the reconditioning fixture assembly in position on the fan disk or on the dummy fan disk. b) With the handle, adjust the height of the tool to the height of the engine. Use the centering devices as a visual reference. c) Carefully, move the reconditioning fixture assembly until it touches the fan disk or the dummy fan disk. d) Unscrew the knobs. Turn the knurled buttons clockwise as far as they will go until the clamps touch the fan disk or the dummy fan disk. Screw the knobs in sequence (1 to 3) to attach reconditioning fixture to the fan disk or to the dummy fan disk (Figure 807). NOTE: The white mark on the knurled buttons must point out. 8) Remove the reconditioning dolly (Figure 808). a) Unscrew the two knobs and turn the two knurled buttons by 180 degrees counterclockwise. b) Remove the reconditioning dolly by lightly lowering the slider with the handle. NOTE: Lightly hold the tool until it finds equilibrium. c) Now, the reconditioning fixture is held by the fan disk or by the dummy fan disk. Make sure that it can turn freely. 9) Put the lift handle in position (Figure 809). 10) Do the adjustment of the scraping blade and the roller set (Figure 810). a) Adjustment of the scraping blade. <1> Put the scraping support in lower position with the two knurled screws. <2> Disengage the lift lever from its position to lower the scraping blade and roller set (Figure 809). <3> Move the scraping support on the containment case in an area without abradable. <4> Make sure that the two rollers of the scraping support touch the containment case. <5> Adjust the clearance between the scraping blade and the containment case with the adjustment screws. NOTE: The clearance must be 0.039 in. (1 mm). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL <6> Put the scraping blade and roller set in upper position with the lift lever and put the scraping support in upper position with the two knurled screws. b) Adjustment of angle and height of the rolls. NOTE: Make sure that the scraping support is in upper position. <1> Disengage the lift lever from its position to lower the scraping blade and roller set (Figure 809). <2> Make a full turn of reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838. Make sure that the rolls constantly touch the containment case. <3> If not, do the adjustment as follows: <a> Use the adjustment bolts to lift rolls No. 1 and No. 2. Roll No. 3 must still touch the containment case. <b> Make a full turn reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838. Make sure that roll No. 3 constantly touches, on that two sides, the containment case. If not, adjust with the adjustment bolts. <c> Adjust roll No. 2 with the adjustment bolts until roll No. 2 is held by a 0.002 in. (0.05 mm) shim on each side of the containment case. Do a check by turning reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838, by 360 degrees. <d> Adjust roll No. 1 with the adjustment bolts until roll No. 1 is held by a 0.002 in. (0.05 mm) shim on each side of the containment case. Do a check by turning reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838, by 360 degrees. <e> Make sure that roll No. 3 continues to touch the containment case. c) Adjustment of the roller guide of the polyester film. <1> Unwind the polyester film onto the containment case and make sure that it stays in the correct axis. NOTE: The polyester film must be equally applied on each side of the containment case. <2> If not, adjust with the adjustment nuts on the two sides of the roller guide and do a check again. <3> Wind the polyester film back on the roller film. d) Put the scraping blade and roller set in upper position. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE SCRAPING SUPPORT IS IN THE UPPER POSITION NOT TO TOUCH THE CONTAINMENT CASE. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION YOU MUST QUICKLY APPLY THE ABRADABLE MATERIAL TO GET A CORRECT QUALITY OF FINISH WHEN YOU APPLY IT. IF NOT, THE SURFACE WILL BE ROUGH AND CAN CAUSE DAMAGE. (b) Apply the abradable material as follows: NOTE: The abradable material must be applied on minimum three sectors, one after the other, to prevent fast polymerization. 1) Do these steps to prepare the Scotchweld EC 3524B/A filler, G02499 [CP2364]: WARNING PUT ON PROTECTIVE GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THE BASE AND HARDENER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS PRECAUTION, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. a) Mix by weight, 100 parts of the base and 94 parts of the hardener. <1> Use the compound in less than 30 minutes. NOTE: Polymerization occurs at 86°F (30°C) after 30 minutes. Prepare the compound in small quantities. b) Mix the base and hardener by hand until it becomes a pale blue homogeneous compound. <1> Mix the base and hardener slowly to prevent air bubbles in the mixture. 2) Apply the abradable material to the reconditioning area. a) Apply a thin layer of abradable in the radius of the reconditioning area with a spatula. b) Apply a thin layer of abradable in the reconditioning area with a spatula. NOTE: If the thin abradable layer does not bond to the case, remove and apply the thin abradable layer again. c) Apply the abradable in the reconditioning area. NOTE: If necessary, apply the abradable in multiple layers. d) Make sure that there is no lack of abradable at the interface between the radius of the abradable liner and the case. NOTE: Do not change the direction of abradable application. (c) Scraping of the abradable material (Figure 811). NOTE: The scraping tool and roller set is in upper position. 1) Put the scraping support in lower position with the two knurled buttons. 2) Put the scraping blade in position before the abradable to be reconditioned. NOTE: Scraping is done in clockwise direction. 3) Disengage the lift lever from its position to lower the scraping tool and roller set (Figure 809). NOTE: The scraping support touches the containment case with its two rollers. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION THE SPEED OF OPERATION MUST BE SUFFICIENTLY SLOW NOT TO PULL THE ABRADABLE MATERIAL AWAY AND CREATE HOLES. 4) Start scraping by turning the wheel to slowly rotate the tool. a) Regularly, remove abradable material from the scraping blade. 5) Repair areas with air bubbles by piercing them and adding abradable material. 6) Put the scraping support in upper position with the two knurled buttons. 7) Put the scraping tool and roller set in upper position with the lift lever (Figure 809). 8) Quickly remove the abradable material from the scraping blade with acetone solvent, B01058 [CP1039]. (d) Put the polyester film in position on the rolls. 1) Unwind the polyester film and put it under the three rolls. Keep the polyester film tensioned against the four rolls. a) Attach the polyester film to the scraping support with 3M 471 tape, G51486 [CP2109]. NOTE: Make sure that the polyester film is kept tensioned. (e) Do the smoothing of the abradable material (Figure 812). 1) Put the roller set in position in front of the area to be smoothed. NOTE: Smoothing is done in counterclockwise direction. NOTE: Never superimpose two layers of polyester film. 2) Disengage the lift lever from its position to lower the scraping tool and roller set (Figure 809). 3) Attach the polyester film to the containment case with a strip of 3M 471 tape, G51486 [CP2109], to make sure that the polyester film stays tensioned. 4) Move the roller set to a speed between 0.06-0.12 in./sec. (1.5-3 mm/s). NOTE: The speed must be slow to get a correct quality of flatness. 5) Make sure that there are no waves, no air bubbles and the edges are correctly cut. If not, do again the adjustment of the angle and height of the smoothing rolls. Do the step 2.F.(9)(a)10)b). NOTE: If you are at the end of the last sector, go to step 2.F.(9)(e)9). 6) Cut the polyester film with the locally manufactured set square after each sector when roll No. 3 is after the reconditioning area (Figure 813). 7) Put the scraping tool and roller set in upper position with the lift lever (Figure 809). 8) Do again steps 2.F.(9)(b) thru 2.F.(9)(e)7) for the other sectors or steps 2.F.(9)(b) thru 2.F.(9)(e)5) for the last sector. 9) At the end of the last sector, remove roll No. 1 and roll No. 2 to complete smoothing with roll No. 3 without smoothing the first sector again. 10) Cut the polyester film with the locally manufactured set square. 11) Put the scraping tool and roller set in upper position with the lift lever (Figure 809). 12) Wait for 12 hours minimum before you remove the polyester film and the colored plastic tape. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) Removal of reconditioning fixture (Figure 814). 1) Make sure that the scraping blade and the roller set are in the upper position. 2) Remove the lift handle and put it in stored position (Figure 809). 3) Put the reconditioning dolly in position. Make sure that it is at the correct height. 4) Make sure that the two knurled buttons of the reconditioning dolly point in. 5) Engage the reconditioning dolly into the reconditioning fixture. 6) Attach the reconditioning dolly into the reconditioning fixture with the two knobs. a) Unscrew the two knobs. b) Turn the two knurled buttons out. c) Tighten the two knobs to tightly attach the reconditioning dolly to the reconditioning fixture. 7) Move up the slider with the handle to between 0.039 in. (1 mm) and 0.079 in. (2 mm) to lift the reconditioning fixture. 8) Loosen the six knobs of the reconditioning fixture to release the reconditioning fixture from the fan disk or from the dummy fan disk (Figure 814). NOTE: Use the reverse sequence than for installation (3 to 1) (Figure 807). 9) Turn the six knurled buttons counterclockwise. NOTE: The white mark on the knurled buttons must point in. 10) Remove the reconditioning fixture assembly with the reconditioning dolly. (g) Reconditioning of the containment case. 1) Remove the carter protector of the reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838, by loosening the wing nuts and put it on the reconditioning dolly (Figure 803). 2. High Pressure Compressor Front Stator Inspection (Figure 601)

A. General

F. High Pressure Compressor Front Stator Inspection

SUBTASK 72-32-00-900-001-F00 (1) If you find damage that is not in the limits, replace the engine, unless you are given other instructions (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00 and TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-001-F00 (2) Look for damage to the Front Stator Case: (a) Cracks 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) A Continue-in-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours, if the cracks in the skin are less than 0.17 in. (4.3 mm) in length and there are no cracks in the flanges. (b) Nicks, pits, marks, and scratches 1) All nicks, pits, marks, and scratches are permitted if the damage is not more than 0.050 in. (1.3 mm) in depth. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) The Continue-in-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours for nicks, pits, marks, and scratches that are more than the limit. SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-002-F00 (3) Look for damage to the actuation rings: (a) Cracks 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) The Continue-in-Service limits are as follows: a) Do an inspection again in or less than 200 cycles if a crack is found but does not extend into adjacent transition radius. b) Replace actuation ring in or less than 200 cycles if a crack is found that connects 2 adjacent ring sides. c) Replace actuation ring in or less than 5 cycles if a crack is found that connects 3 or more ring sides. (b) Distortion, bends, or twists 1) Distortion, bends, or twists are not permitted. 2) A Continue-in-Service limit of 5 cycles is permitted, if there is no separation of the actuation rings. (c) Separation 1) Separation is not permitted. (d) Missing bushings on Stages 1 and 2 1) Up to three missing bushings for each stage permitted. 2) If four missing bushings for each stage are found, repair within 200 cycles (TASK 72-32-00-900-801-F00). 3) If five or more missing bushings for each stage are found, replace the actuation ring flange bushing (TASK 72-32-00-900-801-F00). (e) Missing bushings on Stage 3 1) Up to three missing bushings permitted. 2) If you find four missing bushings, replace the actuation ring bushings in or less than 200 cycles (TASK 72-32-00-900-802-F00). 3) If you find five or more missing bushings, replace the actuation ring bushings (TASK 72-32-00-900-802-F00). (f) Missing or broken bushing legs 1) Missing or broken bushing legs are permitted. SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-003-F00 (4) Look for damage to the connecting links: (a) Cracks in the connecting links on only one side of the engine 1) Cracks are not permitted. 2) A Continue-in-Service limit of 5 cycles is permitted, if the cracked connector link is replaced. (b) Cracks in the connecting links on the two sides of the engine 1) Cracks are not permitted. (c) Missing bushings CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Missing bushings are not permitted. Replace the connecting link (TASK 72-32-00-900-804-F00). SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-001-F00 (5) Look for damage to the IGV and stage 3 lever arms: (a) Broken IGV and stage 3 lever arms 1) Broken arms are not permitted. 2) A Continue-in-Service limit for the engine of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted, if you replace the broken lever arm. (b) Lever arms that are not engaged in the actuation ring or connecting link 1) This condition is not permitted. (c) Cracked, bent, or twisted lever arms 1) Cracked, bent, or twisted lever arms are not permitted. 2) Do these steps: a) Remove the lever arm. b) Compare the removed lever arm with a new lever arm in an optical comparator (P/N: 2202500) to find the angle of the bend or twist. c) For a removed lever arm that has a bent or twisted angle of less than 4 degrees, install a new lever arm and put the engine back into service. d) For a removed lever arm that has a bent or twisted angle of 4 degrees or more, install a new lever arm before you put the engine back into service and replace the engine before 10 cycles or 25 hours. (d) Nicks, dents, and scratches 1) Replace the lever arm if the damage is more than the limits that follow. 2) Nicks, dents, and scratches in Area A are not permitted. 3) All nicks, dents, and scratches in Area B that are not more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). a) Sharp points at the bottom of the nicks, dents, and scratches are not permitted. 4) All nicks, pits, marks, and scratches in area C that are not more than 0.002 in. (0.05 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). NOTE: The limits do not apply to the pin. (e) Do a check for loose variable stator vanes. 1) There is no maximum limit of radial and side motion if the bushing is in place and if there is no metal-to-metal contact. NOTE: Shake the vane stem. Listen for metal-to-metal contact. a) Replace the bushing if it is missing (TASK 72-32-00-900-802-F00). SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-002-F00 (6) Look for damage to the stage 1 and 2 lever arms: (a) Cracked, broken, bent, or twisted lever arms 1) This condition is not permitted. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Lever arms that are not engaged into the actuation ring or connector link 1) This condition is not permitted. (c) Nicks, dents, and scratches in the lever arms 1) Replace the engine if these limits are more than permitted. 2) Nicks, dents, and scratches in Area A are not permitted. 3) All nicks, dents, and scratches in Area B that are not more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). a) Sharp points at the bottom of the nicks, dents, and scratches are not permitted. 4) All nicks, pits, marks, and scratches in area C that are not more than 0.002 in. (0.05 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). NOTE: The limits do not apply to the pin. (d) Do a check for loose variable stator vanes. 1) There is no maximum limit of radial and side motion if the bushing is in place and if there is no metal-to-metal contact. NOTE: Shake the vane stem. Listen for metal-to-metal contact. 2) If you hear metal-to-metal contact, replace the engine (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00 and TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00). 3) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if there is metal-to-metal contact on no more than 50% of the vanes. SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-003-F00 (7) Examine the bellcrank assemblies (two locations): (a) Cracks 1) Replace the bellcrank assembly (TASK 72-32-00-900-805-F00). (b) Nicks, pits, scores, and scratches 1) All nicks, pits, scores, and scratches that are not more than 0.030 in. (0.76 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). 2) If there is damage found that is more than the limits, replace the bellcrank assembly (TASK 72-32-00-900-805-F00).

G. HPC Variable Stator Vane (VSV) Resistance Check

SUBTASK 72-32-00-000-001-F00 (1) Disconnect the tie-rods [28] from the actuation ring clevises (TASK 72-32-00-900-805-F00). (a) On each VSV stage, remove the D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80] that attach the tie-rods [28] to the actuation rings on the left and right sides. SUBTASK 72-32-00-200-001-F00 (2) Perform a VSV resistance (force) check for IGV, Stage 1, Stage 2, and Stage 3 as follows: (a) For each VSV stage, attach a push-pull digital force gauge, COM-1822, or equivalent force indicator to the clevis of each actuation ring and pull the actuation ring to rotate the stage from open to closed, and then back to open. (b) Record the value for each direction (open and closed), for each VSV stage. (c) Make sure that each VSV stage requires not more than 100 lbf (445 N) to move the actuation ring. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-022-F00 (3) Connect the tie-rods [28] to the actuator ring clevis (TASK 72-32-00-900-805-F00) . WARNING REFER TO THE PRODUCT LABEL AND THE MANUFACTURER'S (MATERIAL) SAFETY DATA SHEET (SDS) FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON THE HAZARDS, STORAGE, SAFE HANDLING AND PROPER USE OF THESE PRODUCTS. (a) Lubricate the threads of the D-head bolts [70] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (b) Connect the tie-rods [28] to the clevises on the actuation rings with the D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80]. NOTE: The D-head bolts point aft for the IGV and forward for stages 1, 2, and 3. (c) Tighten the self-locking nuts [80] to 62 in-lb (7.01 N·m) - 68 in-lb (7.68 N·m). G. High Pressure Compressor Stage 4 Vane Trailing Edge Inspection

SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-010-F00 (1) Do an inspection of the HPC stage 4 vane trailing edge: (a) Do a borescope inspection (BSI) of the HPC airfoils and look for erosion of the airfoil corners and chord (TASK 72-00-00-200-804-F00). (b) Do a special flexible BSI of the HPC stage 4 vane sector trailing edges for erosion as follows (Figure 605): 1) Use the borescope resolution monitor, COM-9899, to make sure that the fiber borescope, COM-2196, is serviceable. 2) Connect the fiber light cable to the fiber borescope, COM-2196. 3) Put the flexible light source, SPL-2197, into the LPT bleed port on the HPC front stator at the 10:30 o'clock position. 4) Put the flexible light source, SPL-2197, through the HPC stage 4 vane sector bleed slot. NOTE: You can see five or six vane sector bleed slots through the LPT bleed port. It is recommended to do an inspection in at least two or three positions to get the best viewing angle of the vane sector trailing edge. 5) Articulate the scope to get a focus on the vane sector trailing edge. 6) Look for erosion on the HPC stage 4 vane sector trailing edge, especially near the outer platform (Figure 605, Figure 606, and Figure 607). 7) Re-inspection intervals depend on the amount of serviceable distress found. a) If no erosion is found, then re-inspect before 4,800 cycles. b) If the trailing edge is eroded but not axially past the start of the bleed slot, then re-inspect before 1,600 cycles (Figure 605). c) If the trailing edge is eroded axially past the start of the bleed slot, then remove engine before 100 cycles. 8) Slowly pull the flexible light source, SPL-2197, back out of the port after you complete the inspection.

F. Lever Arms and Bushings (IGV and Stage 3) Replacement

SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-003-F00 (1) Remove the lever arm and bushings. (a) Hold the lever arm with the anti-torque lever, SPL-9071, to make sure the vane does not turn. (b) Remove the nut and washer from the vane stem. (c) Use the lever arm puller, SPL-9072, to remove the lever arm from the vane. (d) If it is necessary, remove the bushings from the stator case and actuation ring. (e) If you install the shims, remove and discard the shims from the 3rd-stage vanes. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-002-F00 (2) Install the lever arm and bushings. (a) If it is necessary, install new bushings in the stator case and actuation ring. (b) Install the lever arm as follows: CAUTION YOU MUST ALIGN THE ROUNDED END OF THE LEVER ARM SLOT WITH THE ROUNDED END OF THE VANE TRUNNION. IF YOU DO NOT ALIGN THE VANE CORRECTLY, ENGINE DAMAGE WILL OCCUR. 1) Align the rounded end of the lever arm slot with the rounded end of the vane stem. a) If the vane stem has a witness mark, the lever arm is installed correctly when the mark is on the same side as the rounded end of the lever arm slot. 2) Put the lever arm on the vane stem. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) Engage the lever arm pin in the actuation ring. 4) Make sure the lever arm fully engages with the vane stem tang. (c) While you hold the lever arm with the anti-torque lever, SPL-9071, to make sure the vane does not turn, install the nut and washer from the vane stem. 1) Tighten the nut to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). (d) Make sure that two or three threads of the vane stem comes out of the nut. 1) Make sure the lever arm correctly engages the vane. 2) If the lever arm does not engage the vane stem tang, do the removal and installation procedures again.

G. Actuation Ring Connecting Link (to the VSV) Removal

SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-007-F00 WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU DO WORK ON THE ENGINE PARTS AFTER THE ENGINE IS STOPPED. THE ENGINE PARTS CAN STAY HOT FOR ALMOST ONE HOUR. DO NOT TOUCH HOT PARTS WITHOUT APPLICABLE GLOVES. HOT PARTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. CAUTION DO NOT TURN, ADJUST OR DISASSEMBLE THE ADJUSTABLE LINK. IF YOU DO MOVE THE ADJUSTABLE LINK, YOU MUST ADJUST THE ADJUSTABLE LINK AGAIN. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS PRECAUTION, INCORRECT ENGINE OPERATION CAN OCCUR. (1) Disconnect the tie rod [7] from the clevis of the defective connecting link [1] as follows: NOTE: Do not adjust tie rod. (a) Remove the nut [6]. (b) Remove the D-head bolt [8]. SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-008-F00 (2) Cut and remove safety wire. SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-009-F00 (3) Remove the bolts [2] that hold the connecting link [1] to the actuation ring [5]. NOTE: There is a locating pin at each end of the connecting link. The straight pin stays in the actuation ring segment. The pin with the head comes out with the connecting link.

H. Actuation Ring Connecting Link (to the VSV) Installation

SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-013-F00 (1) If the trapped straight pin [4] comes out with the connecting link [1], apply Compound, A50138 to the end of thetrapped straight pin [4] that goes in the actuation ring [5]. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-014-F00 (2) Install the trapped straight pin [4] in the actuation ring [5]. NOTE: On the right side, the pin goes in the top segment of the actuation ring. On the left side, the pin goes in the lower segment of the actuation ring. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-015-F00 (3) Install the connecting link [1] to the actuation ring [5] segments. (a) Make sure the trapped straight pin [4] fully engages the hole in the actuation ring [5]. NOTE: Make sure the lever arms are correctly installed in the connecting link bushings. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-016-F00 (4) Install the headed pin [3] in the connecting link [1] and actuation ring [5] segment. SUBTASK 72-32-00-640-003-F00 (5) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the threads and friction surface of the bolt [2]. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-017-F00 (6) Install the bolt [2]. (a) Tighten the bolt [2] between 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) and 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-018-F00 (7) Make sure that the trapped straight pin [4] is correctly installed in the actuation ring [5]. (a) Use safety wire through the inspection hole of the connecting link [1] to feel for the pin. SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-009-F00 (8) Do a visual check: CAUTION BLADE DAMAGE CAN OCCUR IF YOU DO NOT ENGAGE THE LEVER ARMS CORRECTLY. (a) Make sure all the lever arms are correctly installed in the connecting link [1] bushings. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-019-F00 (9) Safety wire the bolts [2]: (a) Use safety wire, G02345 [CP8001]. SUBTASK 72-32-00-640-004-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU SEAT THE D-HEAD BOLT IN THE RECESS OF THE CONNECTING LINK. IF NOT, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE. (10) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the threads of the D-head bolt [8]. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-020-F00 (11) Install the tie rod [7] in the connecting link [1] with the D-head bolt [8] and nut [6]. NOTE: The bolt head goes aft for IGV and forward for stages 1, 2, and 3. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-021-F00 (12) Install the nut [6] and tighten between 105 in-lb (11.86 N·m) to 115 in-lb (12.99 N·m). NOTE: Do not adjust the tie rod. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL

NOTE: A check of the HPC VSV system resistance, as specified in TASK 72-32-00-200-803-F00 of the VSV Bellcrank Assembly, is required prior to return to service. SUBTASK 72-32-00-300-001-F00 (3) Do the repair of the VSV actuator system hardware: (a) Do this task: Variable Stator Vane (VSV) Actuator System Hardware Repair, TASK 72-32-00-900-806-F00. SUBTASK 72-32-00-200-002-F00 (4) Do a resistance (force) check of the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) System for IGV, Stage 1, Stage 2, and Stage 3 (TASK 72-32-00-200-803-F00). (a) Remove the engine if any stage requires more than 100 lbf (445 N) to move the actuation ring. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-023-F00 (5) Do these steps to install VSV Bellcrank Assembly: (a) Clean the component interface and/or the adjacent area. (b) Do a visual inspection of the component interface and/or the adjacent area. (c) Install the VSV bellcrank assembly as follows: 1) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the bolt [20], bolt [21], bolt [23], and bolt [25]. 2) Install the mounting sleeve [50] on the head-end side of the assembly. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Put the sleeve [50] on the inboard side of the bellcrank mounting boss on the connecting link side. b) Position the actuation assembly on the mounting boss and align the bolt holes. 3) Attach both mounting bosses, on the head-end side of the assembly, with two washers [30] and the bolt [20] and bolt [21]. 4) Install the mounting sleeve [50] on the rod-end side of the actuator. a) Put the sleeve [50] on the inboard side of the bellcrank mounting boss on the connecting link side. b) Position the actuation assembly on the mounting boss and align the bolt holes. 5) Attach the mounting boss, on the rod-end and connecting link side of the assembly, with the washer [40] and bolt [23]. 6) Attach the mounting boss, on the rod-end and actuator side of the assembly, with mounting spacer [60], washer [40], and bolt [25]. 7) Tighten the two head-end bolt [20] and bolt [21] to between 110 in-lb (12.43 N·m) and 120 in-lb (13.56 N·m). a) Install the safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002] on the mounting bolts (TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00). 8) Tighten the two rod-end bolt [23] and bolt [25] to between 215 in-lb (24.29 N·m) and 225 in-lb (25.42 N·m). a) Install the safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002] on the mounting bolts (TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00). 9) Lubricate the threads of the D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. 10) Install the rod-ends of the connecting links to the actuation ring clevises and secure with D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80]. NOTE: The bolt head goes aft for IGV and forward for stages 1, 2, and 3. 11) Tighten the self-locking nuts [80] to between 62 in-lb (7.01 N·m) and 68 in-lb (7.68 N·m). SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-024-F00 (6) Install the left or right VSV actuator (TASK 75-31-01-400-801-F00 or TASK 75-31-01-400-802-F00).

H. Test Requirements

SUBTASK 72-32-00-700-003-F00 (3) Perform FADEC system test (TASK 73-21-00-700-802-F00). SUBTASK 72-32-00-700-004-F00 (4) Perform minimum idle leak check (TASK 71-00-00-700-801-F00) to ensure that on the Flight Management Computer System (FMCS) Control Display Unit (CDU) no fault is shown related to the VSV system. SUBTASK 72-32-00-700-005-F00 (5) Perform a Power Assurance test (TASK 71-00-00-700-813-F00). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL

6. Variable Stator Vane (VSV) Actuator System Hardware Repair (Figure 805, Figure 806, Figure 807, Figure 808, and Figure 809)

A. General

(1) This task gives the instructions to disassemble, assemble, and do the repair of the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) actuator assembly. (2) This procedure requires the VSV actuator removed from the engine.

B. References

Reference Title 72-00-00-100-805-F00 Clean the External Engine Surfaces (P/B 701)

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification D00601 [CP2101] Vaseline - Graphite Mineral

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

E. Prepare for the Repair

SUBTASK 72-32-00-000-004-F00 (1) If not already done, do the applicable steps in this task to remove the VSV bellcrank assembly: Variable Stator Vane (VSV) Bellcrank Assembly Removal and Installation, TASK 72-32-00-900-805-F00.

F. Variable Stator Vane (VSV) Actuator System Hardware Repair

SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-013-F00 (1) Do these steps to disassemble the left or right VSV actuator support assembly (Figure 806 or Figure 807): (a) Remove the nuts [11], washers [12], bolts [13], nut [14], washer [15], bolt [16], and bushing [17] that attach the master rod [19] to the bellcrank assemblies. (b) Remove the master rod [19]. (c) Remove the nuts [1] and bolts [2] that attach the bellcranks to the support plates. (d) Remove the upper support plate [4]. (e) Remove the bellcrank [7], bellcrank [8], bellcrank [9], and bellcrank [10]. (f) Remove the bushings [5] from each side of the bellcranks. (g) Remove the sleeves [6] from the bellcranks. (h) Remove the nuts [22] and bolts [23] that attach the tie rod assemblies to the bellcranks. (i) Remove the tie rod [24], tie rod [25], tie rod [26], and tie rod [27]. SUBTASK 72-32-00-100-002-F00 (2) Do the steam clean of these parts (TASK 72-00-00-100-805-F00): (a) The master rod (b) The bellcranks (c) The tie rod assemblies CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) The support plates (e) The links (f) The other VSV hardware. SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-026-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL EACH TIE-ROD ASSEMBLY ON THE CORRECT BELLCRANK STAGE. IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL EACH TIE-ROD ASSEMBLY CORRECTLY, DAMAGE TO THE VSV ACTUATOR CAN OCCUR. (3) Do these steps to assemble the left or right VSV actuator support assembly (Figure 806 or Figure 807): (a) Attach the Inlet Guide Vane (IGV), stage 1 and stage 2 bellcranks (bellcrank [7], bellcrank [8], and bellcrank [9]) to their respective tie-rod assembly (tie rod [24], tie rod [25], and tie rod [26]) with bolts [23] and nuts [22]. NOTE: The nuts must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on torque of 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m). 1) The stage identification on the bellcrank goes up (Figure 808). 2) The bolt goes up through the short end of the bellcrank (Figure 808). (b) Tighten the nuts [22] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m). (c) Install the bolts [2] up through the lower support plate [3] in the stage 1 and 2 positions. (d) Install the sleeves [6] in the lower support plate [3] at the IGV, stage 1, 2, and 3 positions. (e) Install the bushings [5] on the sleeves [6]. 1) The flange goes down. (f) Install the bellcrank [7] on the bushings at the IGV position. 1) The stage identification on the bellcrank goes up. (g) Install the stage 1-3 bellcranks (bellcrank [8], bellcrank [9], and bellcrank [10]). (h) Install the upper support plate [4]. (i) Install the bolt [2] in the support assembly at the IGV position. 1) The head of the bolt goes up. (j) Install the nuts [1]. NOTE: The nuts must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on torque of 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m). (k) Tighten the nuts [1] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m). (l) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], to the bearing surfaces of the master rod [19]. (m) Attach the master rod [19] to the IGV, stage 1 and stage 2 bellcranks with bolts [13], washers [12], and nuts [11]. 1) The bolt head goes up at the IGV position and down at the stage 1 and 2 positions. (n) Install the bushing [17] at the stage 3 position. 1) The flange goes down. (o) Install the bolt [16] at the stage 3 position. 1) The head of the bolt goes up. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (p) Install the washer [15] and nut [14]. NOTE: The nut must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on torque of 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m). (q) Tighten the nut [14] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m). (r) Attach the stage 3 bellcrank [10] to the stage 3 tie rod [27] with bolt [23] and nut [22]. NOTE: The nut must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on torque of 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m). 1) The stage identification on the bellcrank goes up (Figure 808). 2) The bolt goes up through the short end of the bellcrank (Figure 808). (s) Tighten the nut [22] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m). SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-005-F00 (4) Do these steps to examine the free play of the tie rod [24], tie rod [25], tie rod [26], and tie rod [27] (Figure 809): (a) Put the VSV actuator assembly on a surface plate. (b) Use C-clamps to hold the assembly to the angle plate. (c) Install a dial indicator on the end of the IGV tie-rod bearing. (d) With the master rod [19] restrained, try to move the tie-rod up and down by hand. 1) Look at the indicator while you try to move the tie-rod. 2) The maximum free play permitted is 0.010 in. (0.254 mm).

2. Combustion Case Inspection (Figure 601)

A. General

(1) This task gives you the instructions to visually examine the combustion case of the engine. (2) The combustion case is at the center of the engine.

B. References

Reference Title 70-10-07-800-801-F00 Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices (P/B 201) 71-00-02-000-801-F00 Power Plant - Removal (P/B 401) 71-00-02-400-801-F00 Power Plant - Installation (P/B 401) 72-00-00-200-805-F00 Combustion Section Borescope Inspection (P/B 601) 78-31-00-010-801-F00 Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection) (P/B 201) 78-31-00-010-804-F00 Close the Thrust Reverser (Selection) (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

D. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 72-41-00-860-001-F00 (1) For the applicable engine, install a DO-NOT-OPERATE tag on the engine start lever. SUBTASK 72-41-00-860-002-F00 (2) For engine 1; Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE SUBTASK 72-41-00-860-003-F00 (3) For engine 2; Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-41-00-010-001-F00 WARNING DO THESE SPECIFIED TASKS IN THE CORRECT SEQUENCE BEFORE YOU OPEN THE THRUST REVERSER: RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE, DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURES FOR THE LEADING EDGE AND THE THRUST REVERSER (FOR GROUND MAINTENANCE), AND OPEN THE FAN COWL PANELS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS SEQUENCE, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (4) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.

E. Examine the Combustion Case for Damage

SUBTASK 72-41-00-900-001-F00 (1) If you find damage that is not in the limits, replace the engine, unless you are given other instructions. These are the tasks: Power Plant - Removal, TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00, Power Plant - Installation, TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-001-F00 (2) Look for damage on the outer case: (a) Cracks 1) Not serviceable. (b) Nicks, marks and scratches 1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, marks, and scratches which are permitted with these conditions: a) Not more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth, after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (c) Dents 1) All dents with a maximum depth of 0.10 inch (2.5 mm) are permitted if they have a smooth contour. (d) Bends, bulges, or distortion 1) Not permitted. CAUTION IF YOU FIND DISCOLORATION ON THE OUTER CASE, EXAMINE THE CONDITION OF THE INNER PART OF THE COMBUSTOR WITH A BORESCOPE. DISCOLORATION ON THE OUTER CASING IS AN INDICATION OF DAMAGE TO THE COMBUSTOR. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, MORE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE COULD OCCUR. (e) Discoloration 1) Discoloration is permitted only if the metal is not crazed. 2) If you find hot spots in the outer case, then do the applicable task: a) Do this task: Combustion Section Borescope Inspection, TASK 72-00-00-200-805-F00. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-002-F00 (3) Look for damage on the forward and aft flanges: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the outer edge of the flange. 1) It is permitted to have only one crack from a bolt hole. 2) It is permitted to have not more than two cracks on each flange. (b) Cracks that extend radially from the bolt holes into the case 1) Not serviceable. 2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-003-F00 (4) Look for damage to the midflange of the case: (a) Broken bolts 1) All damage is permitted with these limits: a) Not more than 10 damaged bolts. b) Not more than two broken bolts, in a group of 20 bolts. c) A minimum of 5 bolts that are not damaged on each side of the broken bolt. d) A Continue-In-Service limit of 25 cycles is permitted for 10 damaged bolts, with a maximum of 4 broken bolts in a group of 20 bolts. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-004-F00 (5) Look for damage to the fuel nozzle pads (20 locations) when the fuel nozzles are removed for other maintenance: (a) Damage to the threads 1) Chasing of the threads is permitted with this limit: a) There must be more than 4 threads that were not damaged after you chased the threads. (b) Damage to the sealing surface 1) Nicks, marks, scratches and pitting a) There is no limit to the number of nicks, marks, scratches and pitting after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). b) The damage is not more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). c) The damage must not be spread over more than 50 percent of the seal surface after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (c) Particles on the sealing surface 1) Remove all of the particles. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-005-F00 (6) Look for damage to the igniter ports when the igniters are removed for other maintenance: (a) Damage to the threads 1) Chasing of the threads is permitted with this limit: a) There must be more than 3 threads that are not damaged after you chased the threads. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-006-F00 (7) Look for damage to the borescope ports when the borescope plugs are removed for other maintenance: (a) Damage to the threads 1) Chasing of the threads is permitted with this limit: a) There must be more than 3 threads that are not damaged after you chased the threads. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-007-F00 (8) Look for damage to the HPT shroud cooling air pad when the HPT shroud is removed for other maintenance: (a) Damage to the sealing surface 1) Nicks, marks, scratches and pitting a) There is no limit to the number of nicks, marks, scratches and pitting after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). b) The damage is not more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). c) The damage must not be spread over more than 75 percent of the seal surface after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (b) Cracks in the bolt holes 1) Not serviceable. a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that is not more than 0.6 inch (1.5 mm) in length in each bolt hole. SUBTASK 72-41-00-220-008-F00 (9) Look for damage to the CDP bleed pads when the CDP LRU is removed for other maintenance: (a) Damage to the sealing surface 1) Nicks, marks, scratches and pitting a) There is no limit to the number of nicks, marks, scratches and pitting after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). b) The damage is not more than 0.03 inch (0.8 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). c) The damage must not be spread over more than 75 percent of the seal surface after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (b) Cracks in the bolt holes 1) Not serviceable. a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack no longer than 0.6 inch (1.5 mm) in length in each bolt hole. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL
