D. Low Pressure Turbine Case Inspection

SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-001-F00 (1) Look for damage on the aft flange (Figure 601): (a) Cracks that connect the bolt holes 1) Not serviceable. a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack, if the crack connects two bolt holes and does not go into the outer skin of the pressure vessel. (b) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the outer edge of the flange 1) It is permitted to have 5 cracks with a minimum of 5 holes of separation between the cracks. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the casing skin 1) Not serviceable. a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that extends 0.4 inch (10.2 mm) into the skin. (d) Cracks in other areas of the flange 1) It is permitted to have 5 cracks on each flange if they are not more than 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) in length with this condition: a) A minimum of 5.0 inches (127.0 mm) of separation between all other cracks. (e) Cracks in the skin radius of the flange and case 1) Not serviceable. (f) Nicks, scores and scratches 1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, scores, scratches with these limits: a) Not more than 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) long. b) Not more than 0.01 inch (0.25 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). c) There is a minimum separation of 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) with other damage. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-002-F00 (2) Look for damage on the casing skin: (a) Cracks in the parent metal 1) All cracks that are not more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in length and have a minimum separation of 2.0 inches (50.8 mm). a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack which is not more than 0.4 inch (10.16 mm) in length. (b) Nicks and scratches 1) All nicks and scratches 0.01 inch (0.25 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (c) Dents 1) All dents with a maximum depth of 0.02 inch (0.5 mm) are permitted if they have a smooth contour. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-003-F00 (3) Look for damage on all ports that have threads: (a) Damage to the threads 1) No more than one complete thread can be removed or the total damage for all threads cannot be more than one thread, after you chase the threads. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-013-F00 (4) Look for indications on the cap assembly (Figure 603): (a) Cracks 1) Not serviceable. (b) Finding on threads CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Any amount not more than 1/2 full thread after removal of high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). (c) Defective spring 1) Not serviceable. a) A Continue-In Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-004-F00 (5) Look for damage on the ring sector support: (a) Cracks 1) All cracks are permitted if all parts of the ring sector support are still attached by the rivets. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-005-F00 (6) Look for damage on the angle brackets: (a) Broken bracket 1) Not serviceable. a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 10 hours is permitted. (b) Cracks 1) All cracks are permitted if the cooling air tubes and the fasteners are not loose. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-009-F00 (7) Look for damage on the T49.5 probe thermocouple studs: (a) Broken or missing stud 1) Not serviceable. a) Do the repair of the broken stud (TASK 72-54-00-300-801-F00). b) A continue in service limit of 20 cycles is permitted until the broken stud is repaired with these conditions: <1> Damage is limited to one stud per T49.5 sensor. NOTE: Each T49.5 sensor has two probes, each probe is attached to two studs on the LPT. <2> A visual inspection of the area of the broken stud shows no indication of air leak. <3> A visual check makes sure there is no obvious gap between the probe attachment flange and the LPT case. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-006-F00 (8) Look for damage on the cooling air manifold (Figure 602): (a) Cracks in the forward mounting lug 1) One crack on each side of a lug is permitted. (b) A broken forward mounting lug 1) Breakage on one side of a mounting lug is permitted. 2) Breakage or a crack on each side of a forward lug is permitted if the two adjacent cooling air tube supports are not broken or have a crack that is not more than 0.591 inch (15.0 mm) in length. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) If there is breakage or a crack on each side of a forward lug, and the two adjacent cooling air tube supports are broken or have a crack that is more than 0.591 inch (15.0 mm), these are the Continue-In-Service limits: a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 hours or 10 cycles is permitted if one adjacent support is broken. b) If one or two adjacent supports have a crack that is more than 0.591 inch (15.0 mm) long, examine the part at not more than 10 hours or 10 cycles to see if the crack length increases. c) If you find that the crack length did not increase, then repeat the check at not more than 50 hours or 50 cycles, and then at each 100 hours or 100 cycles until the part is repaired or the crack length increases. d) If you find that the crack length increases, a Continue-In-Service limit of 30 hours or 30 cycles is permitted. (c) Cracks in the sheet metal 1) All cracks are permitted with these limits: a) The cracks are not longer than 0.5 inch (12.7 mm). b) The total length of all cracks is not longer than 3.0 inches (76.2 mm). c) The cracks have a minimum separation of 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) between each crack. (d) Dents on sleeve 1) All dents are permitted if they have a smooth contour and are not more than 0.03 inch (0.76 mm) in depth. (e) Nick, scratch and chafing (wear) on tube external surface 1) Maximum finish depth after you make the defect smooth is 0.008 inch (0.20 mm). a) Make the defect smooth by hand blending (CFMI CFM56 Standard Practices Manual 70-41-11) if necessary to remove sharp edges. b) Make sure there is no crack. Do this task: Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (Portable Post-Emulsifiable), TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00. (f) Scratches and chafing on box 1) All scratches and chafing are permitted if they are not more than 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) in depth. (g) Dents on box 1) All dents are permitted if they are without sharp edge and are not more than 0.118 in. (3.0 mm) in depth. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-007-F00 (9) Look for damage on the cooling air tubes: (a) Cracks in tubes 1) All cracks are permitted if not longer than 2.0 inch (50.8 mm) and separated by at least one support member. (b) Dents 1) All dents are permitted if they have a smooth contour and are not more than 20 percent of the tube outside diameter. (c) Cracks in tube clamps CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) All cracks are permitted if the tubes are correctly attached. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-008-F00 (10) Look for damage on the tube supports for the cooling air: (a) Cracks at the mounting flanges 1) All cracks are permitted if the supports are not loose. (b) Cracks in all other areas 1) All cracks are permitted if the cooling air tubes and fasteners are not loose. (c) Breakage of the forward mount lug 1) One broken lug is permitted for one-half of the distribution manifold. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-011-F00 (11) Look for damage on the LPTACC cooling air manifold: (a) Cracks in the tubes 1) No cracks are permitted. (b) Dents and collapse 1) All dents and collapse are permitted if depth is not more than 5 percent of the outer diameter of the tube. (c) Flat area 1) All flat areas are permitted if contour change is not more than 5 percent of the tube. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-012-F00 (12) Look for damage on the LPTACC cooling air duct: (a) Cracks in the tubes 1) No cracks are permitted. (b) Dents and collapse 1) All dents and collapse are permitted if depth is not more than 5 percent of the outer diameter of the tube. (c) Flat area 1) All flat areas are permitted if contour change is not more than 5 percent of the tube. SUBTASK 72-54-00-290-001-F00 (13) If the visual inspection is not satisfactory, do the Borescope Inspection of the Stage 1 Low-Pressure Turbine Nozzle Outer Air Duct Condition, TASK 72-00-00-290-801-F00.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

2. Replacement of Broken Studs on the T49.5 Probe Bracket Assembly (Figure 801, Figure 802, Figure 803, Figure 804)

A. General

(1) This procedure contains one task: to replace the broken studs on the T49.5 Probe Bracket Assembly. (2) If you find a broken stud on the bracket assembly, replace the broken stud if there is sufficient access. NOTE: The replacement of the broken studs depend on accessibility. NOTE: Make sure that free access is available for the drilling and tapping procedure. NOTE: You must discard the repaired bracket assembly at the first LPT rotor/stator disassembly. (3) The T49.5 probe (and thermocouple) bracket assemblies are installed on the LPT case at 2:00, 5:00, 7:30 and 10: 00 o’clock position and below the air cooling tubes.

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 72-54-00-010-003-F00 WARNING DO ALL OF THE SPECIFIED TASKS IN THE CORRECT SEQUENCE TO OPEN THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-54-00-010-004-F00 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU. CAUTION DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER. NOTE: The engine oil is poisonous. Use the personal protection equipment. Put the lubrication unit on the clean bench in a good ventilated area. (2) Do this task: T49.5 Probe Removal, TASK 77-21-01-000-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-54-00-010-005-F00 WARNING DO NOT BREATHE THE PARTICLES, OR GET THEM IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON A RESPIRATOR, GOGGLES, AND GLOVES AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION. THESE PARTICLES CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. WARNING USE EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN, COOL, OR DRY PARTS OR TOOLS. PARTICLES CAN CAUSE AN INJURY TO YOUR EYES. DO NOT USE MORE THAN 30 PSI (207 KPA). DO NOT POINT COMPRESSED AIR AT YOURSELF OR OTHER PERSONS. (3) Use a square access to remove the nuts and the bulkheads. NOTE: It is easier to use a square access to remove the nuts, with bulkheads removed. SUBTASK 72-54-00-320-001-F00 (4) Do these steps to prepare for the broken stud drilling. (a) Calculate the length of the remaining broken tack welded stud shank with the serviceable remaining tack welded stud. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Do these steps to install a locally manufactured tool on the serviceable remaining tack welded stud. 1) Make sure that you correctly engaged the center pin of the tooling in the bore of the T49.5 probe location. 2) Tighten the tooling to the LPT case with the original nut on the serviceable remaining tack welded stud. 3) Make sure that the tooling is correctly installed against the LPT case. (c) Make a selection to get the correct drill guide sleeve for a 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) drill. NOTE: You can identify the sleeve as the clearance guide. (d) Install the retaining screw between the drill guide sleeve and the tooling. (e) Do a check from the top of the drill guide sleeve to the T49.5 probe location of the LPT case. SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-001-F00 NOTE: Do not drill into the stud head when you remove the broken stud shank. Refer to the Standard Practices Manual (Refer to CFMI SPM, Task 70-44-50-320-006) before you drill the hole into the stud head. NOTE: When you do the drilling and tapping operation, use a minimum pressure to do these operations. If you put too much pressure, you can push the fitting away from the inside of the LPT case, as it is only safe tied by a good tack welded stud on one side. (5) Do these steps to drill the broken stud shank. (a) Calculate the necessary drill depth with the dimensions given in the above step and the dimensions shown in the figure to remove the broken stud shank. (b) Make a selection to get the correct drilling stop ring for the 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) drill. (c) Attach the stop ring to the 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) diameter drill. 1) Set it to the depth as calculated as in the above steps. (d) Put the drill into the tooling sleeve. (e) Drill to a depth permitted by the stop ring to remove the remaining broken stud shank. SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-002-F00 (6) Do these steps to prepare for tack welded stud head drilling. (a) Remove the drill guide sleeve (identified as “clearance guide”). (b) Replace it with the other drill guide sleeve (identified as “tapping drill guide”) for a 0.211 inch (5.36 mm) drill. (c) Do a check from the top of the drilling sleeve to the T49.5 probe location of the LPT case. (d) Calculate the drill depth (use the dimensions given before and the dimensions shown in the Figure) to drill through the tack welded stud head and the back plate. NOTE: You must be careful when you drill, and make sure that it does not break through the back plate. SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-003-F00 NOTE: If you do an incorrect calculation of the drill depth and setting of the drill depth stop ring, you may have a risk to go through the insulation blanket. In this case, you must do the full disassembly of the LPT rotor/stator. (7) Do these steps to drill the tack welded stud head. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Install a correct stop ring to drill a 0.211 inch (5.36 mm) diameter hole. NOTE: The stop ring is identified with a drill size of 0.211 inch (5.36 mm). NOTE: Set it to the depth specified as calculated in the “Drilling of the broken stud shank” as in the paragraph above. (b) Put the drill into the tooling sleeve. NOTE: When you perform the drilling operation, and if you find that you have too much depth, you go to drill through the insulation blanket. (c) Drill to a depth permitted by the stop ring to drill the stud head and the back plate. (d) Remove the drill guide sleeve (identified as “tapping drill guide”). (e) Replace it with the other drill guide sleeve (identified as “clearance guide”). SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-004-F00 (8) Do these steps to tap the tack welded stud head. (a) Do a check from the top of the drill guide sleeve to the T49.5 probe location of the LPT case. (b) Calculate the specified tap depth with the dimensions given before and the dimensions shown in the figure, to tap through the tack welded stud head and the back plate only. (c) Set the 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) stop ring to the specified depth with the tap given in the tooling. (d) Put the tap into the tooling sleeve. (e) Tap the head of the tack welded stud and the back plate. NOTE: Refer to CFMI SPM, Task 70-44-60-320-007. (f) Make sure that you vacuum all the unwanted particles. (g) Remove the nut. (h) Remove the tooling. SUBTASK 72-54-00-470-001-F00 (9) Do these steps to install the T49.5 probe on the reworked bracket. (a) To identify the repair, write the bulletin number CFM 56-7B-72-0423 on the locally manufactured washer (Refer to CFMI SPM, Task 70-10-12-350-005). (b) Do this task: T49.5 Probe Installation, TASK 77-21-01-400-801-F00. (c) Install the locally manufactured washer with the lockwire hole below the nut at the location adjacent to the modified broken tack welded stud. (d) Apply a light layer of the lubricant, D50068 [CP2544] on the remaining stud thread and on the new bolt thread. (e) Install the bolt (GE part number J644P09B) on the modified tapped tack welded stud head. NOTE: Make sure that you have the washer correctly located to the lockwire adjacent bolt. (f) Tighten the nut and bolt to 100.0-110.0 Pound-inches (11.5-12.5 Newton-meters). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (g) Lock the bolt to the washer below the nut with a safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or the safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] (Lockwire Installation, TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00). NOTE: If you have the second stud broken, in addition to the already replaced stud, you can do this repair to replace this second broken stud by a bolt. You must safety the bolts together with a lockwire in the head bolt holes. Keep the locally manufactured washer already installed on the first bolt to identify the repair. (h) Do a check from the top of the T49.5 probe to the LPT case. NOTE: You must not have lack of protrusion between the bolt end and the tapped stud head. (i) Make sure that the value of the protrusion is correct. NOTE: You must calculate the protrusion of the bolt thread through the modified tack welded stud head with the dimension used to find the bolt length in the figures. SUBTASK 72-54-00-970-001-F00 (10) Record the Service Bulletin number on the applicable Log Book. SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-010-F00 (11) Do the test that it listed in the T49.5 Probe Installation, TASK 77-21-01-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-54-00-410-002-F00 (12) Do this task: Close the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-804-F00. SUBTASK 72-54-00-700-001-F00 (13) Do this task: Power Plant Test Reference Table, TASK 71-00-00-800-811-F00.

H. LPT Shaft-Plug O-ring Replacement

SUBTASK 72-55-00-020-001-F00 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU. CAUTION DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER. (1) Do these steps to replace the LPT Shaft-Plug O-ring [3] and O-rings [4]. (a) Remove the retaining ring [5] from forward end of the LPT shaft [1], with a scribe. (b) Remove the LPT shaft plug [2] with the puller adapter, SPL-6180, or puller, SPL-11207. (c) Remove and discard O-ring [3] and two O-rings [4] located in the forward/aft grooves of the LPT shaft plug [2]. (d) Remove the puller adapter, SPL-6180, or puller, SPL-11207, from the LPT shaft plug [2]. WARNING ACETONE IS AN AGENT THAT IS FLAMMABLE, EXPLOSIVE, POISONOUS, AND AN IRRITANT. MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS OBEY ALL OF THE PRECAUTIONS WHEN ACETONE IS USED. • GAS/AIR MIXTURES MORE THAN THE LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMIT (LEL) CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION IF HIGH HEAT, SPARKS, OR FLAMES SUPPLY IGNITION. • USE IN AN AREA OPEN TO THE AIR. • CLOSE THE CONTAINER WHEN NOT USED. • DO NOT GET ACETONE IN THE EYES, ON THE SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. • DO NOT BREATHE THE GAS. (e) Clean the oil stains on the plug grooves with acetone solvent, E50001. (f) Install the LPT shaft plug [2] in the storage box. WARNING DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES. (g) Lightly coat new O-ring [3] and two new O-rings [4] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL NEW O-RING IN THE SEAL GROOVES AT THE FORWARD END AND THE AFT END OF THE LPT SHAFT-PLUG. IF THE O-RING IS NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. (h) Install the new O-ring [3] and two new O-rings [4] into the seal grooves of the LPT shaft plug [2]. (i) Install the LPT shaft plug [2] assembly into the forward end of the LPT shaft [1] and onto the CVT. NOTE: Insert the lug of the LPT shaft-plug in aligned slots of the LPT coupling nut and the LPT shaft. (j) Install the retaining ring [5] onto the LPT shaft [1]. (k) Do a visual inspection to make sure the correct installation of the retaining ring [5].

H. CVT O-rings and Damper Seals Replacement

SUBTASK 72-55-00-020-002-F00 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (WARNING PRECEDES) WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU. CAUTION DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER. CAUTION REPLACE THE O-RING AND DAMPER SEALS IN ENGINE WARM CONDITION IN LESS THAN TWO HOURS AFTER ENGINE SHUT DOWN. THE O-RING AND DAMPER SEALS REMOVAL ARE EASY WHEN THE ENGINE IS IN WARM CONDITION. IF YOU DO NOT, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (1) Do these steps to replace the CVT O-ring [13], O-ring [14], and three damper seals [15]. (a) Install the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole. (b) Remove the retaining ring [12] from the forward end of the LPT shaft [10] with a scribe. (c) Do these steps to install the pusher/puller, SPL-6182: 1) Screw the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, into the center vent tube [11]. 2) Install the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, on the fan disk flange with four knurled screws. 3) Engage the plate of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, in the slot of the screw and attach it with the knurled nut. (d) Do these steps to remove the center vent tube [11]: 1) Manually turn clockwise the screw of fixture of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, to disengage the center vent tube [11] from the LPT shaft [10]. NOTE: You can use a wrench if the counter torque is important. 2) Remove the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the fan disk flange. 3) Remove the center vent tube [11] equipped with the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the LPT shaft [10]. 4) Remove the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the center vent tube [11]. (e) Remove and discard the O-ring [13] and O-ring [14] located in the forward/aft grooves of the center vent tube [11]. (f) Remove and discard the damper seals [15] located in the other grooves of the center vent tube [11]. (g) Remove the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING ACETONE IS AN AGENT THAT IS FLAMMABLE, EXPLOSIVE, POISONOUS, AND AN IRRITANT. MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS OBEY ALL OF THE PRECAUTIONS WHEN ACETONE IS USED. • GAS/AIR MIXTURES MORE THAN THE LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMIT (LEL) CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION IF HIGH HEAT, SPARKS, OR FLAMES SUPPLY IGNITION. • USE IN AN AREA OPEN TO THE AIR. • CLOSE THE CONTAINER WHEN NOT USED. • DO NOT GET ACETONE IN THE EYES, ON THE SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. • DO NOT BREATHE THE GAS. (h) Clean the oil stains with acetone solvent, E50001, on the center vent tube [11], in the O-ring and damper seal grooves and in the inner diameter of the fan disk with a lint free cloth. (i) Install the center vent tube [11] in the storage box. WARNING DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES. (j) Lightly coat three new damper seals [15] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL NEW DAMPER SEALS IN THE SEAL GROOVES OF THE CENTER VENT TUBE. YOU MUST HAVE THE PLATE FACE OF THE DAMPER SEALS POINTED TO OUTER OF THE CENTER VENT TUBE. IF THE DAMPER SEALS ARE NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. (k) Install the three new damper seals [15] into the seal grooves of the center vent tube [11]. WARNING DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES. (l) Lubricate the mating face of the rear vent tube with Molykote G Rapid Plus lubricant, D00640 [CP2104], or Dow Corning 321 lubricant, D00641 [CP5062]. (m) Lightly coat new O-ring [13] and new O-ring [14] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL THE NEW O-RING IN THE SEAL GROOVE AT THE FORWARD END OF THE CENTER VENT TUBE. IF THE O-RING IS NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. (n) Install the new O-ring [13] and new O-ring [14] into the seal groves of the center vent tube [11]. (o) Install the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole. (p) Do these steps to pre-install the center vent tube [11]: 1) Screw the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, in the center vent tube [11]. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU INSTALL THE CENTER VENT TUBE. IF YOU CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE LPT SHAFT INTERNAL SUPPORTS AND PAINT, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. 2) Align and install the center vent tube [11] into the LPT shaft [10]. 3) Align the lug of the center vent tube [11] with the aligned slots of the LPT shaft [10] and the LPT coupling. (q) Do these steps to install the pusher/puller and center vent tube [11]: 1) Manually turn counter-clockwise the screw of fixture of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, to engage the center vent tube [11] into the slot of the LPT shaft [10]. NOTE: Be sure to stop turning the screw of the fixture of the pusher/puller before the lug of the CVT touches the slot of the LPT Shaft. NOTE: You can use a wrench if the counter torque is important. 2) Remove the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the fan disk flange. 3) Remove the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the center vent tube [11]. (r) Install the retaining ring [12] onto the LPT shaft [10]. (s) Remove the protective ring, SPL-6183, from the fan disk hole. (t) Do a visual inspection to make sure of the correct installation of retaining ring [12].

(b) Bent seal tooth 1) All quantities permitted, if the cumulative length of the bent tooth is not more than 1/12 of the circumference. (c) High metal 1) Not permitted. (d) Waviness CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) All quantities permitted, if the amplitude of indication is not more than 0.015 in. (0.381 mm). 2) Cracks are not permitted. (e) Crack or missing (worn away) 1) Not permitted. (f) Worn outer diameter 1) All quantities permitted, if the seal tooth outer diameter is between 2.077 in. (52.756 mm) and 2.079 in. (52.807 mm).

G. Turbine Rear Frame (TRF) Oil Inlet Cover Installation

SUBTASK 72-56-00-420-001-F00 (1) Do these steps to install the oil inlet cover [9]: (a) Install the oil nipple [20] on the rear face of No. 5 bearing support. 1) Lubricate a new O-ring [21] with oil, D00623 [CP5066]. 2) Install the O-ring [21] on the nipple [20]. 3) Install the nipple [20] on the rear face of the No. 5 bearing support. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Tighten the nipple [20] manually to seat. b) Tighten the nipple [20] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m). (b) Lubricate a new O-ring [7] with vaseline, D00672 [CP5070]. (c) Install the O-ring [7] on the oil inlet cover [9]. (d) Install a new gasket seal [6], on the No. 5 bearing support. 1) Use guide pin, SPL-14685, to hold the gasket seal [6] until the oil inlet cover [9] is attached. (e) Install the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, on the rear flange of the oil inlet cover [9]. (f) Install the oil inlet cover [9] with the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, on the No. 5 bearing support. 1) Match the position of the cover flange with the oil supply and scavenge tube [5] that comes out at the bottom of the No. 5 bearing support. (g) Apply a thin layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], on the threads of the twelve bolts [8]. (h) Install the twelve bolts [8] that attach the oil inlet cover [9] to the No. 5 bearing support. 1) Tighten the bolts [8] manually. (i) With hand pressure on oil inlet cover [9], use a slide hammer, COM-13625, on oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, or a non-metallic mallet, STD-583, to install the oil inlet cover flange against the No. 5 bearing support. (j) Remove the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, from the oil inlet cover [9]. (k) Initially, tighten the bolts [8] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern, for correct installation of the O-ring [7] (Figure 402). (l) Tighten the bolts [8] to 70 in-lb (8 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern (Figure 402). (m) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern (Figure 402). (n) Wait for 5 minutes minimum. (o) Loosen all bolts [8] by approximately 180°. (p) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern (Figure 402). (q) Wait for 5 minutes minimum. (r) Loosen all bolts [8] by approximately 180°. (s) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern (Figure 402). (t) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) starting with bolt No. 1 clockwise. (u) Do these steps to install the nipple [10] on the oil inlet cover [9]: 1) Lubricate a new O-ring [13] with oil, D00623 [CP5066]. 2) Install the O-ring [13] on the nipple [10]. 3) Install the nipple [10] on the oil inlet cover [9]. a) Tighten the nipple [10] manually to seat. b) Tighten the nipple [10] to 180.0 in-lb (20 N·m) - 195.0 in-lb (22.0 N·m). CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-56-00-420-014-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE PROTECTIVE COVER AND CAPS ON THE STRUTS OF THE TURBINE REAR FRAME. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE PARTS CAN OCCUR. (2) Do these steps to install the oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12]: WARNING ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY. (a) Lubricate threads of the nipple [10], nipple [20] and nuts (rear flange of the nozzle) of the oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12] with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (b) Put the oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12] in their installation position as follows: 1) Connect the damping oil tube [12] to the nipple [20] of the No. 5 bearing support. a) Tighten the coupling nut by hand. 2) Connect the damping oil tube [12] to the oil supply tube [11]. a) Tighten the coupling nut by hand. 3) Connect the oil supply tube [11] to the nipple [10]. a) Tighten the coupling nut by hand. (c) Loosen the oil supply tube [19] and rear sump oil supply tube brackets to have flexibility for connection with the oil supply tube [11]. (d) Connect the oil supply tube [11] to the oil supply tube [19]. 1) Tighten the coupling nut by hand. (e) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [11] to the nipple [10]. (f) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [19] to the oil supply tube [11]. (g) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [19] and rear sump oil supply tube to stiffen it (TASK 72-56-00-300-801-F00). (h) Make sure that the oil supply tube [19] is not in contact with the inside of the TRF strut. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE THE SOFT NOSE PLIERS WHEN YOU TORQUE THE UNION NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES CAN OCCUR. (i) Hold the damping oil tube [12] with the soft jaws pliers, STD-26254. (j) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [11] to the damping oil tube [12]. (k) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the union nut of the damping oil tube [12] connected to the nipple [20] of the No. 5 bearing support. (l) Make sure that the oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12] are installed without strain. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO TIGHTEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUTS. USE ONE TO HOLD THE MATING PART, AND THE OTHER TO TIGHTEN THE COUPLING NUT. IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES AND MATING PART CAN OCCUR. (m) Hold the nipple [10] with the wrench, STD-3724. (n) Tighten the coupling nut of the oil supply tube [11] connected to the nipple [10] to 265.0 in-lb (29.9 N·m) - 300.0 in-lb (33.9 N·m). (o) Hold the coupling nut of the oil supply tube [11] with the wrench, STD-3724. (p) Tighten the coupling nut of the oil supply tube [19] with the oil supply tube [11] to 265.0 in-lb (29.9 N·m) - 300.0 in-lb (33.9 N·m). (q) Do these steps to check the Dim. A (Figure 403): 1) Do a check of Dim. A in four equally spaced locations. NOTE: The tightening step must not cause the oil supply line to move. a) Make sure that the Dim. A is minimum 0.078 in. (2.0 mm). 2) If the Dim. A criterion is less than 0.078 in. (2.0 mm), do these steps: a) Do a visual inspection of the oil supply tube [19]. b) Do a torque check of the two coupling nuts of the oil supply tube [19]. c) Disconnect the oil supply tube [19]. d) Install the oil supply tube [19] again to get Dim. A within the minimum criterion of 0.078 in. (2.0 mm). 3) Make sure that there is no perforation in the insulation blanket of the oil supply tube [19]. 4) If the Dim. A criterion stays less than 0.078 in. (2.0 mm) or if there is perforation in the insulation blanket, replace the oil supply tube [19] (TASK 72-56-00-300-801-F00). (r) Make sure that the oil supply tube [19] is not in contact with the inside of the TRF strut. (s) Tighten the oil supply tube [19] to the rear sump oil supply tube and brackets (TASK 72-56-00-300-801-F00). (t) To tighten the damping oil tube [12], do these steps: CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE THE SOFT NOSE PLIERS WHEN YOU TORQUE THE UNION NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES CAN OCCUR. 1) Hold the damping oil tube [12] with the soft jaws pliers, STD-26254. 2) Tighten the union nut of the damping oil tube [12] with the nipple of the oil supply tube [11] to 90.0 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 100.0 in-lb (11.3 N·m). 3) Tighten the union nut of the damping oil tube [12] connected to the nipple [20] of the No. 5 bearing support to 90.0 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 100.0 in-lb (11.3 N·m). (u) Install safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002], on the coupling nuts of the oil supply tube [11]. (v) Install safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002], on the coupling nuts of the damping oil tube [12]. (b) Mechanical cleaning NOTE: This is a mechanical cleaning because the tube is non-removable. 1) Put protection on the No. 5 bearing to prevent any contamination by the material. NOTE: Be careful to put protection equipment on the No. 5 bearing before you start a mechanical cleaning of oil supply line. 2) Put protection on all the cavities and tube ends to prevent any contamination by the material. 3) Put a cap for the oil supply tube on the outer case side. 4) Put a sufficient quantity of WD-40 lubricant, D00139, penetrant corrosion inhibitor compound, C00174 to fill the tube and keep it to get effect on coking in the concerned area for a sufficient time. 5) Put a container under the tube to collect the penetrant corrosion inhibitor. 6) Remove the cap from the tube and collect the penetrant corrosion inhibitor. 7) Turn the tube in its position to get access to the ends of tube. 8) Introduce a cylinder-brush tool through the tube ends and move the tool to the coked area. 9) Put a small quantity of kerosene, G50611 [CP1065] or aviation turbine fuel, G51056 with a filler tool in the tube. NOTE: Do not permit the kerosene to touch your skin or clothes. Remove your clothes if the fuel touches them. Rinse your skin fully with water where the fuel touched you. Fuel can burn your skin. Kerosene is flammable, an irritant, an allergen, and has poisonous deterioration. Use personal protection equipment. Use vapor/fume control or respirator. 10) Do an alternative movement of rotation on the tool to break the coking contamination. 11) Extract the tool and use lint-free cloths to collect the coked particles. 12) Clean the cylinder-brush tool with kerosene, G50611 [CP1065] or aviation turbine fuel, G51056. a) Repeat the cleaning until tube is free of particles/contamination. NOTE: No oil coked particles/contamination is permitted. NOTE: Be careful to not introduce any particles/contamination to the internal side of bearing support to prevent bearing contamination. If not, you can cause damage to engine. H. Cleaning Internal Lube Oil Tubes

SUBTASK 72-56-00-110-014-F00 (1) This cleaning method is effective for removal of coke from internal lube oil tubes where the tubes can be disconnected to permit flow through or plugged to permit a douche type of flushing. This solution is not to enter sumps or lube system components which cannot be thoroughly flushed and purged. (a) Attach the steel tubing and a suitable pump to the lube tube to be cleaned, to supply cleaning solution to the tube and return it to the heated cleaning bath, STD-6552. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION THIS CLEANING SOLUTION IS STRONGLY ALKALINE. VENT AREA AND WEAR FACE SHIELD AND PROTECTIVE CLOTHING. IF SOLUTION CONTACTS THE SKIN OR EYES, FLUSH EXPOSED AREAS THOROUGHLY WITH COOL WATER AND SEEK IMMEDIATE MEDICAL AID. (b) Pump alkaline permanganate, G51456 [S1001, S1012, S1014, S1192, S1231, S1235] or alkaline rust remover, G51455 [S1218] through the tube and back into the heated cleaning bath, STD-6552 for 3 hours maximum. Soaking time is a function of the coke thickness. NOTE: Solution flow rate is not critical but should be sufficient to maintain tube and cleaning solution operating temperature. Tubing may be rigid or flexible, however, length should be as short as possible to reduce heat losses. The pump packing should be non-oxidizable material such as Teflon. (c) After cleaning, disconnect the lines and drain tube. Flush the tube with cold tap water until distinctive color of cleaning solution disappears. CAUTION DO NOT MIX CLEANING AGENT AND STAIN REMOVER. KEEP TANKS SEPARATED OR DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (d) To remove the cleaning solution stain on the internal surface of the tube when using one of the alkaline permanganate, G51456 [S1001, S1012, S1014, S1192, S1231, S1235] solutions, pump solution of oxalic acid, B50041 [C04-099] through the tube for 2 or 3 minutes at room temperature. NOTE: Hoses may be used with the stain remover solution. Various plastics and elastomers are compatible with this material. (e) Disconnect the lines and drain tube. Flush with the cold tap water until the effluent water has the same acidity as the inlet water (use indicator paper). (f) Disconnect the lines, drain tube and dry with clean shop air. (g) Procedure may be repeated.

4. Oil Scavenge Line Cleaning (Figure 704)

A. General

(1) This task give the instructions to clean coking deposits from the rear sump oil scavenge line and related parts. (a) The scavenge line includes the rear sump scavenge tube installed through the No. 7 turbine frame strut, the rear sump oil scavenge tube and the No. 5 bearing support nipple. (b) The scavenge tube installed through the No. 7 strut is not removable, do a mechanical cleaning of the scavenge tube (not removed). (c) The rear sump oil scavenge tube is removable, if it is necessary, do a chemical cleaning of the removed tube. (2) It is necessary to remove the oil inlet cover to do this task.

(2.0 mm), do these steps: 1) Do a visual inspection of the oil supply tube [6]. 2) Do a torque check of the two coupling nuts of the oil supply tube [6]. 3) Disconnect the oil supply tube [6]. 4) Install the oil supply tube [6] again to get Dim. A within the minimum criterion of 0.078 in. (2.0 mm). (c) Make sure that there is no perforation in the insulation blanket of the oil supply tube [6]. (d) If the Dim. A criterion stays less than 0.078 in. (2.0 mm) or if there is perforation in the insulation blanket, replace the oil supply tube [6].

F. Procedure

SUBTASK 72-56-00-010-045-F00 (1) Do these steps to remove the lock plate which is on the defective stud: (a) Remove the bolts [6] that attach the lock plate [5] to the aft outer frame. (b) Remove the lock plate [5]. SUBTASK 72-56-00-020-008-F00 (2) Do these steps to replace defective studs (Figure 805, Figure 806): (a) If the pin was installed, replace it with a new pin. WARNING DO NOT BREATHE THE PARTICLES FROM GRINDING OR LET THE PARTICLES TOUCH YOU. THE PARTICLES CAN CAUSE DAMAGE, INJURY, OR IRRITATION TO YOU. USE PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. USE LOCAL MECHANICAL EXHAUST VENTILATION OR AN APPROVED RESPIRATOR. CAUTION BE CAREFUL NOT TO CUT INTO THE METAL OF THE FRAME WHEN YOU DO THE GRINDING. DAMAGE TO THE PART CAN OCCUR. 1) Do the counterboring of the stop pin with the locally manufactured tool. 2) Loosen and remove the stud. Discard it. 3) Do an inspection of the pin hole with a gage. (b) If no pin was installed, remove the defective studs from the aft face of the inner hub as follows: WARNING DO NOT BREATHE THE PARTICLES FROM GRINDING OR LET THE PARTICLES TOUCH YOU. THE PARTICLES CAN CAUSE DAMAGE, INJURY, OR IRRITATION TO YOU. USE PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. USE LOCAL MECHANICAL EXHAUST VENTILATION OR AN APPROVED RESPIRATOR. CAUTION BE CAREFUL NOT TO CUT INTO THE METAL OF THE FRAME WHEN YOU DO THE GRINDING. DAMAGE TO THE PART CAN OCCUR. 1) Remove the tack weld which attaches the defective stud to the frame with the small narrow grinding wheel. Refer to TASK 70-41-12 (70-41-12, Power Blending) CFM Standard Practices Manual. 2) Loosen and remove the stud. Discard it. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) Complete the removal of the remaining tack weld material with a small manual grinding tool and grind the tack weld beads to have a continuous surface with the adjacent areas. Refer to TASK 70-41-12 (70-41-12, Power Blending) CFM Standard Practices Manual. WARNING USE EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN, COOL, OR DRY PARTS OR TOOLS. PARTICLES CAN CAUSE AN INJURY TO YOUR EYES. DO NOT USE MORE THAN 30 PSIG (200 KPA). DO NOT POINT COMPRESSED AIR AT YOURSELF OR OTHER PERSONS. 4) Blow the areas adjacent to the hole for the stud with shop air. 5) Do the Fluorescent-Penetrant Inspection of the machined area on the turbine frame. Refer to Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (Portable Post-Emulsifiable), TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00. a) Use S2 sensitivity. b) Cracks are not permitted. (c) Do an inspection of the tapped hole with a gage. 1) Indications are not permitted. 2) If there is any indication in the tapped hole, this repair is not applicable to the part. (d) Install the new studs as follows: 1) Apply a thin layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] on the stud threads which go into the hole of the frame. 2) Tighten the new stud as follows: a) Screw the new stud by hand on the turbine frame. b) Tighten with the wrench to complete the installation. Refer to TASK 70-70-11 (70-70-11, Tightening Methods) CFM Standard Practices Manual. c) Torque the stud to 925 in-lb (104.5 N·m)-1022 in-lb (115.5 N·m). d) Loosen the stud. e) Torque the stud a second time to 925 in-lb (104.5 N·m)-1022 in-lb (115.5 N·m). WARNING METAL PARTICLES FROM MACHINING CAN CAUSE DAMAGE, INJURY, OR IRRITATION TO YOU. USE PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. (e) Machine the pin hole with the locally manufactured tool. Refer to TASK 70-44-50 (70-44-50, Drilling) CFM Standard Practices Manual (Figure 806 and Figure 808). (f) Machine the locally manufactured pin. Refer to TASK 70-44-00 (70-44-00, Machining General) CFM Standard Practices Manual (Figure 807). NOTE: The pin must be machined in relation to the pin hole to have a tightening of 0.0008 in. (0.02 mm) to 0.0012 in. (0.03 mm) minimum. (g) Install the pin and grind the pin flush with the flange of the stud with the locally manufactured tool (Figure 808). NOTE: If there is a bushing, put the new stop pin at 0.394 in. (10.0 mm) minimum from the existing stop pin. (3) Do these steps to install the lock plate which is on the new stud: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Install the lock plate [5] on the flow path fairing [7] flange. (b) Apply a thin layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] on the threads of the bolts [6]. (c) Install two bolts [6] at each end of the lock plate [5]. (d) Check that there is a minimum clearance of 0.024 in. (0.6 mm) all around between the flow path fairing and the struts of LPT frame. (e) Install the remaining bolts [6] on the lock plate [5]. (f) Tighten all bolts [6] to 110 in-lb (12.5 Nm)–120 in-lb (13.5 Nm).

SUBTASK 72-56-01-020-001-F00 (1) Remove the air/oil separator self -locking nut [2] with a wrench [3] (Wrench, SPL-14016 ) as follows: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE LUGS OF THE WRENCHES ENGAGE THE SELF-LOCKING NUT CORRECTLY. IF THE LUGS DO NOT ENGAGE THE SELF-LOCKING NUT, DAMAGE TO THE PARTS CAN OCCUR. (a) Engage the guide in the center vent tube rear extension duct [8]. (b) At the same time, engage the wrench [3] and the countertorque wrench [4] into the slots of the self -locking nut [2] and of the center vent tube rear extension duct [8]. (c) Install the torque multiplier [5] on the countertorque wrench [4] and the lever arm of the torque multiplier [5] on the fork arm of the wrench [3]. (d) Remove the self -locking nut [2]. (e) Remove the countertorque wrench [4] and the torque multiplier [5]. SUBTASK 72-56-01-020-002-F00 (2) Remove the air/oil separator [1] with puller [6] (Puller, SPL-14020) as follows: (a) Install the protector [9], detail of the tool, on the center vent tube rear extension duct seal teeth. (b) Loosen the knurled knobs to retract the finger grips. (c) Position the tool over the center vent tube rear extension duct against the air/oil separator [1]. (d) Tighten the knurled knobs to engage the finger grips into the rear flange of the air/oil separator [1]. (e) Install the slide hammer [7] (slide hammer, COM-13625) on the Puller, SPL-14020. (f) Remove air/oil separator [1]. (g) Loosen the knurled knobs and remove the air/oil separator from the slide hammer, COM-13625.

F. Air/Oil Separator Installation

SUBTASK 72-56-01-420-001-F00 (1) Install the air/oil separator [1] as follows: (a) Remove protector [9] (856A3234P01) from the center vent tube rear extension duct [8]. (b) Install the protector (856A3234P05) of the puller [6] (Puller, SPL-14020) on the center vent tube rear extension duct seal teeth. (c) Measure and record the values A and B. WARNING DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN. (d) Lightly coat the threads of the center vent tube rear extension duct [8] and the journal of the separator with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (e) Lightly coat the mating surfaces of the center vent tube rear extension duct and of the separator with Dow Corning 321 lubricant, D00641 [CP5062]. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING WHEN YOU DO WORK WITH DRY ICE, MAKE SURE YOU USE SAFETY GOGGLES AND INSULATED GLOVES. IF DRY ICE TOUCHES YOUR EYES OR SKIN, FROSTBITE CAN OCCUR. (f) Chill the forward end of the air/oil separator [1] in dry ice for a minimum of five minutes. WARNING WHEN YOU DO WORK WITH DRY ICE, MAKE SURE YOU USE SAFETY GOGGLES AND INSULATED GLOVES. IF DRY ICE TOUCHES YOUR EYES OR SKIN, FROSTBITE CAN OCCUR. (g) Remove the air/oil separator [1] from the dry ice and install it over the center vent tube rear extension duct [8] as follows: 1) Engage the air/oil separator slots with the center vent tube lugs. 2) Turn the air/oil separator [1] by hand to make sure that the lugs engage in the slots. NOTE: Engage the air/oil separator offset slot with the center vent tube offset lug. The air/oil separator offset slot and center vent tube offset lug have spherical indentation for identification. 3) Make sure that you fully seat the air/oil separator [1]. (h) Measure Dimension C. 1) Do this measurement at four equally-spaced locations and calculate the average of the four measurements. (i) Calculate the air/oil separator seating dimension (A - B= Calculated Dimension C). (j) If the difference between the calculated dimension C and the actual dimension C is more than 0.003 inch (0.075 mm), do these steps: 1) Remove the parts. 2) Find the cause for the difference. SUBTASK 72-56-01-420-002-F00 (2) Install air/oil separator self -locking nut [2] as follows: WARNING DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES. (a) Lightly coat the threads of self-locking nut with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442]. 1) Engage the self-locking nut with your hand. (b) Remove the protector (856A3234P05) of the puller [6] from the center vent tube rear extension duct. 1) Engage the self-locking nut with your hand. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE LUGS OF THE WRENCHES ENGAGE THE SELF-LOCKING NUT CORRECTLY. IF THE LUGS DO NOT ENGAGE THE SELF-LOCKING NUT, DAMAGE TO THE PARTS CAN OCCUR. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION EXERCISE EXTREME CARE WHEN USING TORQUE MULTIPLIER. IMPROPER USE CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO ENGINE OR TOOLS. DOUBLE CHECK ALL TORQUE CALCULATIONS. IF TORQUE SHOULD INCREASE SIGNIFICANTLY PRIOR TO FINAL SEATING, REMOVE ROTOR AND INSPECT FOR CAUSE OF TORQUE INCREASE. (c) Install the wrench [3] (Wrench, SPL-14016) as follows: 1) Engage the guide in the center vent tube rear extension duct. 2) At the same time, engage the wrench [3] and the countertorque wrench [4] into these slots of the self -locking nut [2] and of the center vent tube rear extension duct [8]: (d) Seat the self -locking nut [2]. 1) Make sure that the self-locking torque value is between 245-830 lb inches. (28-93 N.m). a) Record this self-locking torque value as value D. (e) Tighten the self -locking nut [2] as follows: 1) Range of torque to be applied for the self locking nut: 856-940 lb inches (95-105 N.m). a) This torque value is called value E. 2) Torque the air/oil separator nut to a torque value F=D+E. 3) Matchmark the self-locking nut position in relation to the shaft. 4) Loosen the self-locking nut, then tighten again to the same value as calculated in the step 3.F.(2)(e)2). 5) Examine the matchmarks as follows: a) If the matchmark on the self-locking nut does not reach the mark on the shaft, disassemble the air/oil separator [1] and examine the condition of parts. Then, start the installation procedure again from step 3.F.(1)(c). b) If the matchmark on the self-locking nut is in line or after the mark on the shaft, continue to the step 3.F.(2)(f). (f) Remove the wrench [3] and the torque multiplier [5].

F. Install the Magnetic Seal

SUBTASK 72-60-00-410-001-F00 CAUTION USE CLEAN, LINT-FREE GLOVES WHEN YOU TOUCH THE MAGNETIC SEALS. THIS WILL PREVENT CONTAMINATION. CAUTION REPLACE ALL OF THE SEAL, IF YOU CAUSED DAMAGE TO A COMPONENT OF THE SEAL. MAGNETIC SEALS ARE MATCHED ASSEMBLIES. IF YOU MIX COMPONENTS, OIL LEAKAGE COULD OCCUR. (1) Do these steps to install the magnetic seal [1]: (a) Install the new O-ring [2] and O-ring [3]: 1) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] on the O-rings. 2) Install the new O-ring [2] on the seal housing assembly (OD). 3) Install the new O-ring [3] on the rotating ring (ID). CAUTION MAKE SURE THE POLISHED FACE OF THE SEAL CASE AND THE CARBON FACE OF THE ROTATING RING ARE CLEAN. LEAKS WILL RESULT IF PARTICLES, EVEN OF A VERY SMALL SIZE, ARE BETWEEN THESE PARTS DURING THE INSTALLATION. (b) Apply a layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] to the carbon seal face of the rotating ring and the polished face of the seal case. (c) Carefully install the rotating ring on the seal housing assembly: 1) Make sure the carbon seal touches the polished surface of the seal case. 2) Align the rotating ring with the internal diameter of the seal housing assembly. (d) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] to the bearing surface of the gear shaft that will touch the rotating ring and the O-ring. CAUTION DO NOT HIT THE MAGNETIC SEAL INTO THE GEARBOX RECESS. THE ROTATING RING AND SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY CAN MOVE APART AND THE CARBON SEAL CAN BE DAMAGED. CAUTION INSTALL THE ROTATING RING AND THE SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY TOGETHER ONTO THE GEAR SHAFT, UNTIL THE SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY TOUCHES THE GEARBOX. DO NOT SEPARATELY SLIDE THE ROTATING PART OF THE SEAL ONTO THE SHAFT. IF YOU INSTALL THE ROTATING RING AND SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY SEPARATELY, OIL LEAKAGE COULD OCCUR. (e) Put the magnetic seal on the gear shaft. 1) Make sure the outer O-ring of the seal housing assembly touches the gearbox bearing housing. (f) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the three gearbox studs. (g) Install the nuts and washers on the studs: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Tighten the nuts with your fingers. 2) Make sure the washers touch the seal housing assembly. (h) Tighten the nuts in a sequence until the seal housing assembly moves fully into its position in contact with the gearbox housing. (i) Tighten the nuts to 29.2-32.7 pound-inches (3.3-3.7 Newton meters). (d) Install the rotating ring on the gear shaft with the pusher/puller, SPL-10797, or the pusher/puller, SPL-2191 (Figure 203): 1) Loosen the pusher/puller nut and screw. 2) Put the rotating ring on the tool and against the sleeve. 3) Tighten the pusher/puller screw, then tighten the pusher/puller nut to make sure the rotating ring will not turn in the sleeve. 4) Install the rotating ring on the gear shaft: a) Turn the pusher/puller, with the handle, until the slots in the rotating ring align with the lugs in the bearing. b) Turn the pusher/puller in each direction to make sure the rotating ring slots are engaged with the bearing lugs. 5) Loosen the pusher/puller screw and nut. (e) Put the seal housing assembly on the gear shaft (Figure 204). 1) Make sure the outer O-ring of the seal housing assembly touches the gearbox bearing housing. (f) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], to the three gearbox studs. (g) Install the nuts and washers on the studs: 1) Tighten the nuts with your fingers. 2) Make sure the washers touch the seal housing assembly. (h) Tighten the nuts in a sequence until the seal housing goes fully into its position in contact with the gearbox housing assembly. (i) Torque the nuts to 29.2-32.7 pound-inches (3.3-3.7 Newton meters). (d) Apply a layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442], on the mating surface of the rotating ring. (e) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442], on the bearing surface of the gear shaft: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL ALL; CFM ALL, POST CFM SB 72-0564 AND PRE CFM SB 72-0879 (Continued) 1) Apply the oil on the bearing surfaces of the gear shaft which will touch the O-ring on the rotating ring. Make sure that the position of the rotating ring is correct in the claws of the grip. 6) Tighten the sleeve to lock the rotating ring in the claws. 7) Insert the pusher/puller assembly into the centering guide to install the rotating ring on the gear shaft. 8) Turn the pusher/puller until the lugs of the rotating ring engage into the slots of the ball bearing inner race. 9) Make sure that the rotating ring is correctly installed. a) Make sure that the bottom face of the sleeve window is in line with the AGB forward face. 10) Loosen the sleeve. a) Push the seal pusher/puller to make sure the rotating ring stays in place. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE GRIP CLAWS ARE FULLY DISENGAGED. DO NOT PULL AND DISENGAGE THE ROTATING RING WITH THE SEAL PUSHER/PULLER. (g) Apply a light layer of oil, D00599 [CP2442], to the polished face of the rotating ring. CAUTION DO NOT TAP THE SEALOL SEAL INTO THE GEARBOX RECESS. THE ROTATING RING AND SEAL CASE CAN MOVE APART AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE CARBON SEAL. (h) Prepare the seal housing assembly for installation (Figure 205, Figure 209): 1) Apply RTV 102 adhesive, A01077 [CP2266], to the oil seal assembly at the angle formed by the centering diameter and the mating face, and to the mating ring where there is no mating face. NOTE: This operation does not need any surface preparing, hand blending or primary coating application. a) Smooth the RTV 102 sealant on all the diameter with a 0.118 x 0.118 in (3 x 3 mm) plastic spatula, except in the area where there is no mating face. 2) Install the new O-ring [22] on the seal housing assembly: CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL ALL; CFM ALL, POST CFM SB 72-0564 AND PRE CFM SB 72-0879 (Continued) a) Apply a light layer of vaseline, D00672 [CP5070], to the O-ring. b) Install the O-ring in the groove on the seal housing assembly (OD). (i) Install the seal housing assembly on the gear shaft. 1) Make sure that the outer O-ring of the seal housing assembly touches the gearbox bearing housing. (j) Make sure that the seal housing assembly is correctly engaged with the centering pin on the N2 drive pad. (k) Remove any unwanted RTV 102 adhesive, A01077 [CP2266], around the seal housing assembly with a dry cloth and a spatula (no solvent). 1) Examine the N2 Pad cover side to make sure that the drain cavity is not clogged by residual RTV 102 adhesive, A01077 [CP2266]. (l) Let the RTV 102 sealant cure for 3 hours before starting the engine. (m) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], to the threads of the two attaching bolts. (n) Attach the seal housing assembly with the two bolts on the N2 drive pad. (o) Make sure that the seal is correctly installed with the checking tool of the pusher/puller, SPL-11935. 72-60-00-200-801-F00Accessory Gearbox and Transfer Gearbox Mount InspectionPDF p. 1337

2. Accessory Gearbox and Transfer Gearbox Mount Inspection (Figure 601 and Figure 602) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This is a visual check of the mounts on the transfer gearbox (TGB) housing and the accessory gearbox housing (AGB). (2) The AGB is on the left side of the fan case and the TGB is at the 9:00 o'clock position on the fan frame.

B. References

Reference Title 71-00-02-000-801-F00 Power Plant - Removal (P/B 401) 71-00-02-400-801-F00 Power Plant - Installation (P/B 401) 71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 71-11-02-410-801-F00 Close the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 72-62-00-000-801-F00 Transfer Gearbox Assembly Removal (P/B 401) 72-62-00-400-801-F00 Transfer Gearbox Assembly Installation (P/B 401)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-001-F00 (1) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-002-F00 (2) Do a visual check of the AGB clevis mounts for damage (Figure 601): (a) If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the engine, unless you are given other instructions. These are the tasks: Power Plant - Removal, TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00, Power Plant - Installation, TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00. (b) Cracks 1) Not serviceable. (c) Loose bushing in the clevis mounts CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Not permitted. (d) Loose mount pin 1) Not permitted. a) Tighten the mount pin if it is loose. SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-003-F00 (3) Do a visual check of the TGB mounts for damage (Figure 602): (a) If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the TGB, unless you are given other instructions. These are the tasks: Transfer Gearbox Assembly Removal, TASK 72-62-00-000-801-F00, Transfer Gearbox Assembly Installation, TASK 72-62-00-400-801-F00. (b) Cracks 1) Not serviceable. (c) Loose attachment bolts 1) Not permitted. a) Tighten the attachment nut (TASK 72-62-00-400-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-004-F00 (4) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.

72-60-00-200-802-F00Accessory Gearbox, Transfer Gearbox, and Horizontal Drive Shaft - Oil Leakage InspectionPDF p. 1341

3. Accessory Gearbox, Transfer Gearbox, and Horizontal Drive Shaft - Oil Leakage Inspection

A. General

(1) This is a visual check for oil leaks from the transfer gearbox (TGB) housing, the accessory gearbox housing (AGB) and the horizontal drive shaft housing (HDS). (2) The AGB is on the left side of the fan case and the TGB is at the 9:00 o'clock position on the fan frame. (3) The HDS housing is between the AGB and the TGB.

B. References

Reference Title 71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201) 71-11-02-410-801-F00 Close the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 72-60-00-010-009-F00 (1) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-005-F00 (2) Do a visual check of the AGB for oil leakage. SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-006-F00 (3) Do a visual check of the TGB for oil leakage. SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-007-F00 (4) Do a visual check of the HDS housing for oil leakage. SUBTASK 72-60-00-900-001-F00 (5) If you find evidence of oil leakage, repair or replace components as it is necessary to stop the leakage. SUBTASK 72-60-00-410-006-F00 (6) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.

H. Replacement of the 32-tooth bevel gear oil nozzle O-rings

SUBTASK 72-62-00-960-001-F00 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER. WARNING ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY. (1) Do these steps to replace the 32-tooth bevel gear oil nozzle o-ring [1] and o-ring [2] (Figure 201, Figure 202). (a) Remove the bolt [3] which attaches the oil nozzle plug [4] to the transfer gearbox (TGB) housing. (b) Remove the plug [4] with the inner adapter P30 [5] of the puller adapters, SPL-6180 and impact puller [6]. (c) Remove the inner adapter P30 [5] of the puller adapter, SPL-6180. (d) Remove and discard the o-ring [7]. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (e) Remove the oil nozzle [8] with the inner adapter P32 [9] of the puller adapter, SPL-6180, and an impact puller [6]. (f) Remove the inner adapter P32 [9] of the puller adapter, SPL-6180. (g) Remove and discard o-ring [1] and o-ring [2]. WARNING MAKE SURE TO PREVENT ACETONE CONTACT WITH SKIN. ACETONE IRRITATES SKIN AND IS EXPLOSIVE. USE FUME CONTROL OR USE A RESPIRATOR TO PREVENT INJURY. (h) Clean the oil nozzle [8] with acetone solvent, B01058 [CP1039]. WARNING ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY. (i) Apply a layer of engine oil, D00599 [CP2442] on the new o-ring [1] and o-ring [2]. (j) Use the seal fittings tool set, SPL-9874 to install the new o-ring [1] on the oil nozzle [8] then manually install the new o-ring [2]. WARNING ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY. (k) Install the new o-ring [7] with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442] on the plug [4]. WARNING ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY. (l) Install the plug [4] with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442] into the oil nozzle [8]. (m) Attach the oil nozzle [8] to the TGB housing with the bolt [3]. 1) Torque the bolt [3] to 95 in-lb (11 N·m) - 105 in-lb (12 N·m).

(b) Remove the V-clamp [2] at the interface between the AGB [1] and the TGB [11]. (c) Lubricate the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (d) Put a container below the TGB and AGB interface. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE IS STOPPED. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU. WARNING DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN. CAUTION DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER. CAUTION DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUID GET IN THE ENGINE OIL. VERY SMALL QUANTITIES OF THIS FLUID CAN CHEMICALLY CHANGE THE OIL. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. (e) Move the TGB sleeve [4] rearward on the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] to get access to the locking nut [25] on the horizontal drive shaft (Figure 402). CAUTION THE HORIZONTAL DRIVE SHAFT LOCKING-NUT HAS LEFT-HAND THREADS. DO NOT APPLY A COUNTERCLOCKWISE TORQUE TO THE NUT. IF YOU DO, DAMAGE TO THE SHAFT CAN OCCUR. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (g) Disengage the horizontal drive shaft [26] from the AGB [1] and fully retract it in the TGB [11]. BECAUSE THE TGB WEIGHS APPROXIMATELY 44 POUNDS (20 KG), INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Remove the two nuts [19], washers [18] and the bolts [17] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame. (b) While you hold the TGB [11], remove the two nuts [10], washers [9], and the bolts [8] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame. (c) As you keep the TGB [11] in a horizontal position, remove it from the engine. (d) Remove and discard the O-ring [27]. (e) Remove and discard the O-ring [31]. SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-001-F00 WARNING DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN. CAUTION DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUID GET IN THE ENGINE OIL. VERY SMALL QUANTITIES OF THIS FLUID CAN CHEMICALLY CHANGE THE OIL. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. (1) Do these steps to prepare the TGB for the installation: (a) Lubricate a new O-ring [27] with oil, D00599 [CP2442] and install it in the sleeve groove (Figure 402). (b) Lubricate a new O-ring [31] with oil, D00599 [CP2442] and install it in the groove of the adaptor [32] (Figure 401). (c) Lubricate the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (d) Fully retract the TGB sleeve [4] on the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] and the horizontal drive shaft [26] in the TGB [11]. (e) Lubricate the radial drive shaft splines with oil, D00599 [CP2442] (Figure 401). (f) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [8] and the bolts [17] that attach the TGB [11] to the engine with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (g) Make sure that the ring on the TGB [11] is serviceable (View A-A). (h) Make sure that the gasket [16] of the oil return tube is serviceable. SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-009-F00 (2) Install the outer radial drive shaft into the fan frame strut. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-002-F00 (3) Do these steps to install the TGB [11] (Figure 401): CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU ENGAGE THE OUTER RADIAL DRIVE SHAFT WITH THE INPUT BEVEL GEAR OF THE TGB. IF YOU ARE NOT CAREFUL, DAMAGE TO THE SEALS AND SPLINES COULD OCCUR. (a) Engage horizontally the outer radial drive shaft splines in the input bevel gear of the TGB [11]; put the TGB [11] in its position on the fan frame. (b) While you hold the TGB [11] in its position, install the top two bolts [8], washers [9], and the nuts [10] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame. 1) Tighten the nuts [10] but do not apply the final torque. (c) Install the bottom bolts [17], washers [18], and the nuts [19] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame. 1) Tighten the nuts [19] but do not apply the final torque. SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-003-F00 (4) Engage the horizontal drive shaft [26] as follows (Figure 402): (a) Lubricate the splines on the horizontal drive shaft with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (b) Move the horizontal drive shaft [26] forward and carefully engage it in the AGB input gear. 1) If the splines do not align, handcrank the AGB to match and engage the horizontal drive shaft splines with the AGB gear splines. a) Remove the locking cover of the locking adapter to turn the AGB geartrain. (c) Lubricate the threads of the AGB [1] input gear with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (d) Install the locking nut [25] on the AGB input gear. NOTE: The locking nut has left-hand threads. 1) Tighten the locking nut [25] with your hand. (e) If you removed the locking cover from the locking adapter, re-install the locking cover before you do the subsequent step. (f) Torque the nuts [10] and nuts [19] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame to 176 in-lb (19.9 N·m) - 195 in-lb (22.0 N·m). (g) Torque the locking nut [25] of the horizontal drive shaft [26] to 1330 in-lb (150.3 N·m) - 1590 in-lb (179.6 N·m). 1) Use the wrench, SPL-2192. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE RETAINING RING IS IN ITS CORRECT POSITION. IF THE RETAINING RING IS NOT IN ITS CORRECT POSITION, THE HORIZONTAL DRIVE SHAFT COULD DISENGAGE AND CAUSE AN ENGINE FLAME OUT. 72-62-00-200-802-F00Transfer Gearbox Internal InspectionPDF p. 1383

3. Transfer Gearbox Internal Inspection

A. General

(1) This inspection use a borescope to examine the internal surfaces of the Transfer Gearbox (TGB). (2) If you find the metal bearing particles in the magnetic chips detectors, do the internal inspection. The borescope equipment will permit you to see if the rollers bearing for the input or output bevel gear is damaged.

CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) The inspection (that follows) looks for damage to the input bevel gear roller bearing. (b) If the MCD inspection was done for a scheduled maintenance program, this is the continue-in-service limit before the TGB replacement. 1) A continue-in-service limit of 2 cycles is permitted if there were no pilot reports of vibration or abnormal noise. SUBTASK 72-62-00-290-001-F00 (4) If you find the metal bearing particles, do a borescope inspection of the roller bearing for the input bevel gear as follows. SUBTASK 72-62-00-020-007-F00 (5) Remove the five bolts that attach the N2 drive pad cover to the AGB. (a) Remove the N2 drive pad cover. 1) Discard the o-rings. SUBTASK 72-62-00-200-001-F00 (6) Examine the roller bearing for the input bevel gear as follows. (a) Connect a light source, SPL-2197 to a 110 Volt AC 60 Hz ground power source and connect the ground. (b) Connect the 0.24 inch (6.0 mm) flexible borescope to the borescope, COM-2196 and to the port on the light source, SPL-2197. (c) Turn on the light source, SPL-2197. 1) Install the borescope, COM-2196 through the vent nipple port of the TGB. (d) Manually turn the TGB. 1) Examine the roller bearing for the input bevel gear for the damage. (e) If the roller bearing is damaged. 1) Do this task: Transfer Gearbox Assembly Installation, TASK 72-62-00-400-801-F00. a) Replace the roller bearing. 2) See the continue-in-service limit above for the detail. (f) If the roller bearing is not damage. 1) Do this task: Power Plant - Installation, TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00. a) Replace the engine. (f) If the roller bearing is not damage. 1) Do this task: Power Plant - Installation, TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00. a) Replace the engine. F. Procedure

SUBTASK 72-63-00-420-005-F00 (1) Do these steps to install the dampers [12] on the end of the AGB upper mount link [1]. (a) Install one damper [12] on each extremity of the AGB upper mount link [1]. (b) Install the AGB upper mount link [1] on the AGB upper clevis mount and the fan case clevis. (c) Lubricate the threads of the two straight pin assemblies [5] that attach the AGB upper mount link [1] with the AGB upper clevis mount and the fan case clevis to the engine with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (d) Install the two straight pin assemblies [5] that attach the AGB upper mount link [1] with the AGB upper clevis mount and the fan case clevis. (e) Install the two washers [3] and the two nuts [2] that attach the straight pin assemblies [5] with the AGB upper mount link [1]. CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO INSTALL THE STRAIGHT PINS. HOLD THE STRAIGHT PIN WITH ONE, AND TIGHTEN THE NUT WITH THE OTHER WRENCH. DO NOT TURN THE STRAIGHT PINS. IF YOU TURN THE STRAIGHT PINS, YOU WILL CAUSE DAMAGE. (f) Tighten the two nuts [2] to 840 in-lb (95 N·m)-930 in-lb (105 N·m). (g) Install the two cotter pins [4] on the straight pin assemblies [5]. (h) Install the main oil/fuel heat exchanger with the servo fuel heater together (TASK 79-21-02-400-801-F00). (i) Reconnect the lines from the servo fuel heater (TASK 73-11-07-400-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-63-00-420-006-F00 (2) Do these steps to install the dampers [10] on the end of the AGB lower mount link [11]. (a) Install one damper [10] on each extremity of the AGB lower mount link [11]. (b) Install the AGB lower mount link [11] on the AGB lower clevis mount and the fan case clevis. (c) Lubricate the threads of the two straight pin assemblies [9] that attach the AGB lower mount link [11] with the AGB lower clevis mount and the fan case clevis to the engine with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (d) Install the two straight pin assemblies [9] that attach the AGB lower mount link [11] with the AGB lower clevis mount and the fan case clevis. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL (e) Install the two washers [7] and the nuts [6] that attach the straight pin assemblies [9] with the AGB lower mount link [11]. CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO INSTALL THE STRAIGHT PINS. HOLD THE STRAIGHT PIN WITH ONE, AND TIGHTEN THE NUT WITH THE OTHER WRENCH. DO NOT TURN THE STRAIGHT PINS. IF YOU TURN THE STRAIGHT PINS, YOU WILL CAUSE DAMAGE. (f) Tighten the nuts [6] to 840 in-lb (95 N·m)-930 in-lb (105 N·m). (g) Install the two new cotter pins [8] on the straight pin assemblies [9]. (h) Reconnect the fuel-in tube to the IDG oil cooler (TASK 73-11-06-400-801-F00). (i) Do this task: Lubrication Unit Installation, TASK 79-21-01-400-801-F00. SUBTASK 72-63-00-420-007-F00 CAUTION DO NOT FULLY REMOVE THE AGB TURNBUCKLE FROM THE ENGINE. INSTALL THE FIRST END AGAIN BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE OTHER END FROM THE ENGINE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION, YOU WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. CAUTION DO NOT CHANGE THE AGB TURNBUCKLE LENGTH DURING THE PROCEDURE, THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE CORRECT ALIGNMENT OF THE AGB MODULE. (3) Do these steps to install the damper [14] on the end of the AGB turnbuckle [16]. (a) Install one damper [14] on the left link [15] and on the right link [19]. (b) Install the left link [15] of the AGB turnbuckle [16] on the AGB clevis and the right link [19] of the AGB turnbuckle [16] on the fan frame clevis. (c) Lubricate the threads of the two straight pin assemblies [13] that attach the left link [15] and right link [19] of the AGB turnbuckle [16] with the AGB clevis and the fan frame clevis to the engine with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (d) Install the straight pin assemblies [13] that attach the left link [15] and right link [19] with the AGB clevis and the fan frame clevis. (e) Install the two washers [18] and the nuts [17] that attach the straight pin assemblies [13] with the left link [15] and the right link [19]. CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO INSTALL THE STRAIGHT PINS. HOLD THE STRAIGHT PIN WITH ONE, AND TIGHTEN THE NUT WITH THE OTHER WRENCH. DO NOT TURN THE STRAIGHT PINS. IF YOU TURN THE STRAIGHT PINS, YOU WILL CAUSE DAMAGE. (f) Tighten the nuts [17] to 840 in-lb (95 N·m)-930 in-lb (105 N·m). (g) Install the two new cotter pins [20] on the straight pin assemblies [13]straight pin assemblies [13].
