(a) These are the tasks: Accessory Gearbox Removal, TASK 72-63-00-000-804-F00, Accessory Gearbox Installation, TASK 72-63-00-400-804-F00. SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-006-F00 (3) Visually examine the mount fittings on the fan frame (Figure 601, Sheet 3): (a) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes in the mount lugs CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Not serviceable. 2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that goes through one mounting lug bolt hole, not more than 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) in length. (b) Cracks in the areas of the mount lugs 1) Not serviceable. 2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in length. (c) Nicks, marks, and scratches 1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, marks, and scratches which are permitted with these conditions: a) Not more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) in length. b) Not more than 0.02 in. (0.51 mm) in depth, after you remove the high metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). c) Minimum separation of 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) between areas of damage. SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-002-F00 (4) Examine the AGB housing for damage: NOTE: If you find AGB displacement while working on any of the AGB mounted equipment, it is recommended to do an inspection of the AGB mounts and rod links within the next 200 hours or 100 cycles. (a) If you find AGB displacement when you do work on the AGB mount equipment, do this step: 1) It is recommended to do an inspection of the AGB mounts and rod links in the subsequent 200 hours or 100 cycles. (b) Cracks 1) Not serviceable. (c) Nicks, dents, or scratches 1) All damage is permitted with this limit: a) Not more than 0.035 in. (0.89 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00). SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-003-F00 (5) Examine the AGB clevis mounts for damage: (a) Cracks 1) Not serviceable. (b) Loose bushing in the clevis mounts 1) Not permitted. (c) Loose mount pin 1) Not permitted. a) Tighten the mount pin if it is necessary. (d) Cracks or crazing in the AGB mount rubber are permitted. (e) Eccentricity of the mounting pin axis relative to the axis of the outer bushing of the rubber damper CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Maximum Serviceable Limit: Maximum allowed eccentricity (half of the difference between the minimum and maximum clearances) is 0.06 in. (1.5 mm) (Figure 601, Sheet 4). 2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted to replace the dampers (Replacement of a Damper in the Mount Fitting, TASK 72-63-00-300-801-F00), if there is no contact of metal against metal. SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-005-F00 (6) Examine the AGB upper and lower mount links, turnbuckle, and associated clevis for damage (Figure 602): (a) Axial and/or radial looseness of mount link or turnbuckle 1) Any amount is permitted if there is no contact between the mount links or turnbuckle extremity and associated clevis. CAUTION THE MOUNT LINKS OR TURNBUCKLES SURFACES MUST BE PARALLEL AS FAR AS POSSIBLE TO THE CLEVIS SURFACES DURING THE CLEARANCE CHECK. DO NOT ROTATE THE ROD LINK OR TURNBUCKLE. THE CLEARANCE CHECK MUST BE DONE AT THE EXTREMITY OF THE LINKS. AN INCORRECT CHECK CAN LEAD TO EQUIPMENT DAMAGE. 2) If a mount link or turnbuckle extremity is in contact with the AGB or engine clevis, a maximum In-Service extension of 500 operating cycles is permitted before you do the installation of a damper. NOTE: On engine POST CFM56-7B-SB 72-0465, you already have a damper at each link end. a) Do these tasks for each link to replace the dampers: <1> Axial Link End Dampers Removal, TASK 72-63-00-000-802-F00. <2> Axial Link End Dampers Installation, TASK 72-63-00-400-802-F00. b) For the AGB and engine clevis of the mount links: <1> Impacts, marks, wear or fretting <a> Any amount permitted if less than 0.008 in. (0.2 mm) in depth. c) For the AGB upper and lower mount links, turnbuckle (if removed during damper installation) (Figure 602, Sheet 2): <1> Spherical bearing axial wear <a> Dim. X = 0.1799 in. (4.57 mm) “max”. <2> Spherical bearing radial wear <a> Any amount. <3> Ball groove and corrosion <a> Any amount. <4> External ring with missing lubricating lining <a> Any amount. <5> External ring tears <a> Not serviceable. <6> If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the axial link end(s) or the mount link. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL <a> These are the tasks: Axial Link End or Upper (Lower) Mount Link Removal, TASK 72-63-00-000-803-F00 Axial Link End or Upper (Lower) Mount Link Installation, TASK 72-63-00-400-803-F00. NOTE: This task includes an adjustment of the AGB position. (a) Tears, cut 1) Any amount is permitted. (b) Missing dampers straps 1) Any amount is permitted. SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-004-F00 (8) Look for damage to the lockwire: (a) Broken, missing or loose lockwire 1) Not permitted. a) Do this task: Lockwire Installation, TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00. Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

F. Procedure

ALL; FOR ALL NON 7BE PRE CFM SB 72-0564 OR PRE SB 72-0879 SUBTASK 72-63-01-420-001-F00 CAUTION INSTALL THE COVER ON THE AGB. WITHOUT THE COVER, OIL LEAKS WILL OCCUR. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. CAUTION INSTALL NEW O-RINGS ON THE COVER OF THE AGB. USED O-RINGS CAN CAUSE OIL LEAKS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. (1) Do these steps to attach the handcranking drive cover [3] to the handcranking drive pad of the AGB: NOTE: Installation of the AGB hand-cranking cover must be classified as “flight safety sensitive maintenance”. An independent inspection of the correct installation of the hand-cranking cover must be carried out prior to release to service of the aircraft or the engine, as applicable. CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7) EFFECTIVITY ALL ALL; FOR ALL NON 7BE PRE CFM SB 72-0564 OR PRE SB 72-0879 (Continued) (a) Lubricate two new o-rings [4] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (b) Put the two new o-rings [4] on the handcranking drive cover [3]. (c) Install the handcranking drive cover [3] on the handcranking drive pad of the AGB. (d) Lightly lubricate the threads of the bolt [1] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (e) Install the four bolts [1] and four washers [2]. 1) Tighten the bolts to 97-106 pound-inches (11-12 Newton meters). ALL; FOR ALL NON 7BE POST CFM SB 72-0564 OR POST SB 72-0879 OR CFM56-7BE SUBTASK 72-63-01-420-002-F00 CAUTION INSTALL THE COVER ON THE AGB. WITHOUT THE COVER, OIL LEAKS WILL OCCUR. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. CAUTION INSTALL NEW O-RINGS ON THE COVER OF THE AGB. USED O-RINGS CAN CAUSE OIL LEAKS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. (2) Do these steps to attach the handcranking drive cover [3] to the handcranking drive pad of the AGB: (a) Lubricate the new o-ring [4] with oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (b) Put the new o-ring [4] on the handcranking drive cover [3]. (c) Install the handcranking drive cover [3] on the handcranking drive pad of the AGB. (d) Lightly lubricate the threads of the bolts [1] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101]. (e) Install the three bolts [1] and three washers [2]. 1) Tighten the bolts [1] to 97-106 pound-inches (11-12 Newton meters). ALL

G. Handcranking Driver Cover Installation Test

SUBTASK 72-63-01-790-001-F00 (1) Do the test that is listed in the Power Plant Test Reference Table (TASK 71-00-00-800-811-F00).

H. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 72-63-01-410-001-F00 (1) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.
